chapters.title: Chapter 351: The Dragon Princess Has a Demigod Grandmother?!
paragraphs: The instant those words left Rhaenyra’s mouth, Luke’s clone froze behind the building, because until this moment, he had genuinely believed that Shadow of Nyx was practically flawless when it came to hiding the difference between the original body and the doppelganger.

After all, Shadow of Nyx didn’t create an ordinary illusion or some hollow copy, but brought forth another real version of Luke recorded within the Void, which was precisely why even those who interacted with the clone directly usually couldn’t distinguish it from the original.
However, as that thought crossed his mind, Luke suddenly remembered one important detail that he kept overlooking whenever he became too confident in his Titan abilities.
‘I’m not Nyx.’

Nyx had taken this racial ability and refined it through experience until its usage reached an extreme level, while Luke was still a newly awakened Titan who had inherited the completed ability through the System without possessing the countless years of mastery behind it.
Almost as if the System had been waiting for him to realize that himself, its voice appeared beside him.

[That’s why I’ve told you before that there are always methods capable of breaking or seeing through your Titan abilities, so you actually need to practice them instead of assuming the inherited version will solve everything for you.]
Luke’s clone remained silent while the System continued.

[It’s good that you keep developing new attack techniques, but sometimes you forget that your Titans possess abilities beyond direct destruction, and many of those abilities have far more uses than simply hitting something harder.]
There really wasn’t anything Luke’s clone could say against that, and even if the original body had been standing here instead, he probably wouldn’t have found a convincing argument either.

Luke had always been obsessed with obtaining greater destructive power, especially techniques capable of defeating opponents above his realm, but that obsession had also caused him to neglect several abilities whose value couldn’t be measured purely by how much damage they caused.
Meanwhile, high above Blackstone, Aurielle stared at Rhaenyra with obvious disbelief before slowly turning her gaze toward the building where Luke’s clone was hiding.
“This isn’t Luke?” Her expression became visibly baffled as the realization settled in. “I’ve been spending all this time with Luke’s clone?”
Rhaenyra released a quiet sigh after seeing her reaction.
‘So she really didn’t know.’
That only created another question in Rhaenyra’s mind, because if the person Aurielle had been living with was merely a clone, then where had the real Luke disappeared to?
Even her Golden Chain pointed toward the Luke hiding below, making the situation more confusing, yet Aurielle reached her own conclusion much faster.
‘He went to that pink-haired bitch.’
Selene’s face immediately appeared in her mind, along with the invitation she had previously gotten, inviting Luke to accompany her if he could.
Aurielle’s expression gradually became colder.
‘My husband has been spending time with another woman while leaving a clone here with me...’
Just thinking about it made anger surge through her chest, and when her gaze returned to Rhaenyra, another thought followed immediately.
‘And now another bitch has come here to take him away.’
Unfortunately for Rhaenyra, she was the only one currently standing in front of Aurielle, which made deciding where to direct that anger extremely simple.
“Attack!”

Aurielle’s command echoed through the air without warning, startling even Rhaenyra for a brief moment, although before the Dragon Princess could properly react, a quiet voice reached her from the side.
“Dream Prison.”
Purple dream energy flickered around Theia as she activated her S-Rank Origin Skill and directed the mental prison straight toward Rhaenyra.
However, the result was completely different from what she expected.
Nothing happened.
There wasn’t even a moment where Rhaenyra’s consciousness appeared to waver, and Theia’s expression immediately changed as she realized that Dream Prison had failed to properly take hold.
At the same time, Rhaenyra finally turned her golden gaze toward her.
“Hmm?”
She looked over Theia for a moment before her attention moved across the other women standing around Aurielle.
“Now that I’m actually looking properly, Luke has gathered quite a lot of women around his him.”
She seemed considerably more interested in that discovery than in the mental attack Theia had just attempted against her.

The reaction left the others baffled, because Theia’s Dream Prison was an S-Rank Origin ability wielded by a genuine B-Rank Arcane Core Mage, and against opponents within her own general level, the technique was powerful enough that even those with strong wills normally had to actively resist or escape from it.
Rhaenyra, however, hadn’t resisted.
The ability simply hadn’t caught her at all.
Theia’s face slowly lost its color as the most obvious conclusion appeared in her mind.
“She’s A-Rank.”
Silence immediately spread among the people closest to her.
Even Aurielle’s anger faltered for a moment as horror appeared across her face, because there wasn’t a single person currently inside Blackstone capable of confronting an A-Rank existence.
Rhaenyra noticed their reactions, although she showed little interest in explaining herself, because the reason behind her new strength had occurred only several days earlier.
A few days ago, within the Dragon Continent, Rhaenyra stood among the scorched remains of another monster that had attempted to enter the territory entrusted to her by her father.
Scarlet flames still burned across portions of the ground while smoke drifted through the air, yet Rhaenyra barely paid attention to the corpse as she brushed some dust from her clothes.
“Sigh, that old geezer is really killing me with boredom.”

Her father had given her this territory and ordered her to protect it for an entire year, which Rhaenyra considered incredibly tedious, especially when most of the creatures foolish enough to invade couldn’t even entertain her for long.
At least something worthwhile had happened during that time.
Only a few days earlier, she had finally broken through the boundary that had held her back and stepped into A-Rank, officially becoming an Ancient Dragon.
Rhaenyra had barely finished thinking about that achievement when a pair of arms suddenly wrapped around her from behind.
“Ohh, my little dragon! I missed you so much!”
Rhaenyra’s body stiffened for an instant before recognition immediately replaced her surprise.
“Grandma?!”

She quickly turned her head, because the last thing she remembered hearing was that her grandmother had entered seclusion while searching for some kind of cosmic answer, which meant Rhaenyra hadn’t expected to see her here of all places.
Zephyrielle Arkanthyr merely continued holding her granddaughter with obvious affection.

Seeing her again, Rhaenyra couldn’t help releasing a small sigh, because nobody looking at the woman in front of her would ever believe that she had already lived for thousands of years, much less that she was a genuine demi-god.

Zephyrielle’s long hair flowed behind her in shimmering strands of white mixed with sapphire, giving the impression that moonlight and blue crystal had been woven together, while two elegant dragon horns rose from above her head and immediately displayed the ancient blood flowing through her veins.

Her beauty had barely been touched by age, and even after meeting princesses, queens, and powerful women from different races, Rhaenyra still hadn’t encountered anyone she considered more beautiful than her grandmother.
Normally, seeing Zephyrielle would have made her happy, because among her entire family, her grandmother had always been one of the people who supported and spoiled her the most.
Unfortunately, Rhaenyra knew exactly what was about to happen.

chapters.title: Chapter 352: Zephyrielle Demands to See Her Grandson-in-Law!
paragraphs: "You little dragon..." Zephyrielle finally released her slightly before looking at her with clear dissatisfaction. "You got married quietly and didn’t even tell me a single word?"
’Here it comes.’
Rhaenyra already felt a headache beginning.

Zephyrielle’s annoyance only increased as she continued, "I told my son not to marry that bitch Draevyra, but did he listen to me? Of course not, and now look what happened. She took my granddaughter and arranged her marriage without even bothering to tell me."
The "bitch" she was referring to so casually was none other than Rhaenyra’s own mother.

For reasons Rhaenyra had never fully cared enough to investigate, her grandmother and mother had never liked each other very much, although strangely enough, Zephyrielle still adored both Rhaenyra and her younger sister.
Rhaenyra had long since accepted that trying to understand the relationship between the older women in her family would only cause unnecessary headaches.
Unfortunately, what came next was exactly what she had been hoping to avoid.
"So..." Zephyrielle’s irritation disappeared almost instantly, replaced by a cheerful smile as she looked around the territory. "Where is my grandson-in-law?"
Rhaenyra fell silent.
Her grandmother spoke as though she knew absolutely nothing about what had happened during the Hero Summoning, but Rhaenyra wasn’t foolish enough to believe that act for even a second.
Zephyrielle might have emerged from seclusion only recently, yet if a demi-god of her level genuinely wanted information, Rhaenyra suspected that even the stars themselves would answer her questions.
Then the smile on Zephyrielle’s face changed slightly.
"Don’t tell me, darling, that you left your husband behind with another woman?"
Her voice remained gentle, yet a colder edge quietly entered it.

Dragons were naturally possessive creatures, and their pride was even worse, so the idea that her granddaughter had simply left her own husband in the hands of some lower-level human woman was enough to irritate Zephyrielle.
It didn’t matter to her that Luke himself was a weak human Hero.
He belonged to her granddaughter.
That alone was enough.
"So tell me, darling, when am I going to meet my grandson-in-law?" Zephyrielle asked with the same pleasant smile before tilting her head slightly. "Or should I simply go and meet him myself?"
Rhaenyra immediately shook her head.
There was absolutely no chance she was allowing that.
If Zephyrielle personally went looking for Luke while feeling this curious about him, Rhaenyra wasn’t confident that her so-called husband would return in one piece.

Even though she didn’t have any romantic feelings for Luke and still considered him far too weak to properly stand beside her as a husband, the thought of that cutie being reduced to half a corpse because of her grandmother wasn’t something she wanted either.
"I’ll bring him, Grandma..." Rhaenyra finally muttered with obvious reluctance.
To her, Luke was still more like an amusing toy she had been given than someone she genuinely accepted as her husband, but Zephyrielle had made one thing very clear.
Even a weak toy, once it belonged to a dragon, should remain within that dragon’s possession.
"Good, and don’t disappoint me the way your father did."
Zephyrielle smiled as she gently patted Rhaenyra’s head, although the meaning behind those words was obvious enough—she expected her granddaughter to bring Luke to her as soon as possible.
"Hmm..." Rhaenyra reluctantly nodded, and only after receiving that answer did Zephyrielle finally seem satisfied.
Without another word, her figure disappeared from where she stood.

Rhaenyra immediately released the breath she had been holding, because although she had always been comfortable around her grandmother and genuinely enjoyed spending time with her, everyone in the family understood one simple rule regarding Zephyrielle Arkanthyr.
When she was happy, she could be the most affectionate person imaginable, but once her mood turned bad, everyone around her suffered along with it.
Rhaenyra was still recovering from that encounter when another calm voice came from behind her.
"Do you need me to come with you?"

Rhaenyra turned slightly and found Emberlyn Starfall standing nearby, her youngest sister having apparently followed their grandmother here because she had been worried about what might happen once Zephyrielle learned about Rhaenyra’s marriage.
Seeing that her elder sister had survived the conversation without their grandmother becoming genuinely angry had already allowed Emberlyn to relax considerably.
"No need."
Rhaenyra rejected the offer without hesitation before stepping away, and with a dismissive snort, her humanoid form began expanding.

Crimson scales rapidly spread across her growing body as powerful limbs replaced her human figure, while two gigantic wings unfolded behind her until, within moments, a thousand-meter-long crimson dragon stood where the woman had been.
WHOOOOOM!

With one powerful flap of her wings, violent currents swept across the surrounding land as Rhaenyra launched herself into the sky, quickly gaining altitude before turning toward the teleportation platform that would take her toward the Human Continent.
Emberlyn remained where she was and watched the crimson figure shrink against the distant sky.
"Sigh, I was only trying to help."
Despite her elder sister’s refusal, Emberlyn couldn’t stop a trace of curiosity from appearing on her face when she thought about the Human Hero whom Rhaenyra had been ordered to bring back.

She had never personally met Luke, yet somehow this one human had ended up marrying five princesses belonging to imperial royal families of five different races, something that had never happened anywhere in the recorded history of Valtharion.
Naturally, Emberlyn couldn’t help wondering what kind of person he actually was.
Back in Blackstone, Rhaenyra’s thoughts about her grandmother were abruptly interrupted when another quiet voice reached her ears.
"Ultimate Ability — Dream Convergence."
Rhaenyra’s attention immediately shifted toward Theia, but before she could react further, the entire world surrounding her changed.
Blackstone disappeared.

Aurielle vanished from her sight along with the soldiers, buildings, streets, and everyone else who had been present only an instant earlier, leaving Rhaenyra suspended within an unfamiliar dreamscape created by Theia’s S-Rank Origin Skill.
Rhaenyra calmly looked around before a faint trace of disdain crossed her draconic features.
"Heh, futile tricks."

Dream Convergence might have been capable of trapping powerful opponents, and Theia had previously forced even A-Rank beings into her dream world for a short period, but Rhaenyra possessed something particularly troublesome for an illusion-based ability.
Her Dragon Eyes.

Golden light gathered faintly within her pupils as her vision penetrated through the false world surrounding her, allowing her to see the structure beneath the manifested dream rather than becoming lost inside it.
"Break."
The single command left her mouth calmly.
CRAAAAACK!
Fractures immediately spread across the dreamscape like cracks running through glass, and before Theia could reinforce the technique, the entire artificial world shattered apart.
Rhaenyra’s vision returned to Blackstone.

At the same moment, Theia staggered backward several steps before blood escaped from her mouth, the violent destruction of Dream Convergence sending the backlash straight through her mind and Origin connection.
"Cough!"
She caught herself before falling, one hand pressing against the ground as she tried to stabilize her breathing.

Rhaenyra barely spared her another glance, because Aurielle was already rushing toward her from the front with golden-white energy gathering around her body, while nearby, Elena’s enormous white angelic wings spread open as she prepared to join the attack.
Rhaenyra sighed.
"All of you are far too weak, yet it seems none of you understand that."
The moment those words left her mouth, the daylight above Blackstone suddenly disappeared beneath an expanding crimson shadow.

chapters.title: Chapter 353: Luke vs. Rhaenyra Finally Begins!
paragraphs: People throughout the territory instinctively raised their heads, and the sight waiting above them caused whatever courage remained in many of their hearts to vanish.
A thousand-meter-long crimson dragon now filled the sky.
"Dragon..."
That single word escaped several mouths almost simultaneously, but before anyone could recover from the sight of Rhaenyra’s true form, her gigantic jaws opened.
Then came the roar that had made the Dragon Race legendary throughout Valtharion.
GRRRRROOOOOOOOOAAAAARRRRRR!!!
The sound struck Blackstone like a physical wave.
Windows broke apart as their frames became empty, then even rooftops shook, while the air itself seemed to vibrate beneath the draconic roar sweeping through the territory.
For most people, there wasn’t even enough time to understand what had happened.
Their consciousness simply disappeared.
Mortals collapsed immediately, followed by cultivators throughout the lower realms, while even those who had reached C-Rank failed to remain conscious beneath the roar of an Ancient Dragon.
Within moments, almost the entire territory had gone silent.
Only a handful of people remained capable of resisting at all.

Inside one of the distant buildings, even the B-Rank elder connected to Jerreck struggled to move beneath the direct pressure of Rhaenyra’s draconic presence, leaving him unable to interfere despite understanding that something dangerous was happening outside.
Above the territory, Aurielle remained floating in front of Rhaenyra.
Her condition, however, was anything but stable.

Her hair had turned a brilliant shade of purple while one of her eyes radiated light and the other contained absolute darkness, yet the power gathering around her clearly exceeded what her current body could safely contain.

Twilight energy continuously surged through her, but rather than becoming stronger with every passing moment, Aurielle’s body trembled beneath the strain of wielding something it wasn’t yet prepared to control.
Below them, Theia was still conscious as well, although barely.

The backlash from Dream Convergence had already injured her, and now she was forced to endure the Dragon Roar directly while kneeling against the cracked ground, blood continuing to stain the corner of her lips.
Rhaenyra swept her gaze across the silent territory with little concern before looking toward the place where Luke’s clone had been standing earlier.
Then she paused.
Her gigantic golden eyes shifted slightly.
"Where is he?"
Luke had been there only moments earlier, and Rhaenyra was certain he hadn’t physically moved, because his presence had remained within the range of her draconic senses the entire time.
Yet now there was nothing.
Before she could investigate further, a faint voice reached her from the air ahead.
"Luke is mine...
Rhaenyra turned back toward Aurielle.
The Human Princess appeared almost absentminded as unstable Twilight energy continued flowing around her body, yet her gaze remained fixed entirely upon the dragon before her.
"Luke is mine... mine alone, and none of you have any right to him."
Rhaenyra’s patience finally began to disappear.

She still didn’t understand what kind of magic Luke had somehow worked upon Aurielle to make her behave like this, but up until now, Rhaenyra had deliberately restrained herself because she had no intention of killing or seriously injuring the people belonging to her so-called husband.
Aurielle, however, seemed determined to interpret that restraint as weakness.
"Aurielle, it seems you’ve forgotten something very simple."
Rhaenyra’s voice remained indifferent as her immense body shifted through the air.
"The weak should remain quiet when standing before the strong."
Her crimson tail moved.

There was no need for her to use anything close to her full strength, so Rhaenyra deliberately controlled the strike, intending only to hit Aurielle hard enough to leave her half-dead rather than killing her outright.
The gigantic tail swept through the air toward Aurielle.
Below them, Theia immediately understood how dangerous the attack was.
Her emerald eyes widened.
If Aurielle was struck and something happened to her, then Theia knew better than almost anyone what Luke’s reaction would be.
"No!"
She forced herself upward despite the blood running from her lips.
"Don’t do this!"
Rhaenyra didn’t stop.

Her tail continued along the same path without increasing or decreasing its speed, while the unconscious soldiers, mages, guild members, and citizens scattered throughout Blackstone could do nothing to interfere.
Theia could only watch as the crimson tail closed the remaining distance toward Aurielle, whose unstable mind still seemed trapped between rage and the Twilight power surging through her body.
Then, just before the attack connected—
BOOOOOOM!
A seventy-foot-tall Titan clad in sleek black armor materialized directly between them.
Luke raised his right hand.
The thousand-meter dragon’s tail slammed straight into his open palm.
BOOOOOM!

A violent shockwave burst outward from the collision, blasting the surrounding air away and sending ripples across the sky above Blackstone, yet Luke’s gigantic body didn’t shift backward even slightly.
His fingers closed around Rhaenyra’s tail.
He remained floating there calmly.
"Master..."
The word escaped Theia’s lips almost unconsciously.

At the same instant, the summoner bond connecting Luke to his summons suddenly became unmistakably clear, and the familiar presence that Aurora, Vaelira, Theia, and the others had never been able to properly feel from the doppelganger now radiated directly from the Titan standing above them.
This was Luke.
The original Luke.
Behind him, some of the confusion clouding Aurielle’s mind finally began to clear, and when she looked toward the towering figure protecting her, recognition appeared across her mismatched eyes.
"Luke..."
Her voice came out softly, but Luke didn’t turn toward her.
His attention remained fixed entirely upon Rhaenyra.
There was no playfulness in his expression, nor any trace of the nervous husband who usually tried to escape whenever several of his wives gathered in one place.
He had already learned everything that happened through the memories and information carried by his clone.
And right now, his gaze toward Rhaenyra was cold.
Before Aurielle could move closer, space rippled beside her.
WHOOSH!
Luke’s doppelganger reappeared wearing Valzareth, immediately reaching out and taking hold of Aurielle before carrying her away from the confrontation.

The clone descended toward the territory below, where Aurora and Vaelira lay unconscious from the Dragon Roar, and without wasting time, he lifted both of them using his enhanced strength before moving toward Theia.
Theia tried to rise on her own, but her injuries made the effort almost pointless, so the clone simply picked her up as well before turning toward the Lord’s Estate.
Above them, Luke continued holding Rhaenyra’s tail while the others were evacuated behind him.
Aurielle remained conscious within the clone’s grasp, while Theia occasionally looked back toward the sky at the seventy-foot Titan who had appeared at the final instant.
Neither woman looked away.
As the clone carried them farther toward the mansion, the towering silhouette of Luke gradually became smaller in their vision until the buildings began blocking the battlefield from sight.
Soon afterward, the doppelganger reached the entrance connected to the Time Chamber and brought Aurielle, Aurora, Vaelira, and Theia inside.
Only after they crossed completely into safety did the last visible trace of Luke’s seventy-foot figure disappear from their view, leaving the original body outside to face the Ancient Dragon alone.
"Rhaenyra."
Outside Blackstone, Luke finally called her name, yet for once, even he couldn’t decide what emotion his voice was supposed to carry.

Should there be warmth because she was his wife, someone he was finally meeting again after such a long time, or should there be anger because only moments ago, she had nearly struck Aurielle and forced his entire territory unconscious beneath her Dragon Roar?

Before Luke could properly settle those conflicting thoughts, Rhaenyra’s thousand-meter dragon body rapidly began shrinking, the crimson scales and gigantic wings disappearing as she returned to her humanoid form and floated calmly in front of his seventy-foot Titan figure.
She looked directly toward his giant armored face before speaking with faint mockery.
"What happened? Are you angry because of what I did earlier?"

chapters.title: Chapter 354: Volume II Ends With Luke Getting Kidnapped by His Wife!
paragraphs: Without waiting for his answer, Rhaenyra floated even closer until she was almost directly before his face, and whatever amusement had remained in her expression disappeared.
"Don’t tell me, Luke, that you’re actually trying to act like my husband."
Her golden draconic eyes stared into his as her voice became colder.
"Don’t, because a marriage ceremony doesn’t decide a dragon’s partner."
Luke’s expression barely changed after hearing those words, although the fingers of his right hand slowly clenched.
He knew exactly where that rejection came from.
’Because I’m weak...’

During the time they had remained apart, Luke had learned considerably more about dragons and their traditions, including one particularly important fact: dragons almost never willingly accepted someone weaker than themselves as their true partner.
Rhaenyra’s situation had been different from the beginning.

Her family had already rejected the marriage arrangement involving the Dragon Hero, so when the Hero of Light was summoned and the Dragon Temples demanded that a royal princess be sent to marry him, even Rhaenyra’s family, despite possessing demi-gods among their bloodline, couldn’t simply reject the priesthood a second time.
Doing so would have been dangerously close to openly disrespecting the Dragon God and the traditions upheld by the Dragon Temples.
That was why Rhaenyra had married him.
Not because she had chosen him.
Rhaenyra’s voice interrupted his thoughts, although this time there was no mockery in it, only obvious annoyance.
"Come with me. My grandmother wants to see you."
Luke didn’t answer immediately.
For several seconds, he simply floated there while the wind moved between them, and then his voice finally emerged from beneath the Titan armor.
"And if I refuse?"
Even Rhaenyra fell silent.

For a moment, she simply stared at the giant standing before her, because the person confronting her now felt completely different from the weak Hero she had subdued and carried away barely two months earlier.

Luke had already reached D-Rank, yet the aura radiating from his current Titan body reached far beyond what someone at that realm should normally possess, while the strange seventy-foot form standing before her gave Rhaenyra an even more uncomfortable feeling.
Her golden draconic gaze slowly moved across his armored body.
’This form...’
The more carefully she observed it, the more certain she became that Luke’s current body was fundamentally different from the one she remembered.
If she reduced her own strength to Luke’s realm and fought him as an equal, Rhaenyra doubted whether her dragon body could even survive a direct punch from this giant.
She paused upon that thought before correcting herself.
’No... it isn’t "maybe."’
’At the same realm, that punch would destroy me.’
Luke had become something far beyond the weak human she remembered, and even his presence now carried something that hadn’t existed when she first met him.
However—
Rhaenyra quietly sighed.
He was still weak.
At least, compared to the other Heroes.
Several of them had already crossed B-Rank and were now racing toward A-Rank, while Luke had only recently reached D-Rank despite possessing combat power far beyond his cultivation realm.
’He’s still too weak.’
Once she reached that conclusion, whatever brief interest his transformation had created faded beneath her usual confidence.
"I’ll say this one last time, Luke."
Her voice became cold again.
"Come with me peacefully, or I’ll use force just like I did before."
At almost the same moment, the System’s voice appeared inside Luke’s mind.
[Ahem! Luke, pride is one thing, but maybe you should actually listen to your wife this time, because technically... she isn’t wrong.]
Luke completely ignored it.
Unfortunately, this might have been one of those rare moments when listening to the System would have saved him considerable pain.
Luke drew back his arm.
Then he punched Rhaenyra.
WHOOOOOSH!
His gigantic fist tore through the air toward her, and seeing the incoming attack, Rhaenyra merely released another tired sigh.
"So you chose the painful way."
She raised one hand.
Just like the second day after Luke had arrived in this world.
THUUUUMP!

Luke’s gigantic fist slammed directly into her palm, releasing a violent shockwave that spread through the surrounding sky and pushed the nearby clouds apart, yet Rhaenyra’s comparatively tiny humanoid body didn’t move backward even slightly.
Her hand remained pressed against his knuckles as though she had stopped something completely ordinary.
Luke showed no surprise.
He had known this would happen before he even threw the punch.

Rhaenyra was now A-Rank, while Luke himself remained D-Rank, and even with the overwhelming advantages of his Titan body, the punch he had just thrown only contained power around the Mid-B-Rank level.
There was no realistic chance of overpowering her.
Still, he had thrown it.
Not because he expected to win, but because there was something the Luke from two months ago would never have possessed enough confidence to say.
A smile slowly appeared across his gigantic face.
"I am your husband, Rhaenyra Crimsonscale, and whether you like it or not, that is the truth."
For the first time since meeting her, Luke said those words without hesitation.
Without fear.
Without shrinking away simply because the dragon standing before him was stronger.
Unfortunately, courage didn’t protect him from the consequences.
Rhaenyra’s expression changed instantly.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Luke barely registered her movement before a fist struck directly into his chest.
His Titan armor and chest tore apart beneath the impact as his seventy-foot body became a black blur across the sky, flying backward for kilometers before crashing directly into a distant mountain.
BOOOOOOM!
The mountain shattered beneath the collision, stone and dust erupting outward as Luke’s broken Titan body disappeared beneath the collapsing rock.
Then Rhaenyra’s furious voice echoed across the ruined landscape.
"Say that again."
Those were the final words heard across Blackstone before Rhaenyra vanished from the Human Continent, taking Luke’s broken body along with her.
And with that—
Volume II came to an end.
Ahem!
Well... I definitely didn’t plan for Volume II to end exactly like this.
The original ending was supposed to have Luke receive a little more beating before Rhaenyra eventually carried his sorry body toward the Dragon Continent between her claws.
Yeah, extremely romantic.
But—
Luke decided to open his mouth and openly claim that Rhaenyra was his wife, and all of you already know what happened immediately afterward.
[Ahem!]
Okay, okay!
First of all, thank you to everyone who has continued reading this novel and stayed with both me and Luke throughout his journey so far.
So, what happens next?

Volume III will take place on the Dragon Continent, where Luke will finally begin discovering the greater structure of Valtharion, its different races, powers, and many of the things that have remained outside his reach until now.
Of course, while learning all of that, he will also have the considerably more dangerous task of trying not to die while conquering his fiery dragon wife.
There will also be new rivals waiting for him.
The Dragon Hero?
Nah, that guy is currently far too strong for Luke.
But our MC will reach that level as well.
He just needs time.

After the Dragon Continent arc, there will be a major timeskip leading toward the end of the one-year agreement, and the following volume will focus heavily on Nyra, Luke’s fourth wife, where he will finally save her—or perhaps more accurately, openly claim her.
And after that...
The Hero Ceremony.
So I hope everyone is excited for what comes next, because I definitely am.
Thank you again for staying with the story.
Your most amazing author,
—EternalVoidRuler
No argument on this.

chapters.title: Chapter 355: Luke Survives Rhaenyra... Then Flirts With Her Sister?!
paragraphs: Volume III - ??? (Title will be decided at the end of volume...)
27th Day of Fructus Month, Year 50,001.

Within the Dragon Continent of Kharenthyr, the largest among all the known continents of Valtharion, there remained territories so vast that even kingdoms elsewhere could appear small in comparison, although that title only applied to the lands known to the current races.
Beyond the Endless Sea, nobody truly knew what remained.

Some believed there were forgotten lands hidden beyond those endless waters, while others believed nothing existed there at all, but since nobody who ventured far enough had ever returned with a reliable answer, Kharenthyr continued to be regarded as the largest known continent of Valtharion.
Within one of its many territories, a region known as Bravaryn, there something resembling a dead body lay beneath a tree in the middle of the wilderness.

The man was half-naked from the waist up, with only a pair of badly torn pants remaining on his body, and although he was technically still alive, the way he had been lying there completely motionless for days made him look enough like a corpse that anyone passing nearby could easily make the wrong assumption.
Apparently, one particular woman had been wondering the exact same thing.

She was crouched beside him beneath the shade of the tree, her long snow-white hair falling around her shoulders while two silver-crystal dragon horns rose elegantly from her head, and although the position caused part of her skirt to shift upward toward the unconscious man’s side, her attention remained entirely focused on the stick currently held between her fingers.
Poke.
She pressed the end of the stick against his cheek.
Nothing happened.
Poke. Poke.
The man’s face shifted slightly beneath the pressure, yet there was still no genuine reaction, causing the young woman to continue the strange ritual she had repeated every day for the past week.
For exactly one minute each day, she would come here, crouch beside him, and poke his face with a stick just to see whether the supposedly healed man had finally decided to wake up.
Until now, the result had always been the same.
This time, however, a faint groan finally escaped him.

The woman’s icy-blue draconic eyes immediately brightened with curiosity as she stopped the stick halfway toward his cheek, because after an entire week of receiving absolutely no response, the sleeping corpse had finally done something.
Instead of disturbing him further, she remained where she was and quietly waited to see what he would do once he fully regained consciousness.
Luke’s eyelids slowly opened.

His mind remained hazy while his vision refused to properly focus, leaving the surrounding trees and patches of sunlight blurred together for several seconds before his senses gradually began returning.
He stared upward first, finding branches and green leaves above him, then slowly shifted his gaze around the unfamiliar wilderness as he tried to understand where he had ended up.
Eventually, his eyes moved toward the woman crouching beside him.
Luke saw her snow-white hair first, followed by the pair of silver-crystal horns rising from her head, and then her beautiful face framed by those calm icy-blue eyes.
His gaze remained there for approximately half a second.
Then it moved downward.
Because of the way Emberlyn was crouching beside him, Luke’s current position gave him a rather unfortunate—or perhaps fortunate—view beneath part of her shifted skirt.
His blue eyes focused for a moment.
Then, without the slightest hesitation, Luke gave his first opinion after waking from a week-long coma.
"Those red panties don’t suit you. I think blue would look much better."
Silence immediately descended beneath the tree.
Emberlyn stared at him blankly, apparently needing several seconds to understand why the supposedly half-dead Hero’s first words after awakening had involved the color blue.
Then realization struck.

Her calm expression finally broke as a faint red color spread across her face, and she quickly adjusted her skirt while staring at Luke as though reconsidering whether allowing him to wake up had actually been a good idea.
Luke, however, showed absolutely no concern for the consequences of his observation.
Instead, he pushed himself up from the ground and stretched his arms above his head, feeling several joints release after remaining motionless for so long.
His body felt surprisingly normal.
There was no lingering pain from Rhaenyra’s punch, no broken bones, no torn muscles, and none of the injuries he distinctly remembered receiving before everything had gone black.
Luke rolled one shoulder before looking around again.
"Where the hell am I?"
Emberlyn finally recovered from his earlier comment and tossed the stick away, deciding that after successfully awakening the strange human, it had fulfilled its purpose.
"If I’d known Rhaenyra was going to bring you back in a near-dead state, I suppose letting Grandma bring you herself in a half-dead state wouldn’t have made much difference."
Luke slowly turned toward her.
His mouth twitched.

’wife...?’

Within the Dragon Continent of Kharenthyr, the largest among all the known continents of Valtharion, there remained territories so vast that even kingdoms elsewhere could appear small in comparison, although that title only applied to the lands known to the current races.
Beyond the Endless Sea, nobody truly knew what remained.

Some believed there were forgotten lands hidden beyond those endless waters, while others believed nothing existed there at all, but since nobody who ventured far enough had ever returned with a reliable answer, Kharenthyr continued to be regarded as the largest known continent of Valtharion.

chapters.title: Chapter 356: Rhaenyra Catches Her Husband Flirting With Her Sister!
paragraphs: As Luke and Emberlyn continued through the palace grounds, every servant they passed immediately lowered their head toward the Dragon Princess, although more than a few secretly shifted their gaze toward Luke once she had walked past.
Their curiosity was understandable, because the man casually walking beside Her Highness possessed none of the obvious draconic features commonly seen throughout Kharenthyr.

There were no horns above his head, no scales along his skin, and no wings resting behind his back, yet despite clearly being an outsider, he was walking beside Emberlyn as though doing so were completely natural.
Luke noticed those curious glances almost immediately, and after watching another pair of servants bow deeply as Emberlyn passed, a playful smile appeared on his face.
"So, do I need to bow to you as well, My Princess?" Luke asked while walking beside her, then deliberately changed the address. "Or should I call you Your Highness?"
Emberlyn paused for a moment before turning toward him with a strange look.
This human genuinely confused her.

Almost everyone Emberlyn encountered either showed her proper respect because of her status or remained cautious around her because of her strength, and among the younger dragons especially, very few people behaved casually enough to openly tease her like this.
Yet Luke seemed completely comfortable.
’Maybe he simply doesn’t know anything about me.’
That seemed like the most reasonable explanation, because if Luke had only recently arrived on the Dragon Continent, then he probably had no idea about her reputation or strength.
With that thought, Emberlyn resumed walking.
"It’s up to you."
"Tch, you’re no fun."
Luke clicked his tongue before increasing his pace slightly and catching up beside her again, while Emberlyn ignored his complaint and continued toward the deeper sections of the palace.
Soon, the two disappeared beyond another golden passageway, leaving the servants who had been bowing behind them finally free to raise their heads.
"Who was that man?"
"I don’t know, but he was really handsome."
Another servant looked toward the corridor where Luke and Emberlyn had disappeared.
"Maybe he’s another suitor trying to marry Lady Emberlyn?"
That possibility immediately made sense to several of them, because this certainly wouldn’t have been the first time someone had come hoping to obtain Emberlyn’s hand.

She wasn’t merely regarded as one of the strongest dragons among her generation, but also as one of the most beautiful, which naturally meant powerful young dragons and heirs from influential bloodlines had attempted to approach her before.
None of them, however, knew that the strange human walking beside her was considerably more complicated than another ordinary suitor.
After walking farther into the palace, Emberlyn eventually brought Luke before a gigantic bathhouse whose appearance alone displayed the excessive wealth dragons seemed to consider normal.

Rubies and diamonds had been embedded throughout the walls and pillars in such quantities that Luke briefly wondered whether dragons simply treated gemstones as ordinary decorations, while faint reflections from the surrounding crystals spread across the polished golden floor.
However, what drew Luke’s attention most was the pool occupying nearly the entire central section.
Calling it a pool barely seemed accurate.
It stretched for several kilometers through the bathhouse, its clear water disappearing far enough into the distance that it looked closer to a private lake than something built merely for bathing.
’No wonder this palace is so ridiculously big.’

Luke nodded to himself as he finally understood part of the reason behind the unusual scale of everything around him, because while dragons could adjust their size to a certain degree, some clearly preferred remaining in their natural forms whenever possible.
"Hmm, not bad."
Luke walked closer to the water before looking around the otherwise empty bathhouse.
"Does anyone actually use this place?"
He hadn’t really expected an answer, especially since he had already started removing the remains of his torn clothing, but Emberlyn’s calm voice immediately came from behind him.
"Yes. It’s big sister bathhouse."
Luke stopped.
He slowly looked over his shoulder.
His silence wasn’t caused only by discovering that he was about to bathe inside Rhaenyra’s personal bathhouse, because there was another considerably more immediate problem.
She hadn’t left.
Emberlyn was still standing several steps behind him, and Luke had already removed the torn pants that had been the last piece of clothing covering him.
Luke turned fully toward her with a speechless expression, only to become even more surprised when he noticed where Emberlyn’s attention had gone.
Her icy-blue gaze had lowered and were now looking at his dangling little brother.
"Miss Emberlyn..." Luke slowly said while looking at her. "Are you planning to keep staring?"

Emberlyn didn’t immediately answer, and rather than showing the embarrassment Luke expected, she continued examining his little brother with the same calm curiosity she had displayed since meeting him.
That reaction only made Luke more amused.
’This younger sister is surprisingly bold.’
He stepped closer until only a small distance remained between them, then reached out with his right hand and placed it around her waist.
Emberlyn’s calm expression finally shifted.
Before she could properly react to the unexpected contact, Luke pulled her closer until her body rested against his.
"Don’t you know that a beautiful woman like you should keep some distance from men?"
Emberlyn remained completely still for several seconds.

The situation was unfamiliar enough that her mind needed a moment to process it, because despite the many dragons who had tried approaching her over the years, none had ever simply placed an arm around her waist and pulled her into an embrace.
Her father and grandfather had shown her affection before, but that had always been limited to ordinary familial gestures such as patting her head.
Being held by an unrelated man was entirely different.
Luke noticed the unusual stillness in her expression and raised an eyebrow.
"Don’t tell me you’ve never been this close to a man before?"

Until now, Emberlyn’s calm reaction to his naked body had made Luke assume she possessed at least some experience with situations like this, yet the way she had completely frozen after being embraced suggested the exact opposite.
Before Emberlyn could answer, however, a familiar blue screen abruptly appeared before Luke.
[Sigh, Luke, you’re playing with fire.]
Luke mentally scoffed.
’What fire? She feels more like hot ice.’
The System remained silent for a moment before responding.
[Luke, I’m not talking about her.]
Luke became confused.
[Just look behind her.]
’Behind her?’
Still keeping one arm around Emberlyn, Luke tilted his head slightly and looked past her shoulder.
Then his body stiffened.
Standing at the entrance of the bathhouse was Rhaenyra.
"After you’re finished flirting with my sister, come outside."
Her golden draconic gaze moved between the two of them.
"Grandma is waiting for you."
Luke remained silent.

This was the same woman who had nearly killed him during their previous encounter, so seeing her standing there while he was completely naked and holding her younger sister against himself should probably have been one of the most dangerous situations he had encountered since arriving in Kharenthyr.
What confused him, however, was Rhaenyra’s reaction.
He had expected anger similar to Aurielle’s or Selene’s whenever another woman became too close to him, yet Rhaenyra merely stood there with obvious irritation without immediately attacking.
’Right...’
Luke’s expression changed slightly.
’She doesn’t love me.’
That thought immediately explained much of her restraint, although the irritation visible in her golden eyes still left him uncertain about what exactly bothered her.
Perhaps she simply disliked seeing the man officially regarded as her husband flirting with her younger sister, especially when Emberlyn had originally been the princess intended to marry him.
’Or maybe she’s actually jealous but doesn’t want to show it because of that personality of hers.’
Luke entertained that possibility for barely a second before dismissing it himself.
’No... probably not.’
If Rhaenyra had genuinely become jealous enough to lose control, Luke suspected he would already have been embedded inside another mountain.
What Luke didn’t know was that Rhaenyra had, in fact, been extremely tempted to hit him again.

Unfortunately for her, nearly killing him during their previous encounter had earned her a long lecture from Zephyrielle and a very clear warning not to repeat the same mistake, leaving Rhaenyra with little choice but to tolerate her so-called husband for now.
After giving Luke one final look, she turned away.
"Don’t make Grandma wait."
Then she left the bathhouse.
Only after Rhaenyra disappeared beyond the entrance did Luke release the breath he had unconsciously been holding.
’That went surprisingly well.’
He turned his attention back toward Emberlyn and finally realized that his arm was still wrapped around her waist.
She hadn’t moved.
"Ahh, sorry."
Luke released her immediately before stepping back.
"I forgot I was still holding you."
He gave her cheek a light pat, finding the skin unexpectedly soft beneath his fingers, then smiled playfully as he turned toward the waiting water.
"I’ll take my bath now, so you can wait outside."
Without waiting for another response, Luke stepped into the clear water and gradually submerged himself, finally washing away the dirt left from spending an entire week unconscious beneath a tree.
Emberlyn remained standing where he had left her for several moments.

Only after Luke was already inside the pool did her mind seem to fully return, and this time, a much more noticeable blush spread across her face as she remembered how casually he had pulled her against himself.
Luke wasn’t looking in her direction anymore.
Emberlyn silently stared at him for another moment before turning around and walking toward the exit, although her usual composed expression had still not completely returned.
The gigantic golden doors slowly closed behind her.
THUUUUM.
Only then was Luke finally left alone inside the bathhouse.

chapters.title: Chapter 357: All Four Titan Spirits Finally Wake Up!
paragraphs: Inside the bathhouse, Luke remained submerged in the warm water while leaning against the edge of the pool, although his thoughts had already drifted far away from Kharenthyr.
"How are Aurielle and the others doing...?"

He tried once again to sense the connection with his clones, but just like before, something within the Dragon Continent seemed to be interfering with it, preventing him from receiving anything clearly.
That failure reminded Luke of another problem he had been putting aside.
His Shadow of Nyx was still only a D-Rank ability.

Although the System had granted him the legendary racial ability itself, its current strength still depended upon Luke’s own realm unless he personally learned and mastered the underlying principles, or eventually raised the ability all the way to SSS-Rank. Against opponents near his own level, that limitation wasn’t particularly troublesome, but Luke had been fighting beings far above D-Rank often enough to understand that even a legendary ability could become unreliable when the difference in realm became too large.
With a quiet sigh, Luke relaxed farther against the side of the pool while staring absently across the clear water, wondering what he should focus on next.
At that exact moment, however, four small figures suddenly materialized in front of him.
"Huh?"
Luke opened his half-closed eyes, and the instant he recognized the four familiar figures floating above the water, a genuine smile appeared on his face.
"Welcome back, everyone."

His mood visibly brightened as Caelith gently descended onto his right shoulder, while Nyx settled comfortably on the left. Myrkhal, naturally choosing the least normal place available, sat directly on top of Luke’s head and began swinging his small legs back and forth, lightly hitting Luke’s forehead with every movement, while Sevaroth remained floating in front of him.
"Yeah, it seems quite some time has passed," Caelith said gently as she looked around the unfamiliar bathhouse.
Luke was just about to explain everything that had happened during their absence when Nyx raised a hand and stopped him.
"Sevaroth already told us what happened while we were asleep, so you don’t need to explain everything again."
Luke glanced toward Sevaroth before giving a small nod, while Nyx looked around at the golden walls and distant edge of the oversized pool.
"So where are we now?"
"In Kharenthyr, the Dragon Continent, where my dragon wife lives."
Luke paused for a moment before adding with a helpless expression, "She kidnapped me from the Human Continent."
The four Titan spirits immediately reacted with quiet amusement, and even Nyx couldn’t completely hide his smile after hearing that Luke had somehow managed to get kidnapped by his own wife.
"Hmm, that explains it," Sevaroth said while sensing the surrounding atmosphere. "The air here feels different, and even this palace isn’t as simple as it looks."
Luke nodded, although seeing all four of them together reminded him of something far more important than the palace around them.
There was one question he had wanted to ask for a long time.
"Everyone, can you help me with my cultivation?"

The playful atmosphere faded slightly as Nyx, Caelith, and Sevaroth immediately turned their attention toward him, while Myrkhal continued swinging his legs from the top of Luke’s head as though the matter had nothing to do with him.
Nyx smiled faintly.
"We already discussed that before we went to sleep, although we were forced into slumber before we had the chance to explain it to you."
Luke immediately became more attentive, but Nyx remained silent for a few seconds before his expression grew noticeably more serious.
"Luke, I don’t know exactly how your System transformed you into a real Titan, but from what we can sense, your current state is still incomplete."
Luke’s smile faded.
Nyx continued, "Only a small fraction of our bloodlines has truly merged with you, while most of your original bloodline still retains human characteristics."
Luke listened carefully without interrupting, and after Nyx finished speaking, Caelith continued the explanation.
"The clearest example is your current stage. Your System made you a low-level Titan appropriate for your Silver-stage, or D-Rank, body, instead of turning you into a D-Rank Firstborn Titan."
Luke looked toward her in confusion.
"Aren’t those the same thing?"
Nyx shook his head.

"No. Although we understand why your System did it this way, because genuine Firstborn Titans were born at much higher realms, where our bodies were already capable of carrying the power contained within our bloodlines."
He looked directly at Luke.
"Your current body can’t."
Luke fell silent.

If that was really the case, then the difference between what he currently was and a genuine Firstborn Titan was considerably greater than he had assumed, which also meant that reaching that level through ordinary cultivation might take far longer than he wanted.
Caelith noticed the change in his expression and smiled gently.
"However, after seeing that your System successfully placed four of our bloodlines inside you and somehow allowed them to coexist without clashing, we reached another conclusion."
Luke turned slightly toward her.
"What conclusion?"
"Even though we can’t reproduce what your System did, you already possess Myrkhal’s bloodline, and that gives us another possibility."
The moment his name was mentioned, Myrkhal immediately became more energetic, swinging his legs faster while grabbing a handful of Luke’s black hair and lightly pulling it.
Luke ignored him.
"Can you stop talking in riddles and just tell me?"
Nyx gave a faint smile before finally explaining.
"Fine. Rather than turning you into a Titan body capable of merely carrying all of our individual bloodlines, we’re thinking of doing something completely different."
Luke waited.
"We want to turn your body into something capable of creating and sustaining an entirely new bloodline, one formed by combining all of ours."
Luke froze.
For several seconds, even the faint movement of the water around him seemed to disappear from his attention as he processed what Nyx had just said.
The idea was absurd enough that even the Origin Titan would likely have been shocked by it.

Luke was already doing something that should have been extremely difficult, because four Forbidden Titan bloodlines existed inside the same body without destroying one another, while at his peak state he could still access the complete power belonging to each individual Titan.
Yet this method would take that concept much further.

Instead of merely allowing Luke to wield each Forbidden Titan separately, the bloodlines themselves would begin merging into a completely new lineage, which meant that in the future, Luke might even become capable of combining two or more Forbidden elements directly rather than simply switching between them.

Even Myrkhal’s Titan Fusion was still different from what Nyx was proposing, because despite Myrkhal’s ability to imitate and combine Titan characteristics through his Faces, even he had never been capable of perfectly fusing multiple Forbidden Titans into one permanent existence. His Faces simply couldn’t withstand the weight of those bloodlines indefinitely, while Luke’s System and Nexus Harmony had somehow already created the foundation necessary to make such coexistence possible.
"Is that actually possible?"
Luke’s voice carried genuine disbelief, but Nyx nodded without hesitation.
"It should be."

He paused briefly before continuing, "If this succeeds, you won’t simply become a stronger version of your current Silver-stage Titan body. You will become an entirely different kind of Titan, although the true path won’t begin until you break through into the Golden realm."
Luke’s attention sharpened even further.

Nyx continued, "And once the new body stabilizes, you won’t need to rely on Titan transformation just to access the physical advantages of your bloodline, because your normal body itself will gradually begin carrying those Titan characteristics."
Caelith nodded beside him.
"After all, a Titan of the same realm is naturally far stronger than most other races, because that strength belongs to the body itself rather than coming from a temporary transformation."
Those words immediately reminded Luke of another question that had bothered him for quite some time.
"Then how exactly does my Titan transformation work?"
The four spirits looked toward him.

Luke continued, "I mean, I can already use many of your abilities in my normal form, but once I transform, I can use your powers much more freely, without those restrictions, while also gaining the Titan physical stats."
For a moment, all four Titan spirits simply looked at him.
Then amused smiles appeared on their faces.
"You still haven’t figured that out by yourself?"
Luke tilted his head slightly because, despite everything he had learned about Titans so far, he genuinely hadn’t understood what his transformation actually represented.
Seeing his confusion, Sevaroth finally took over the explanation.
"Haven’t you ever wondered why maintaining your Titan form consumes so much more stamina and energy than using your abilities normally?"
Luke immediately nodded, because that question had bothered him more than once, especially during longer battles where the difference in consumption became painfully obvious.

Sevaroth continued, "That’s because your Titan transformation isn’t actually turning you into something completely different. Your System is simply forcing the Titan bloodline hidden inside your current body into an overexcited state, bringing out far more of its power than your normal body can naturally sustain."
Luke’s expression changed slightly as he listened.

"In other words," Sevaroth continued, "your transformation temporarily forces your current-realm Titan bloodline toward its prime state, which is why you can use its physical strength, racial characteristics, and abilities with far fewer restraints."
Luke finally began connecting everything.
"So if my bloodline became pure enough..."

"You wouldn’t need that temporary state anymore," Sevaroth finished for him. "Your normal body itself would already possess those characteristics, so there would be nothing left for the transformation to forcibly awaken."
Luke became silent for a moment as the explanation finally made sense.

His Titan transformation wasn’t giving him strength that didn’t belong to him; instead, the System was forcibly drawing out the portion of Titan power already hidden within his current-realm bloodline, temporarily pushing his body into a state it wasn’t naturally capable of maintaining.
"No wonder the stamina consumption is so ridiculous."

chapters.title: Chapter 358: Luke’s New Titan Cultivation Path Is Finally Revealed!
paragraphs: Maintaining that state meant continuously feeding energy into a body that wasn’t yet naturally capable of supporting it.
Once that realization settled in, Luke’s thoughts immediately returned to the new cultivation path the four Titans had been discussing.
"Then when can I start cultivating?"
There was clear anticipation in his voice, because if this method truly worked, then his current weakness wouldn’t remain forever.
The memory of Rhaenyra’s punch immediately returned to him, along with the feeling of his body being shattered and sent through a mountain before he could properly resist.

Luke understood that he had only arrived in Valtharion a few months ago, while most of the people around him had spent years, decades, or even longer cultivating their strength, so comparing himself with them wasn’t entirely fair.
The problem was that the other summoned Heroes hadn’t been here much longer than him either, yet several had already reached B-Rank.
Luke had no intention of remaining behind.

However, seeing the excitement appearing on his face, the four Titan spirits exchanged glances, because what they were about to explain was considerably less pleasant than the result Luke was imagining.
"Luke," Nyx finally said, "this cultivation won’t be easy, because you aren’t simply trying to break through from one realm to another."
His expression became more serious.
"At every realm, you’ll be constructing a new Titan body."
Luke’s excitement faded slightly after hearing that, although he remained quiet and allowed Nyx to continue.

"There are benefits, of course. Like we said earlier, once your body becomes complete enough, you won’t need to rely on Titan transformation merely to access the physical strength that should naturally belong to you, and your normal form will gradually be capable of carrying your full Titan characteristics."
Nyx paused before adding another important point.
"This cultivation path will also eliminate the Early, Mid, High, and Peak divisions you’re accustomed to."
Luke raised an eyebrow.
"So once I finish constructing the Titan body of my current realm..."

"You break through directly into the next realm," Nyx confirmed. "There won’t be four smaller stages in between, because your advancement depends on completing the body itself rather than accumulating enough energy to move through minor stages."
That immediately sounded far better to Luke.
However, Nyx’s expression didn’t relax.
"Unfortunately..."
Luke’s smile disappeared again.
Nyx let out a quiet sigh before finally giving him a basic explanation of what the cultivation would actually require.
"In this path, every major realm is divided into eight connected Reformations, and every single one must be completed before your body can advance."
[FIRST REFORMATION]
"BLOOD"
Methods:
"FIRSTBORN BLOOD SCRIPT"
"BLOODLINE PREDATION"
Purpose:
Purify Luke’s existing blood and rewrite it into the foundation of his new Titan lineage.

During this process, Luke must engrave the principles belonging to every Titan currently fused with him directly into his blood, meaning concepts such as Void, Form, Creation, Seal, and any future Titan principle must eventually exist within every refined portion of his blood rather than remaining isolated within separate bloodlines.

At the same time, Bloodline Predation allows him to hunt powerful creatures and extract suitable blood essence, which can then be broken down and used as evolutionary material for the developing lineage.
[SECOND REFORMATION]
"HEART"
Method:
"ORIGIN HEART FORGE"
Purpose:
Transform Luke’s heart from a mortal circulation organ into a living forge capable of continuously refining Titan blood.

Rather than merely pumping blood through his body, the completed Titan Heart must gradually become capable of tempering, purifying, and strengthening the blood with every circulation, allowing the new lineage to sustain itself naturally instead of depending entirely upon conscious refinement.
[THIRD REFORMATION]
"MARROW"
Method:
"GENESIS MARROW"
Purpose:
Rewrite the source responsible for creating new blood.

Without Genesis Marrow, Luke’s body would continue producing inferior blood according to its previous biological structure, forcing him to repeatedly purify newly created blood even after completing the Firstborn Blood Script.
Once the marrow is successfully rewritten, however, the body itself will begin producing blood already suited to Luke’s evolving Titan lineage.
[FOURTH REFORMATION]
"SKELETON & FLESH"
Methods:
"TITAN BONE DOMINION"
"LAW-BEARING FLESH"
Purpose:
Create a physical frame capable of surviving the pressure generated by Luke’s evolving bloodline and multiple Titan Authorities.

The bones must become strong enough to support the force produced by a true Titan body, while the flesh, muscles, tendons, and skin must be rewritten until they can naturally contain and transmit the principles belonging to every Titan lineage fused into Luke.
[FIFTH REFORMATION]
"MIND & NERVOUS SYSTEM"
Methods:
"TITAN MIND PARTITION"
"AUTHORITY NERVOUS SYSTEM"
Purpose:
Create a mind and neural structure capable of controlling numerous Titan Authorities simultaneously.

As Luke gains more Titans, simply possessing their powers will no longer be enough, because his consciousness and nervous system must also become capable of processing, controlling, and transmitting several Forbidden principles without suffering overload or internal conflict.
[SIXTH REFORMATION]
"SOUL"
Method:
"SOUL-BLOOD SYNCHRONIZATION"
Purpose:
Force Luke’s soul to fully recognize the evolving Titan body as its natural vessel.

If the bloodline becomes too different from the soul inhabiting it, rejection will eventually appear, so the soul itself must continuously evolve alongside the body until Luke no longer feels as though he is transforming into a Titan, but instead recognizes the Titan body as his true biological existence.
[SEVENTH REFORMATION]
"ORGANS"
Method:
"TWELVE TITAN ORGANS"
Classification:
Authority Organogenesis
Purpose:
Replace the limitations of ordinary biological organs with a unified Titan internal system.

Every major organ must gradually be reconstructed so it can function under the pressure of multiple Forbidden Titan principles, eventually allowing Luke’s entire internal body to operate as one complete Titan system rather than a collection of strengthened human organs.
[EIGHTH REFORMATION]
"BREAKTHROUGH"
Methods:
"TITAN MOLTING
"HEAVENLY THUNDER TEMPERING"
Purpose:
Destroy the obsolete body state and permanently establish the next Titan realm.

After the previous seven Reformations are completed, Luke must shed the limitations of his old body through Titan Molting, allowing a new body to emerge from the structure he has spent the entire realm constructing.
The newly formed body must then endure natural thunder and lightning, using that external force to temper every completed Reformation at once and permanently stabilize the next Titan realm.
Nyx allowed Luke several moments to absorb the information before speaking again.
"That’s only the basic overview. The actual process behind every Reformation is far more complicated, and there is still one major problem."
Luke looked toward him again.
Nyx sighed because, in theory, the path they had designed suited Luke almost perfectly.

Myrkhal’s bloodline gave Luke something no ordinary Titan possessed, because its control over form and the unknown made it possible to suppress the rejection that should occur when fundamentally different bloodlines were forced together, turning otherwise incompatible lineage characteristics into something far more manageable.
Yet Myrkhal alone still wouldn’t be enough.

Luke also possessed Nexus Titan and its Titan Harmony, which meant that if the newly created bloodline successfully survived the fusion process, Nexus Harmony could unify the final result instead of allowing the Forbidden Titan characteristics to remain as separate powers inside the same body.
That was the truly frightening possibility.
Luke wouldn’t merely become a Titan carrying several Forbidden bloodlines.
He could eventually become one completely new Titan whose natural bloodline contained all of them.
Nyx briefly fell silent as the implications passed through his mind.
’If he truly succeeds...’

At his prime, Luke might eventually possess enough power to destroy an entire universe, and perhaps, if this path continued far enough, he could even reach the realm that Nyx and the others had once failed to touch.
While Nyx remained lost in that thought, Caelith finally turned toward Luke and explained the problem they had deliberately avoided mentioning until now.
Caelith looked toward Luke before finally revealing the problem they had been avoiding.
"Luke, none of us can directly temper your bloodline for you, which means you would have to personally engrave our principles into your blood, flesh, organs, soul, and every other Reformation."
Luke’s expression slowly became serious.

Caelith continued, "Void, Form, Creation, Seal, and every Forbidden principle you gain in the future would have to be understood well enough for you to reproduce them yourself, and before you can begin doing that properly, we would first have to teach you."
Luke remained silent for a moment before asking the question whose answer he already suspected he wasn’t going to like.
"Okay... and how long would that take?"
Caelith answered with the same gentle expression she always wore.
"A few billion years."
Luke stared at her.
Caelith stared back.
"...A few what?"
"Billion years."
For several seconds, nothing except the faint movement of water inside the bathhouse could be heard.
Luke slowly looked toward Nyx, hoping he would deny it, but Nyx remained completely serious.
Then he looked toward Sevaroth.
Same expression.
Finally, his gaze moved upward toward Myrkhal, who was still sitting comfortably on top of his head.
Myrkhal happily waved at him.
"...So you’re also part of this nonsense."
Luke’s mouth twitched as he chose to completely ignore Caelith’s earlier answer, although the calm expression on her face made it very clear that she hadn’t been joking.
Nyx finally spoke.
"Luke, we hold Authorities over Forbidden elements. Do you really think something like that can simply be learned in a few years?"
Luke remained silent.
"You already possess our bloodlines, our guidance, and a basic Titan body capable of interacting with those principles, which is the only reason a few billion years would even be possible."
Nyx’s expression became more serious.
"Without those advantages, even eternity might not be enough unless you were personally chosen by the universe or possessed talent specifically meant to comprehend those powers."
Luke leaned farther against the pool and stared upward.
"Okay, then I’ll die of old age first."
