Once the marrow is successfully rewritten, however, the body itself will begin producing blood already suited to Luke’s evolving Titan lineage.
[FOURTH REFORMATION]
"SKELETON & FLESH"
Methods:
"TITAN BONE DOMINION"
"LAW-BEARING FLESH"
Purpose:
Create a physical frame capable of surviving the pressure generated by Luke’s evolving bloodline and multiple Titan Authorities.

The bones must become strong enough to support the force produced by a true Titan body, while the flesh, muscles, tendons, and skin must be rewritten until they can naturally contain and transmit the principles belonging to every Titan lineage fused into Luke.
[FIFTH REFORMATION]
"MIND & NERVOUS SYSTEM"
Methods:
"TITAN MIND PARTITION"
"AUTHORITY NERVOUS SYSTEM"
Purpose:
Create a mind and neural structure capable of controlling numerous Titan Authorities simultaneously.

As Luke gains more Titans, simply possessing their powers will no longer be enough, because his consciousness and nervous system must also become capable of processing, controlling, and transmitting several Forbidden principles without suffering overload or internal conflict.
[SIXTH REFORMATION]
"SOUL"
Method:
"SOUL-BLOOD SYNCHRONIZATION"
Purpose:
Force Luke’s soul to fully recognize the evolving Titan body as its natural vessel.

If the bloodline becomes too different from the soul inhabiting it, rejection will eventually appear, so the soul itself must continuously evolve alongside the body until Luke no longer feels as though he is transforming into a Titan, but instead recognizes the Titan body as his true biological existence.
[SEVENTH REFORMATION]
"ORGANS"
Method:
"TWELVE TITAN ORGANS"
Classification:
Authority Organogenesis
Purpose:
Replace the limitations of ordinary biological organs with a unified Titan internal system.

Every major organ must gradually be reconstructed so it can function under the pressure of multiple Forbidden Titan principles, eventually allowing Luke’s entire internal body to operate as one complete Titan system rather than a collection of strengthened human organs.
[EIGHTH REFORMATION]
"BREAKTHROUGH"
Methods:
"TITAN MOLTING
"HEAVENLY THUNDER TEMPERING"
Purpose:
Destroy the obsolete body state and permanently establish the next Titan realm.

After the previous seven Reformations are completed, Luke must shed the limitations of his old body through Titan Molting, allowing a new body to emerge from the structure he has spent the entire realm constructing.
The newly formed body must then endure natural thunder and lightning, using that external force to temper every completed Reformation at once and permanently stabilize the next Titan realm.
Nyx allowed Luke several moments to absorb the information before speaking again.
"That’s only the basic overview.
The actual process behind every Reformation is far more complicated, and there is still one major problem."
Luke looked toward him again.
Nyx sighed because, in theory, the path they had designed suited Luke almost perfectly.

Myrkhal’s bloodline gave Luke something no ordinary Titan possessed, because its control over form and the unknown made it possible to suppress the rejection that should occur when fundamentally different bloodlines were forced together, turning otherwise incompatible lineage characteristics into something far more manageable.
Yet Myrkhal alone still wouldn’t be enough.

Luke also possessed Nexus Titan and its Titan Harmony, which meant that if the newly created bloodline successfully survived the fusion process, Nexus Harmony could unify the final result instead of allowing the Forbidden Titan characteristics to remain as separate powers inside the same body.
That was the truly frightening possibility.
Luke wouldn’t merely become a Titan carrying several Forbidden bloodlines.
He could eventually become one completely new Titan whose natural bloodline contained all of them.
Nyx briefly fell silent as the implications passed through his mind.
’If he truly succeeds...’

At his prime, Luke might eventually possess enough power to destroy an entire universe, and perhaps, if this path continued far enough, he could even reach the realm that Nyx and the others had once failed to touch.
While Nyx remained lost in that thought, Caelith finally turned toward Luke and explained the problem they had deliberately avoided mentioning until now.
Caelith looked toward Luke before finally revealing the problem they had been avoiding.
"Luke, none of us can directly temper your bloodline for you, which means you would have to personally engrave our principles into your blood, flesh, organs, soul, and every other Reformation."
Luke’s expression slowly became serious.

Caelith continued, "Void, Form, Creation, Seal, and every Forbidden principle you gain in the future would have to be understood well enough for you to reproduce them yourself, and before you can begin doing that properly, we would first have to teach you."
Luke remained silent for a moment before asking the question whose answer he already suspected he wasn’t going to like.
"Okay... and how long would that take?"
Caelith answered with the same gentle expression she always wore.
"A few billion years."
Luke stared at her.
Caelith stared back.
"...A few what?"
"Billion years."
For several seconds, nothing except the faint movement of water inside the bathhouse could be heard.
Luke slowly looked toward Nyx, hoping he would deny it, but Nyx remained completely serious.
Then he looked toward Sevaroth.
Same expression.
Finally, his gaze moved upward toward Myrkhal, who was still sitting comfortably on top of his head.
Myrkhal happily waved at him.
"...So you’re also part of this nonsense."
Luke’s mouth twitched as he chose to completely ignore Caelith’s earlier answer, although the calm expression on her face made it very clear that she hadn’t been joking.
Nyx finally spoke.
"Luke, we hold Authorities over Forbidden elements.
Do you really think something like that can simply be learned in a few years?"
Luke remained silent.
"You already possess our bloodlines, our guidance, and a basic Titan body capable of interacting with those principles, which is the only reason a few billion years would even be possible."
Nyx’s expression became more serious.
"Without those advantages, even eternity might not be enough unless you were personally chosen by the universe or possessed talent specifically meant to comprehend those powers."
Luke leaned farther against the pool and stared upward.
"Okay, then I’ll die of old age first."

chapters.title: Chapter 359: No Wonder the Other Heroes Reached B-Rank So Fast!
paragraphs: His mouth twitched again because he didn’t have billions of years to waste, and he certainly hadn’t been moving this desperately just to accomplish something after several cosmic eras.
Hell, Luke was currently trying to become strong enough to change his situation within a single year.
A few billion years wasn’t even remotely an option.
At that moment, however, the savior finally opened its mouth.
Or rather...
A familiar blue screen appeared before everyone.
[Ahem! Luke, I have a solution.]
Luke stared at the System screen.
The four Titan spirits also turned toward it.
For several seconds, all five of them carried almost the same expression, as though silently telling the System not to start speaking nonsense again.
Then they remembered exactly what they were dealing with.

This was the same System that had freed the Titan from imprisonment, allowed Luke to possess several Forbidden Titan bloodlines simultaneously, brought items from other universes, and repeatedly accomplished things that should have been impossible.
Maybe this time it actually did have a solution.
Luke straightened slightly.
“Continue. I’m listening.”
The System immediately responded.
[Well, there happens to be a special offer available right now.]
[You can obtain a cultivation technique that already contains every method they just described.]
Luke’s expression changed.
The System continued before he could interrupt.
[You won’t need to spend billions of years personally learning every Forbidden principle deeply enough to construct the refinement methods yourself.]
[The technique already contains the complete processes for engraving, purification, reconstruction, organogenesis, synchronization, and body evolution.]
[You only need to fulfill the external requirements, provide the necessary resources, and cultivate according to its instructions.]
A long System panel immediately unfolded before Luke.
Even Nyx, Caelith, Myrkhal, and Sevaroth became more attentive as the cultivation sequence appeared.
[CULTIVATION SEQUENCE]
For every major realm:
1. Hunt and devour suitable bloodline essence.
2. Refine and engrave the Blood Script.
3. Reforge the heart through Origin Heart Forge.
4. Rebuild the marrow through Genesis Marrow.
5. Refine the skeleton and flesh into a Titan body.
6. Refine the mind and nervous system.
7. Synchronize the soul with the evolving bloodline.
8. Complete Authority Organogenesis.
9. Enter Titan Molting.
10. Use natural heavenly lightning to temper the newly created body and complete the breakthrough.
Only after all ten stages have been completed can the practitioner enter the next Titan realm.
Luke carefully read through everything, while the Titan spirits silently examined the sequence as well.
None of them objected.
Although some details were far beyond ordinary cultivation, every major step matched the path they had just designed for Luke.
The System screen suddenly changed again.
[However, you only need to personally handle the first and final external requirements.]
Luke blinked.
“What?”
[You hunt and gather the required blood essence.]
[Then you cultivate.]

[The technique automatically performs Blood Script engraving, heart reforging, marrow reconstruction, flesh and bone refinement, mind and nerve evolution, soul synchronization, organogenesis, and Titan Molting according to the bloodlines and Authorities currently present inside you.]
Luke slowly sat upright.
[Once the internal evolution is complete, you only need to find suitable natural heavenly lightning and personally endure the final tempering.]
The System apparently wasn’t finished.
[Basically, you hunt, eat, cultivate, get struck by lightning, and become stronger.]
[No need to spend billions of years studying Forbidden principles or grind every internal refinement manually like some liver-grinding protagonist.]
Luke’s mouth twitched.
The four Titans also became strangely silent.
[After all, I am the best System, so naturally the System Market only provides the best products.]
The screen practically radiated smugness.
Then another message appeared.
[Should I purchase this cultivation technique?]
[Gods have started Divine Wars over techniques of this level, you know.]
Luke stared at the screen.
Nyx stared at the screen.
Caelith stared at the screen.
Sevaroth stared at the screen.
Even Myrkhal finally stopped swinging his legs.
For several seconds, nobody spoke.

The System’s sales pitch was already ridiculous enough, but the fact that Luke would only need to hunt bloodline creatures, provide their essence, cultivate, and then endure heavenly lightning while an entire multi-Authority Titan body reconstructed itself automatically was far more absurd.
But claiming that gods had started Divine Wars over such a technique was on another level entirely.
Luke eventually recovered first.
“So what’s the price?”
Despite everything, he still believed he might actually be able to afford it.

He currently possessed three Monthly Claims if Theia’s was included, along with roughly sixteen thousand accumulated charges, and although those resources were valuable, this technique clearly wasn’t something he could casually ignore.
[Calculating...]
Luke waited.
[A few System backlogs will be displayed during calculation.]
[Please ignore them.]
“...Fine.”
Luke nodded.
Another screen appeared.
[Luke is poor.]
[He doesn’t even have a single yandere wife or sugar mommy helping his financial situation.]
Luke’s eyebrow twitched.
[Therefore, the System has no choice but to spend money from its own pocket.]
[Ahh... what a generous and magnificent System I am. ( ̄▽ ̄)/]
Luke’s mouth twitched even harder.
The System continued calculating as though it couldn’t see his expression.
[Calculating...]
[Applying special discount...]
[Applying pathetic-host discount...]
Luke decided not to respond.
Finally, the calculation finished.
[Done.]
[Luke, the final price will be all of your remaining Monthly Claims for this year, every currently accumulated System charge, and any Monthly Claim obtained during the current month.]
Luke froze.
[Please sign here.]
A glowing signature box appeared beneath the message.
“O_O”
Luke’s mouth fell open.
“Are you robbing me?”
With that many Monthly Claims, he could obtain several extremely high-ranking rewards monthly, while his sixteen thousand charges alone represented a large amount of accumulated return power.
Yet the System wasn’t merely asking for everything he currently possessed.
It was taking future claims in advance.
The System immediately noticed his reaction.
[Sigh.]
[Luke, do you seriously not understand what you’re buying?]
Luke stared at the screen.
[Fine, let me explain something first.]
[Do you know what happened to the other Heroes after receiving both their patron god’s blessing and Valtharion’s blessing?]
Luke thought about it for several seconds before shaking his head.
He knew those Heroes had experienced frightening growth soon after being summoned, but he had never known exactly what had caused it.
The System answered.
[When their respective gods bless their chosen Heroes, those Heroes generally receive an SSS-Rank Skill.]
Luke’s expression changed slightly.
[Then Valtharion’s blessing grants another evolution.]
[A Divine-Rank Origin Skill.]
Luke immediately sat straighter.
The System continued.
[An Origin Skill of that level is essentially a direct road toward godhood, provided the Hero survives, continues cultivating, and doesn’t become lazy halfway through.]
“What the fuck?!”
Luke couldn’t stop himself from cursing.
Those people hadn’t merely received good talent.
They had effectively entered Valtharion with god-level foundations already prepared for them.
No wonder some Heroes had already climbed into B-Rank despite arriving only shortly before him.
[Yup.]
The System seemed strangely pleased by his reaction.
[So understand this properly.]
[The technique I’m offering doesn’t merely save you several billion years of learning.]
[Its rank is also above Divine.]
The four Titan spirits immediately became serious.
Luke stared at the screen as the next words slowly appeared.
[EX-RANK.]
[Classification: Eternal Rank.]
[The same rank at which your Titan once existed.]
The bathhouse became silent again.
This time, even Nyx and the others didn’t immediately react.
An EX-Rank technique wasn’t merely another powerful treasure.
According to the laws they understood, something at the Eternal level wasn’t supposed to be casually manufactured, distributed, or even obtained simply because someone was powerful enough.
Eternal existence itself was connected directly to the authority of the universe.
If the universe did not permit an existence to cross that boundary, then simply possessing strength wasn’t enough to force the transition.
That was also one of the reasons Nyx, Caelith, Myrkhal, and Sevaroth had been imprisoned rather than killed.
Their enemies couldn’t truly erase them.
An Eternal existence had already become inseparable from the aspect it represented.

If an Eternal being represented Fire, then as long as fire still existed somewhere within that universe, even if it were only a single spark burning in some forgotten corner of reality, that connection could eventually allow the Eternal being to return at full power.
That was what Eternal meant.
Not simply longevity.
Existential persistence.
Sevaroth finally understood why the System had sounded so confident.
“No wonder...”
Everyone turned toward him.
“No wonder this technique can perform those Reformations automatically.”
Sevaroth looked toward the System screen.

“A method capable of simultaneously controlling several Forbidden principles, rewriting them into one body, maintaining stability between them, and repeating the process across every realm shouldn’t be possible through an ordinary cultivation technique.”
His voice became more serious.
“Only something standing at the Eternal grade could handle that level of contradiction without collapsing.”
The System immediately displayed another smug message.
[Exactly.]
[With this technique, not only will your cultivation become drastically faster, but your path will no longer possess a normal breakthrough ceiling.]
Luke stared at the message.
[As long as you continue fulfilling its cultivation requirements and survive your breakthroughs, the technique itself possesses a complete path to Eternal Rank.]
Luke’s expression slowly changed.
The System wasn’t finished.
[And you won’t become an ordinary Eternal.]
[Because this technique will use the cultivation path your Titans just designed.]
[Every Forbidden Titan bloodline you possess will be rewritten into the same evolving lineage.]
[Every future Titan will contribute to that lineage.]
[Every realm will reconstruct your entire Titan body around the combined result.]
The next message remained on the screen for several seconds.
[If you truly reach the end of this path...]
[What is born may become something even entire universes would fear.]
No one laughed this time.
Even Myrkhal had become quiet.
Luke slowly looked from the System screen toward the four Titan spirits, then back again.
Finally, one last panel appeared.
“THE ETERNAL ORIGIN ZERO”
Rank: EX
Classification: Eternal Cultivation Technique
Path: Unknown Titan Genesis
Status: Available for Purchase
[Would you like to purchase...]
“The Eternal Origin Zero”?
And if you wants to see the Images of Character and Cover Images.

chapters.title: Chapter 360: Why Is There No Information About the Dragon Emperor’s Wife?!
paragraphs: [So, would you like to purchase...]
"The Eternal Origin Zero"
[Yes] or [No]
Luke stared at the notification for several moments before finally raising his hand beneath the watchful gazes of the Titan spirits and pressing the option.
[Yes]
[Congratulations, Luke! You have obtained your first EX-Rank item!]
"Okay, that was easier than expected."
Luke muttered before smiling toward the others, and the four Titan spirits also relaxed slightly after seeing the purchase go through without anything strange happening.
A moment later, information concerning "The Eternal Origin Zero" began flowing into Luke’s mind, giving him a basic understanding of how the technique worked.
The requirement was surprisingly straightforward compared with everything the Titans had explained earlier.

Luke simply had to continue hunting beings, gather their bloodline essence, and cultivate, while the technique itself would automatically carry out the complicated internal processes of purification, engraving, reconstruction, and refinement with only minimal pain involved.
"Great."
With the matter finally settled, Luke climbed out of the bath before taking out a set of magical clothes.

The fabric immediately shifted around his body, transforming into a black shirt and matching black pants, while a brown leather belt formed around his waist. Luke rolled his sleeves up toward his elbows and left the upper button of his shirt undone, making the outfit more comfortable before finally turning toward the exit.
"Let’s start this new journey."
Luke calmly walked out of the bathhouse, where two maids dressed in proper maid uniforms were already waiting outside.
Unlike the half-dragons he had seen earlier, neither woman possessed any visible draconic features.
’A dragon?’
That was the first thought that came to Luke’s mind, because unlike half-dragons, true dragons were capable of completely hiding their racial characteristics while maintaining humanoid form.
"Sir, the Princess is waiting for you. Please follow us."
Both maids bowed politely, and Luke gave a small nod before following them through the palace.

The hallways were absurdly large, with ceilings and passages wide enough that even a dragon could move through them without much difficulty, which only made Luke more aware that this place had never been designed according to human proportions.

In this section of the palace, only a few maids and butlers could be seen moving around, each dressed professionally and quietly attending to their duties while Luke continued following the two women.

After nearly five minutes of walking, they finally stopped before another grand chamber whose entrance rose hundreds of meters into the air, making Luke appear almost insignificant when standing before it.
’Damn... everything here is huge. It feels like I’m walking through a palace built for giants.’
Luke clicked his tongue in amusement before nodding toward the two maids, who bowed once more and quietly left him there.
Two female guards stood beside the gate.

Unlike the armored knights Luke was accustomed to seeing throughout the Human Continent, neither woman wore armor, and both were dressed rather simply, making them appear almost ordinary at first glance.
The two guards briefly examined Luke before one of them turned toward the closed gate and called loudly.
"My Lady, the guest has arrived!"
For several moments, nothing happened, yet the guards remained completely still until a gentle female voice eventually came from somewhere beyond the gate.
"Let him in."
"Yes, My Lady.
With that, both guards stepped toward the center of the entrance and placed one hand against their respective halves of the gigantic gate.
"Humph!"
Rrrrrmm...
The gate resisted for a brief moment before slowly beginning to move under their strength.
Skrrrrrr...
Its lower edge scraped across the floor as both sides gradually opened, until they finally struck the inner walls with a heavy impact.
BOOM!
Luke remained completely silent.
The sound itself wasn’t what surprised him.
The instant the two guards had exerted their strength, Luke had briefly sensed the power hidden inside their bodies.
’A-Rank...’
His expression became strange.
’A freaking A-Rank... working as a gate guard?’

For a moment, Luke genuinely felt as though his understanding of power had been turned upside down, because on the Human Continent, an A-Rank existence stood just below the King Tier and possessed enough strength to threaten entire kingdoms.
Yet here, two of them were simply standing beside a gate.
"Sir?"
One of the guards finally called to him after noticing that he had stopped moving.
Luke returned to his senses and gave a small nod.
"Yeah."
He silently accepted another reality of the Dragon Continent.

Dragons naturally possessed extremely long lifespans and continued becoming stronger over time, while unlike many ordinary races, they didn’t suffer from the same harsh realm barriers that stopped others from advancing.
’It’s really good to be a dragon...’
Luke paused.
’Wait, I don’t have realm barriers anymore either because of my new technique.’
That thought immediately improved his mood.
’Just wait. I’ll leave all of you behind soon enough.’
STEP.
Luke crossed the threshold, and the gigantic doors behind him began closing once again.
BOOM!
Luke glanced backward.
’Does nobody here care about noise pollution?’
Choosing to ignore that question, he finally turned toward the interior.
"Hmmm... okay, now this is getting out of hand."
Luke wasn’t standing inside a normal chamber.
He was standing inside another world.

Mountains rose in the distance, wide bodies of water stretched across the land, and even a sun and moon hung high above the artificial sky, making it difficult to believe that all of this existed behind a pair of palace doors.
Luke slowly looked around, taking in trees that rose hundreds of meters into the air, while some stretched even higher and reached thousands of meters toward the false heavens.
For a moment, he genuinely felt as though he had left Valtharion and entered an entirely different world.
"So, do you like it?"
A gentle voice suddenly came from beside him.
Luke turned and found Emberlyn standing there as casually as though the two of them had known each other for years.
"Don’t know."
Luke didn’t praise the place and simply gave the first answer that came to mind, which caused Emberlyn to smile slightly.
"Our Grandma has created this."
Luke’s expression changed again.

He had been hearing about this mysterious grandmother repeatedly ever since arriving on the Dragon Continent, and surprisingly, she was also the reason Rhaenyra had brought him here in the first place.
Yet Luke still knew almost nothing about her.

From the information his clones had gathered in the Human Capital before he was brought here, Luke knew that the father of the current Dragon King was the Dragon Emperor, a demi-god whose reputation extended across Valtharion.
More importantly, the Dragon Emperor officially held the title of the strongest known demi-god in the entire world.

There were even rumors claiming that gods descending through Apostles would struggle to defeat him, while his achievements during the Demon War included personally killing several Demon Emperors and building a terrifying reputation throughout that era.
’No wonder demons don’t casually come here.’
Luke immediately understood why the Dragon Continent remained relatively untouched by demonic forces.
’With someone like that sitting here all this time, invading this continent would practically be suicide.’
However, one detail still bothered him.
Despite everything his clones had learned about the Dragon Emperor, Luke had never found any meaningful information concerning the Dragon Emperor’s wife.
It was almost as though anything related to her had either been hidden extremely well or deliberately erased.
Noticing that Luke had once again fallen into thought, Emberlyn smiled faintly before gesturing for him to follow.
"Let’s go. Elder Sister and Grandma are waiting for you."

Luke stared at the notification for several moments before finally raising his hand beneath the watchful gazes of the Titan spirits and pressing the option.

You have obtained your first EX-Rank item!]
"Okay, that was easier than expected."

The requirement was surprisingly straightforward compared with everything the Titans had explained earlier.

Luke simply had to continue hunting beings, gather their bloodline essence, and cultivate, while the technique itself would automatically carry out the complicated internal processes of purification, engraving, reconstruction, and refinement with only minimal pain involved.
"Great."
With the matter finally settled, Luke climbed out of the bath before taking out a set of magical clothes.
The fabric immediately shifted around his body, transforming into a black shirt and matching black pants, while a brown leather belt formed around his waist.
Luke rolled his sleeves up toward his elbows and left the upper button of his shirt undone, making the outfit more comfortable before finally turning toward the exit.
"Let’s start this new journey."
Luke calmly walked out of the bathhouse, where two maids dressed in proper maid uniforms were already waiting outside.
Unlike the half-dragons he had seen earlier, neither woman possessed any visible draconic features.
’A dragon?’
That was the first thought that came to Luke’s mind, because unlike half-dragons, true dragons were capable of completely hiding their racial characteristics while maintaining humanoid form.
"Sir, the Princess is waiting for you.
Please follow us."
Both maids bowed politely, and Luke gave a small nod before following them through the palace.

The hallways were absurdly large, with ceilings and passages wide enough that even a dragon could move through them without much difficulty, which only made Luke more aware that this place had never been designed according to human proportions.

In this section of the palace, only a few maids and butlers could be seen moving around, each dressed professionally and quietly attending to their duties while Luke continued following the two women.

After nearly five minutes of walking, they finally stopped before another grand chamber whose entrance rose hundreds of meters into the air, making Luke appear almost insignificant when standing before it.
’Damn... everything here is huge.
It feels like I’m walking through a palace built for giants.’
Luke clicked his tongue in amusement before nodding toward the two maids, who bowed once more and quietly left him there.
Two female guards stood beside the gate.

Unlike the armored knights Luke was accustomed to seeing throughout the Human Continent, neither woman wore armor, and both were dressed rather simply, making them appear almost ordinary at first glance.

"My Lady, the guest has arrived!"
For several moments, nothing happened, yet the guards remained completely still until a gentle female voice eventually came from somewhere beyond the gate.
"Let him in."
"Yes, My Lady.
With that, both guards stepped toward the center of the entrance and placed one hand against their respective halves of the gigantic gate.
"Humph!"
Rrrrrmm...
The gate resisted for a brief moment before slowly beginning to move under their strength.
Skrrrrrr...
Its lower edge scraped across the floor as both sides gradually opened, until they finally struck the inner walls with a heavy impact.
BOOM!
Luke remained completely silent.
The sound itself wasn’t what surprised him.
The instant the two guards had exerted their strength, Luke had briefly sensed the power hidden inside their bodies.
’A-Rank...’
His expression became strange.
’A freaking A-Rank... working as a gate guard?’

For a moment, Luke genuinely felt as though his understanding of power had been turned upside down, because on the Human Continent, an A-Rank existence stood just below the King Tier and possessed enough strength to threaten entire kingdoms.
Yet here, two of them were simply standing beside a gate.
"Sir?"
One of the guards finally called to him after noticing that he had stopped moving.
Luke returned to his senses and gave a small nod.
"Yeah."
He silently accepted another reality of the Dragon Continent.

Dragons naturally possessed extremely long lifespans and continued becoming stronger over time, while unlike many ordinary races, they didn’t suffer from the same harsh realm barriers that stopped others from advancing.
’It’s really good to be a dragon...’

’Wait, I don’t have realm barriers anymore either because of my new technique.’
That thought immediately improved his mood.
’Just wait.
I’ll leave all of you behind soon enough.’

BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 361: “Isn’t This My Cute Grandson-in-Law~?”
paragraphs: With those words, her feet quietly left the ground as she began floating upward without any visible spell formation or noticeable release of energy.
Luke’s mouth twitched slightly when he noticed that.
’Great... so she’s A-Rank too, and I still had the courage to flirt with her earlier.’
He immediately decided not to think too much about what had happened inside the bathhouse, silently hoping Emberlyn wasn’t the kind of person who would hold a grudge over something that small.
Still, another thought crossed Luke’s mind.

For some reason, whenever he interacted with women who weren’t his wives, he usually ended up becoming far more confident and dominant in the conversation without even trying, while the moment one of his actual wives appeared, that confidence had a strange habit of disappearing.
"Okay."
Luke muttered before calling upon the wings of his Winged Titan, and with a strong flap, his body rose into the air beside Emberlyn.
’I need to improve my control over Force.’

If he could manipulate it precisely enough, Luke believed he should eventually be capable of flying without relying on Vorthar’s titan form, although reaching that level of control would require considerably more practice.
The two continued flying through the artificial world for several minutes before eventually reaching a lake so wide that calling it a small ocean wouldn’t have been much of an exaggeration.
As they began descending, Emberlyn glanced toward Luke before speaking in a quieter voice.
"Remember, Grandma is very sweet and kind, but don’t provoke her or make her angry."
Luke immediately nodded.
He had absolutely no intention of deliberately provoking an unknown high-ranking existence, especially after everything he had already learned about the dragons living here.
Once they landed beside the lake, Luke finally saw two figures waiting near the water.
One was Rhaenyra.

The other was a young woman who appeared to be around twenty years old, whose long hair flowed behind her in shimmering strands of white and sapphire, looking as though moonlight and blue crystal had been woven together, while two elegant horns rose from above her head.
At that moment, however, the beautiful young woman was casually pinching both of Rhaenyra’s cheeks.
Luke stared at the scene for several seconds, then leaned slightly toward Emberlyn.
"Where’s your grandma?"
Emberlyn became speechless for a moment.

Only then did she remember that, by human standards, the words grandmother and grandfather normally brought to mind elderly people with obvious signs of age, because humans possessed comparatively short lifespans and even powerful cultivators often carried some visible trace of the years they had lived.
Without saying anything else, Emberlyn raised one hand and pointed toward the young woman currently pinching Rhaenyra’s cheeks.
"She’s our grandma."
"O_O"
Luke’s mouth slowly opened.
For several seconds, he genuinely wondered whether Emberlyn was joking, because telling him that a woman who looked barely older than twenty was someone’s grandmother sounded completely absurd.
Emberlyn ignored his stunned expression and calmly introduced her.
"She is Zephyrielle Arkanthyr... Dragon of the Stillness Beyond Time."
Luke silently repeated the title in his mind.
’Dragon of the Stillness Beyond Time...’
Even without knowing what her power actually did, the title alone sounded ridiculously grand.
At that exact moment, Caelith’s voice came from within him.
"Luke, she’s a demi-god."
Luke nearly cursed aloud.
’Damn, another demi-god? And with a title like that?’
Fortunately, he managed to stop himself before anything escaped his mouth, because Zephyrielle chose that exact moment to release Rhaenyra’s cheeks and turn toward the newcomers.
Rhaenyra also looked over.
The moment she saw Luke, however, her expression barely changed, as though whether he was standing there or not made little difference to her.
[It seems you still have a lot of work to do, Luke.]
The System immediately commented after noticing Rhaenyra’s reaction.
Luke ignored it.
At the moment, increasing his cultivation mattered considerably more than worrying about whether Rhaenyra acknowledged him as her husband.
Zephyrielle, on the other hand, reacted very differently.
"Ohhh~ Isn’t this my cute and handsome grandson-in-law~?"
Before Luke could properly understand what was happening, Zephyrielle disappeared from beside Rhaenyra and appeared directly in front of him.
Luke instinctively stiffened, but by then, both of her hands had already reached his face.
"What a cutiepie~"
She immediately began pinching his cheeks.
Emberlyn giggled quietly from the side, clearly familiar with this behavior from her grandmother.

Luke, meanwhile, became increasingly embarrassed and tried pulling his head backward, only to discover that he couldn’t move his face out of Zephyrielle’s hands at all, as though all the strength inside his body had suddenly become meaningless.
More unsettling than that, however, was the strange sensation that appeared while Zephyrielle continued smiling at him.
Luke felt exposed.
Not physically, but in a way that made it seem as though everything hidden inside his body had already been laid bare before her gaze.
’Damn... is this what those protagonists feel like when they meet some mysterious old monster who can see through everything with one look?’
Zephyrielle didn’t say anything, but Luke’s instinct wasn’t wrong.
With nothing more than a glance, she had already realized that the being standing before her was no longer human.
That discovery immediately confused her, because everything surrounding Luke’s arrival in Valtharion indicated that he had entered this world as a human.
So Zephyrielle silently asked the stars.
The answer she received confirmed exactly that.
Luke had arrived in Valtharion as a human, yet sometime afterward, his existence had changed into an entirely different species.
’Interesting.’
Zephyrielle’s smile widened slightly as she finally released Luke’s cheeks.
"What a cute grandson-in-law I’ve gotten."
She gently patted Luke’s head before disappearing from his side and reappearing beside Emberlyn.
"Ohhh~ Only my dear Emberlyn is left."
Without warning, Zephyrielle began pinching Emberlyn’s cheeks as well.
"When are you going to find another grandson-in-law for me?"
Unlike Luke, Emberlyn barely reacted, maintaining an almost completely normal expression as though years of experience had already made her immune to her grandmother’s habit of pinching her cheeks.
Zephyrielle clicked her tongue.
"Tch. If you keep acting like that, how is any man supposed to like you?"
This time, Emberlyn’s calm expression finally cracked slightly, and the corner of her mouth twitched.
Apparently, even she wasn’t completely immune when her grandmother started bringing up marriage.
After teasing Emberlyn for another few moments, Zephyrielle eventually returned to Rhaenyra’s side before turning toward Luke once again.
"Alright, I only wanted to meet my grandson-in-law, and now that I’ve done that, I should probably leave."
She smiled warmly, although before leaving, she seemed to remember something else.
"My useless son gave poor Rhaenyra some troublesome work and made her manage this useless territory for an entire year, so help your wife while you’re here, alright?"
Zephyrielle tilted her head slightly while smiling toward Luke.
Luke immediately nodded.
He didn’t dare refuse.
Rhaenyra’s expression, however, became visibly uglier after hearing her grandmother casually assign Luke to help her, although she merely showed her irritation and didn’t openly argue.
"Good."
Zephyrielle smiled one final time before disappearing without warning.
The lakeside immediately became much quieter.

Left behind were Luke, the Hero of Light, Emberlyn silently observing from nearby, and Rhaenyra, the wife who still refused to acknowledge Luke as her husband and was now staring directly at him with an expression that suggested she had already forgotten everything her grandmother had just said.
Luke stared back at her.
Emberlyn remained silent, clearly waiting to see what would happen next.
So now...
What exactly was Luke supposed to do?

chapters.title: Chapter 362: Normal, Legendary, Forbidden... and Eternal Titan Zero! Foundation!
paragraphs: After Zephyrielle left, Rhaenyra remained silent for a moment before slowly walking toward Luke.
STEP.
Once she reached him, she stopped directly in front of him and looked straight into his eyes.
"Forget my grandma’s words. I can deal with my own problems."
Luke listened without showing much reaction before giving a simple nod.
"Well, I don’t even have time to deal with that, because I have my own problems to handle."

Rhaenyra’s expression shifted slightly, clearly not expecting that answer, yet before she could say anything else, Luke had already moved past her and started heading toward the exit of the artificial world.
’He didn’t pester me or complain?’

Rhaenyra watched his retreating back with growing confusion, because she had expected him to once again insist that she was his wife and shouldn’t speak to him that way, which was the kind of behavior she associated with humans and their strange attachment to marriage.
She had even expected Luke to ask her for resources so he could increase his realm faster, especially after everything that had happened between them, yet he hadn’t asked for anything at all.
"Let’s go, Emberlyn."
Luke spoke without turning around as the wings of his Winged Titan emerged from his back, and with a strong flap, he rose into the air.
Emberlyn looked toward him for a moment, then quietly followed without questioning where he intended to go, leaving Rhaenyra standing behind them.
"...Why is my sister listening to him?"
Rhaenyra muttered in confusion as she watched the two disappear into the distance, genuinely unable to understand what had happened between them during the short time she hadn’t been around.
"Ahh, whatever!"
She quickly pushed the matter aside and left as well, because she still had to deal with the Orcs that had invaded this region.

Outside the artificial world, Luke and Emberlyn walked through the dense forest, where towering trees stretched far above them while insects moved through the undergrowth and small docile beasts occasionally wandered between the thick roots.
Emberlyn remained quiet while walking beside Luke, although one question continued bothering her.
’Why did I agree to follow him so easily?’
After thinking about it for a while, one possibility came to mind.
’Maybe I just want to see something new.’

Ever since staying on the Dragon Continent, where she wasn’t allowed to casually leave, most of Emberlyn’s entertainment had come from spending time with her elder sister or other members of the family, so following Luke around was at least something different from her usual routine.
Luke, meanwhile, wasn’t thinking about anything nearly as casual.
His cultivation had already become his highest priority, and after obtaining "The Eternal Origin Zero", there was one question he needed answered before deciding what to do next.
’How many ranked beings do I actually have to kill?’
That was the important part.

If he needed Blood Essence to cultivate, then he needed prey, but knowing exactly how much essence his new body required would determine whether he needed to hunt a few powerful beings or slaughter entire armies.
’System, tell me.’
The familiar blue screen immediately appeared before him.
[Here is the calculated number of beings required for you to reach C-Rank.]
The moment the System responded, Nyx, Caelith, Myrkhal, and Sevaroth also materialized around Luke, clearly curious about the requirements of the Eternal-Rank technique.
’Alright.’
Luke continued walking while reading through the long panel that unfolded before him.
[BLOOD ESSENCE REQUIREMENT CALCULATION]
Current Realm: D-Rank
Target Realm: C-Rank
"The Eternal Origin Zero" has calculated several possible Blood Essence requirements based on the quality and scale of the Titan body being constructed.
[OPTION I — HIGH REQUIREMENT]
Equivalent Blood Essence Required:
B-Rank → 1,000
A-Rank → 100
S-Rank → 10
SS-Rank → 1
Any mixture of Blood Essence may be used as long as the required total equivalent is reached.
[OPTION II — LEGENDARY TITAN LEVEL]
Equivalent Blood Essence Required:
B-Rank → 5,000
A-Rank → 500
S-Rank → 50
SS-Rank → 5
SSS-Rank → 1
This amount is sufficient to reconstruct a body approaching the biological standard of a Legendary Titan.
[OPTION III — FORBIDDEN TITAN LEVEL]
Equivalent Blood Essence Required:
A-Rank → 1,000
S-Rank → 100
SS-Rank → 10
SSS-Rank → 1
Conversion Ratio:
1 SSS-Rank
= 10 SS-Rank
= 100 S-Rank
= 1,000 A-Rank
This requirement corresponds to the reconstruction of a Forbidden Titan-class body.
[OPTION IV — ETERNAL TITAN ZERO]
Equivalent Blood Essence Required:
A-Rank → 2,000
S-Rank → 200
SS-Rank → 20
SSS-Rank → 2
This requirement corresponds to the construction of an Eternal Titan Zero-class foundation.
[NOTICE]
Blood Essence from different realms may be combined.
Example:
D-Rank Blood Essence
C-Rank Blood Essence
B-Rank Blood Essence
A-Rank Blood Essence
can collectively fulfill the same breakthrough requirement.
Only Blood Essence obtained from D-Rank beings or higher can be absorbed by the current cultivation process.
Luke continued staring at the panel for several seconds, and the deeper he went through the numbers, the stranger his expression became.
’System... are you kidding me?’

Even the four Titan spirits appeared somewhat surprised by the sheer amount of Blood Essence required for someone still in D-Rank, although the numbers became considerably more manageable if Luke hunted beings above his own realm.
The System naturally noticed their reaction.
[Luke, creating a higher-grade Titan body isn’t a joke, because the quality of the body directly determines the benefits you receive from it.]

[Look at your own Titans. Their Forbidden-class bodies possess ridiculous compression and compatibility with their respective Authorities, which is one of the reasons they can naturally comprehend and control their elements far more easily than ordinary beings.]
Luke understood the logic, although understanding it didn’t make the numbers look any less ridiculous.
[That’s why I’m giving you several choices. If you don’t want to pursue the highest possible foundation, you can simply choose Option I and construct that level of body instead.]
The System paused briefly before another message appeared.
[However, if you choose Option IV and construct an Eternal Titan Zero body, then yes, the requirement is extremely high, but the benefits will be equally ridiculous.]
Luke’s attention immediately returned to the panel.
[You won’t see the true result until you successfully enter C-Rank, but I guarantee that you won’t be disappointed.]
[For example, if you reach C-Rank using Option IV, then attacks originating from D-Rank will become completely ineffective against your body.]
Luke slowed slightly.
The System continued.

[It doesn’t matter whether that D-Rank attack contains Divinity, Forbidden power, an Authority, or some other extraordinary property. As long as the attack itself remains at D-Rank, your Eternal Titan Zero body will be immune to it.]
[Even if billions of D-Rank beings attacked you simultaneously, they wouldn’t be able to move your body, much less leave a scratch.]
Luke stopped paying attention to the surrounding forest for a moment, while the four Titan spirits also became noticeably more serious after reading that claim.

The concept that enough weaker beings could eventually overwhelm someone stronger existed throughout Valtharion just as it did anywhere else, although there were obviously limits depending on the difference in realm.

An infinite number of mortals couldn’t simply kill a god, but when the difference narrowed enough, overwhelming numbers could still become dangerous, and there were even theories that sufficiently large numbers of demi-gods could bring down a genuine god.
’But if I build that body, then anything below my realm becomes completely irrelevant.’
Anticipation immediately appeared within Luke.

He already possessed several methods suited for fighting large numbers of enemies, especially through his Titans and their Forbidden powers, so armies had never been his greatest concern, yet there was still a difference between being powerful against numbers and becoming completely immune to them.
’What if an entire world ambushed me someday, though? What if billions of beings from my own realm attacked at the same time?’
Luke’s expression became slightly ugly when he imagined that possibility, because despite everything he possessed, he knew exactly what the answer would currently be.
He would lose.
Luke was strong for his realm and possessed abilities that broke ordinary logic, but he was nowhere near truly invincible, and that was a title very few beings could ever claim.
If "The Eternal Origin Zero" could eventually erase even that weakness, then the absurd requirements of Option IV suddenly didn’t seem quite as unreasonable.

Meanwhile, the four Titan spirits exchanged glances, because even at their former Eternal Rank, their bodies could still be damaged by beings capable of reaching them, despite each of them possessing a Forbidden Titan physique.

Their bodies had been extraordinarily powerful, but those physiques had never granted them absolute immunity against attacks from beings below their realm, while this so-called Eternal Titan Zero body was apparently capable of doing exactly that.
As for what kind of logic allowed such a body to exist, even they didn’t know.
’Fine.’
Luke continued walking through the forest before finally making his decision.
’I am choosing Option Four.’

STEP.
Once she reached him, she stopped directly in front of him and looked straight into his eyes.
"Forget my grandma’s words.
I can deal with my own problems."
Luke listened without showing much reaction before giving a simple nod.
"Well, I don’t even have time to deal with that, because I have my own problems to handle."

Rhaenyra’s expression shifted slightly, clearly not expecting that answer, yet before she could say anything else, Luke had already moved past her and started heading toward the exit of the artificial world.
’He didn’t pester me or complain?’

Rhaenyra watched his retreating back with growing confusion, because she had expected him to once again insist that she was his wife and shouldn’t speak to him that way, which was the kind of behavior she associated with humans and their strange attachment to marriage.
She had even expected Luke to ask her for resources so he could increase his realm faster, especially after everything that had happened between them, yet he hadn’t asked for anything at all.
"Let’s go, Emberlyn."
Luke spoke without turning around as the wings of his Winged Titan emerged from his back, and with a strong flap, he rose into the air.
Emberlyn looked toward him for a moment, then quietly followed without questioning where he intended to go, leaving Rhaenyra standing behind them.
"...Why is my sister listening to him?"
Rhaenyra muttered in confusion as she watched the two disappear into the distance, genuinely unable to understand what had happened between them during the short time she hadn’t been around.
"Ahh, whatever!"
She quickly pushed the matter aside and left as well, because she still had to deal with the Orcs that had invaded this region.

Outside the artificial world, Luke and Emberlyn walked through the dense forest, where towering trees stretched far above them while insects moved through the undergrowth and small docile beasts occasionally wandered between the thick roots.
Emberlyn remained quiet while walking beside Luke, although one question continued bothering her.
’Why did I agree to follow him so easily?’
After thinking about it for a while, one possibility came to mind.
’Maybe I just want to see something new.’

Ever since staying on the Dragon Continent, where she wasn’t allowed to casually leave, most of Emberlyn’s entertainment had come from spending time with her elder sister or other members of the family, so following Luke around was at least something different from her usual routine.
Luke, meanwhile, wasn’t thinking about anything nearly as casual.
His cultivation had already become his highest priority, and after obtaining "The Eternal Origin Zero", there was one question he needed answered before deciding what to do next.
’How many ranked beings do I actually have to kill?’
That was the important part.

If he needed Blood Essence to cultivate, then he needed prey, but knowing exactly how much essence his new body required would determine whether he needed to hunt a few powerful beings or slaughter entire armies.
’System, tell me.’
The familiar blue screen immediately appeared before him.
[Here is the calculated number of beings required for you to reach C-Rank.]
The moment the System responded, Nyx, Caelith, Myrkhal, and Sevaroth also materialized around Luke, clearly curious about the requirements of the Eternal-Rank technique.
’Alright.’
Luke continued walking while reading through the long panel that unfolded before him.
[BLOOD ESSENCE REQUIREMENT CALCULATION]
Current Realm: D-Rank
Target Realm: C-Rank

[OPTION I — HIGH REQUIREMENT]
Equivalent Blood Essence Required:
B-Rank → 1,000
A-Rank → 100
S-Rank → 10
SS-Rank → 1
Any mixture of Blood Essence may be used as long as the required total equivalent is reached.
[OPTION II — LEGENDARY TITAN LEVEL]
Equivalent Blood Essence Required:
B-Rank → 5,000
A-Rank → 500
S-Rank → 50
SS-Rank → 5
SSS-Rank → 1
This amount is sufficient to reconstruct a body approaching the biological standard of a Legendary Titan.
[OPTION III — FORBIDDEN TITAN LEVEL]
Equivalent Blood Essence Required:
A-Rank → 1,000
S-Rank → 100
SS-Rank → 10
SSS-Rank → 1
Conversion Ratio:
1 SSS-Rank
= 10 SS-Rank
= 100 S-Rank
= 1,000 A-Rank
This requirement corresponds to the reconstruction of a Forbidden Titan-class body.
[OPTION IV — ETERNAL TITAN ZERO]
Equivalent Blood Essence Required:
A-Rank → 2,000
S-Rank → 200
SS-Rank → 20
SSS-Rank → 2
This requirement corresponds to the construction of an Eternal Titan Zero-class foundation.

Blood Essence from different realms may be combined.
Example:
D-Rank Blood Essence
C-Rank Blood Essence
B-Rank Blood Essence
A-Rank Blood Essence
can collectively fulfill the same breakthrough requirement.
Only Blood Essence obtained from D-Rank beings or higher can be absorbed by the current cultivation process.

chapters.title: Chapter 363: The Eternal Origin Zero Extracts an Entire Existence?!
paragraphs: If he was already going to rebuild his entire existence through "The Eternal Origin Zero", then there was little reason to settle for an inferior foundation merely because the requirement was difficult.
However, just as Luke made his decision, the System’s tone suddenly changed.
[Sigh... unfortunately, there is one more condition.]
Luke immediately became suspicious.
[This technique requires you to personally hunt the beings whose essence you absorb, because calling it Blood Essence is actually an oversimplification.]

[Once you personally kill a suitable target, "The Eternal Origin Zero" doesn’t merely absorb its bloodline essence; your body extracts everything useful from that existence, including its soul, spirit, mind, karma, destiny, and other aspects connected to its existence.]
Luke’s expression changed slightly after reading that.
[That’s why you must personally hunt them.]
[Otherwise, you could simply find yourself a sugar mommy and ask her to bring you an SSS-Rank corpse to absorb.]
Luke completely ignored the sugar mommy comment, although he didn’t particularly mind the requirement itself.
Hunting the targets personally would allow him to accumulate combat experience while cultivating, and more importantly, Luke had never liked depending entirely upon someone else for his own growth.
With that settled, he turned slightly toward Emberlyn, who was walking beside him with her usual calm expression.
"You said earlier that your father ordered Rhaenyra to protect this territory for one year, right?"
Emberlyn came out of her thoughts and glanced toward him.
"Yes, and she also has to eliminate the invading forces occupying this region."
"Invading forces?"
Luke looked genuinely confused.
He couldn’t immediately understand what kind of species would have enough courage to invade the Dragon Continent, especially after learning just how powerful some of the beings living here were.
Noticing his confusion, Emberlyn explained.

"The Dragon Continent is connected to many islands and surrounding regions where different species and tribes live, and many of them know very little about the civilizations outside their own territories, so we generally call them barbarian tribes."
Luke listened while continuing through the forest.

"Since those tribes aren’t powerful enough to threaten the Dragon Continent as a whole, the elders usually allow the younger generation to deal with them, which gives young dragons actual combat experience without placing them in excessive danger."
Luke nodded after hearing that.
It made sense.
Emberlyn continued, "There’s another reason as well. Among the major continents, the Dragon Continent is second only to the Demon Continent in how closely parts of it border the Endless Forest."
"So species from the Endless Forest occasionally emerge and attempt to occupy nearby regions of the Dragon Continent whenever they find an opportunity."
Luke raised an eyebrow slightly.

"The elders still don’t explore too deeply into the Endless Forest, but most tribes that come out aren’t particularly powerful and usually don’t possess any demi-gods, so they’re treated as another form of training for the younger generation."
Emberlyn paused briefly before adding, "And whatever resources those tribes possess can naturally be taken by whoever defeats them, provided they have enough strength to claim them."
"Ohh, I understand."
Luke finally understood why Rhaenyra had been assigned to this territory.
Her task wasn’t merely to defend the region whenever something attacked; she was also expected to locate the invading forces already occupying parts of the land and remove their established bases.
Luke looked around at the dense forest surrounding them, where the trunks of the gigantic trees stretched upward until much of their upper canopy disappeared from sight.
Considering the size of the Dragon Continent, even this single territory could cover an absurd amount of land, which meant searching blindly for hidden enemy bases would be extremely inefficient.
"So, do you know where any of those outposts are?"
Emberlyn nodded almost immediately.
"A tribe of Orcs recently emerged from the Endless Forest and started occupying several nearby areas, and I found one of their outposts while exploring during my free time.
Luke’s expression immediately brightened.
"Perfect. Take me there."
Emberlyn gestured for him to follow, and before long, the two disappeared deeper into the forest.
Some time later, Luke and Emberlyn sat upon a thick branch high above the ground, looking down through the leaves toward an Orc encampment hidden between the gigantic trees.

Nearly everything inside the camp had been designed to blend with the forest, with tents, cloth coverings, wooden structures, and even parts of their equipment dyed in different shades of green, making the settlement considerably harder to notice from a distance.

The outpost was also heavily fortified despite the lack of metal walls, because thick earthen barriers nearly fifty feet high surrounded the entire settlement, although compared with the trees towering around them, even those walls appeared strangely small.
Luke carefully observed the movement inside the camp before his attention settled upon a particularly noticeable Orc.

The creature stood nearly ten feet tall with dark green skin and carried a long staff in one hand, while shells, carved stones, bones, small skulls, and various strange ornaments covered much of his body.
"Is that a shaman?"
"Yes."
Emberlyn glanced toward Luke with faint surprise, apparently wondering how he had recognized the Orc’s role so quickly.
Luke’s mouth twitched slightly.
’Why do these Orcs look almost exactly like the ones from novels and comics?’
He didn’t waste much time thinking about it, however, because his attention quickly shifted toward something far more important.
Their numbers.
[ORC OUTPOST 1]
Total Population: ~50,000 Orcs
Highest Realm: B-Rank
Power Distribution:
B-Rank → 1
C-Rank → 80
D-Rank → 8,000
Below D-Rank → 41,919
Total → 50,000
"Hmm... only one B-Rank."
Luke rubbed his chin thoughtfully and he felt the different aura of each being.

The outpost was almost perfect for his current situation, because although its population was large enough to provide a meaningful amount of Blood Essence, the strongest individual present was still within a range, that he could handle.
More importantly, fighting through the outpost would allow him to sharpen his combat experience instead of simply relying upon the overwhelming abilities granted by his Titans.
Nyx, Caelith, Myrkhal, and Sevaroth floated nearby without interfering, because they had already decided to let Luke determine how he wanted to proceed.

Emberlyn behaved similarly, settling more comfortably upon the thick branch while watching the camp below with mild curiosity, clearly interested in seeing how the Hero of Light intended to deal with the Orcs.
Luke stood up and glanced toward her.
"Alright, beauty, wait here. I’ll deal with them soon."
He gave Emberlyn a playful wink before stepping from the branch.
’Weird person.’
Emberlyn completely ignored the gesture and continued watching.
Luke dropped through the canopy.
WHOOSH!
Several branches bent beneath the force of his descent before his body struck the ground near the outpost.
BANG!
Dirt, leaves, and broken twigs blasted outward from beneath his feet, while the impact immediately caught the attention of the Orcs stationed upon the nearest watchtowers.
The guards turned toward the source of the sound before raising their weapons.
"Intruder!"
Their warning echoed through the outpost.
Luke looked upward in mild surprise. ’They speak Valtharion’s common language?’
He hadn’t expected a tribe that had recently emerged from the Endless Forest to communicate using the same language, although he didn’t have time to investigate the reason yet.
Deeper inside the outpost, a heavily built green-skinned Orc sat comfortably upon a throne-like wooden chair while drinking wine from a large cup.
Several women were performing in front of him, although they clearly weren’t Orcs.
They were inhabitants of the Dragon Continent.

True dragons represented only a small portion of the continent’s overall population because of their naturally low birth rate, while numerous half-dragon species lived throughout their territories, and these women belonged to one such race.
Their lower bodies resembled serpents, while their upper bodies remained humanoid, with patches of draconic scales visible across different parts of their skin.
Yarvokh, the Orc captain responsible for this outpost, had been casually drinking while watching their performance when an Orc Shaman suddenly entered.
"Yarvokh, the outer guards have spotted a humanoid intruder, and he doesn’t possess any visible draconic characteristics."
Yarvokh paused with the cup near his mouth before looking toward the Shaman.
After considering the report for a moment, he casually leaned back against his chair.

"Then it’s probably one of those young dragons walking around in humanoid form, because those older, lazy, arrogant dragons would rather sit inside their lairs than personally come all the way out here."
He resumed drinking without showing much concern.
Their outpost stood near the edge of the Dragon Continent, and Yarvokh didn’t believe anyone truly powerful would personally bother coming this far merely to deal with them.
This wasn’t the Orc tribe’s first conquest either.

Before arriving here, they had fought repeatedly throughout different regions of the Endless Forest, where conflict over safe territory was common despite the forest’s seemingly endless size, because much of that land contained dangers that even established tribes preferred to avoid.
For that reason, many species competed over already-secured territories rather than blindly expanding deeper into unexplored regions, and the Orcs had been no different.
Unfortunately, their most recent campaign had ended in defeat, forcing the tribe to retreat with what remained of its population until they eventually reached the Dragon Continent.

After discovering the weaker inhabitants living near its outer regions, the Orcs’ old habit of conquest quickly returned, and they began attacking settlements while establishing bases throughout the surrounding territory.
Yarvokh took another drink before casually waving one hand toward the Shaman.
"Go and bring me his head."
The Orc Shaman nodded and turned toward the exit, while Yarvokh looked back toward the frightened half-serpent women standing before him.
"Why did you stop? Keep dancing."
The trembling women immediately resumed their performance while the warning cries from outside continued spreading through the outpost.

chapters.title: Chapter 364: One Kill Makes the Entire Orc Army Afraid—and Greedy!
paragraphs: Outside the outpost, the moment Luke was spotted, the previously relaxed camp erupted into activity as Orcs rushed toward the walls and watchtowers, eager to see who had been foolish enough to approach them alone.
"A young dragon? Hahaha! I’ll kill him myself and earn the title of Dragon Slayer!"
That single declaration only made the surrounding Orcs more excited.

True dragons rarely appeared this far out, and aside from the crimson dragon that had been destroying their bases throughout the past month, most of their time on the Dragon Continent had consisted of attacking settlements and expanding their conquered territory.
"Shut up!"
A harsh voice immediately suppressed the growing commotion.
The Orc Shaman strode through the crowd with his staff in hand before glaring at the rowdy warriors gathered around him.
"Stop standing here gossiping and get outside. Bring me that dragon’s head!"
The surrounding Orcs immediately became quieter, although the bloodlust burning across their expressions only grew stronger at the thought of another battle.
Seeing their reaction, the Shaman gave a satisfied nod before adding, "Whoever brings back the young dragon’s head will receive a personal reward from Captain Yarvokh."
"Really?!"
"HURAAAHHH!"
That announcement immediately sent the Orcs into another frenzy, and thousands began grabbing whatever weapons were nearest to them.

Heavy metal clubs, broad swords, war hammers, axes, and other crude weapons quickly filled their hands, yet almost none of the Orcs bothered wearing complete armor, instead fastening thick pieces of metal around vulnerable areas such as the chest, neck, shoulders, and waist.
There was another feature shared by nearly every warrior.

Across their green skin ran interconnected crimson tattoos that stretched from their torsos toward their arms, backs, legs, and necks, forming a single continuous pattern that seemed to cover their entire bodies.
The Orc Shaman raised his staff.
"GO!"
"Slaughter him!"
"Kill the dragon!"
THUMP! THUMP! THUMP! THUMP!

Thousands of D-Rank Orc warriors surged through the outpost entrance at once, each standing around nine feet tall with heavily developed muscles, and their combined footsteps caused the surrounding ground to tremble slightly beneath their charge.
The C-Rank Orcs didn’t join them.

Instead, they gathered along the top of the earthen wall with their arms folded, watching the battlefield with relaxed expressions while the Shaman stood among them, his staff resting against the ground.
None of them seemed particularly concerned.
"How many do you think it’ll take?"
"Maybe a thousand."
Another C-Rank Orc laughed.
"I’d say three thousand."
The Shaman didn’t join their conversation and simply kept watching the lone figure standing beyond the walls.
Luke hadn’t moved.

His shoulder-length black hair shifted gently in the forest breeze while he stood with one hand resting casually at his side, showing none of the tension that should have appeared upon seeing thousands of Orc warriors charging directly toward him.
To the Shaman, Luke looked less like someone facing an army and more like a lion that had wandered outside for a casual stroll and couldn’t be bothered by the pack of dogs running toward it.
’Why isn’t he afraid?’
For a moment, the Shaman became confused.
’Does that arrogance really run this deeply in young dragons?’
His thoughts briefly returned to the reports concerning the gigantic crimson dragon that had spent the past month hunting down their bases.

Even some A-Rank members of their tribe had encountered that creature, only to return severely injured and order the remaining forces to stop expanding openly and develop their positions more carefully.
Still, the Shaman quickly dismissed the uneasiness in his heart.
’Whatever.’
The young dragon standing outside didn’t look anything like that monster.
Soon, he would be dead.
"KILL HIM!"
"HE’S MINE!"
"SLAUGHTER!"
"BLOOD!"
Luke calmly watched the thousands of Orcs rushing toward him while their voices echoed through the forest.
"Paragon’s Judgment."
Luke whispered the name, and a golden sword immediately materialized within his right hand.
Floating some distance above him, Caelith noticed the weapon and smiled slightly.
"He already released one of its seals. That’s good, because the more seals he breaks, the closer Paragon will come to recovering its real power."
Nyx, Myrkhal, and Sevaroth remained quiet beside her, simply observing Luke to see how he intended to handle the approaching army.
Would he transform?
Would he summon his armor?
Or would he fight with nothing more than his current body?
Luke lightly moved Paragon through the air while examining the incoming Orcs.
"Hmm... D-Rank?"
He shook his head.
There was no reason to increase his strength yet.

Even without Titan transformation or armor, his current physical stats had already reached around the level of an Early C-Rank human fighter, which placed these D-Rank Orc warriors considerably below him.
A smile appeared on Luke’s face.
"Let’s dance, baby."
The words had barely left his mouth when his figure vanished.
The Orcs at the front instinctively slowed.
Their earlier shouting abruptly weakened as thousands of warriors stared at the place where Luke had been standing only an instant earlier.
"Where did he go?
"Fools!" one of the C-Rank Orcs shouted angrily from the wall. "Use your senses! He didn’t disappear, he’s just faster than you!"
The warning came too late.
"Ugh—!"
A strangled sound suddenly came from the middle of the formation.
Several Orcs immediately turned toward it.
One of their warriors stood completely frozen, both hands clutching his throat, where a deep crimson line now stretched across his neck.
Strangely, no blood flowed from the wound.
Luke was already standing behind him with Paragon lowered beside his body.
The surrounding Orcs had barely recognized him when something far more disturbing happened.
"AAAAHHHH!"
The wounded Orc released a terrified scream as his body suddenly began shrinking.
His thick muscles collapsed inward first, followed by his bones, organs, skin, blood, and everything contained within his body, while his entire nine-foot frame twisted toward a single central point.
"What the hell?!"
Several nearby Orcs instinctively stumbled backward.
The screaming warrior continued compressing until his entire existence had been drawn into a rapidly shrinking sphere, whose surface gradually turned deep crimson and began releasing a dense glow.
Luke watched silently.
Within only a few seconds, the Orc disappeared completely.
Floating where he had once stood was a small crimson sphere filled with vibrant blood energy, its surface pulsing faintly almost like a freshly refined elixir.
No corpse remained behind.
The nearest Orcs stared at it in horror.
Yet beneath that horror, something else immediately awakened inside them.
Desire.

Their bodies instinctively recognized the energy contained within the sphere, and every D-Rank Orc nearby suddenly felt an overwhelming urge to seize it, swallow it, and make whatever was contained inside part of themselves.
Even the C-Rank Orcs standing upon the wall reacted.
The Shaman’s previously calm expression finally changed.
’What is that?’
Despite being a realm higher than the Orc who had just died, he could clearly sense that consuming the crimson sphere might save him months of cultivation.
That shouldn’t have been possible.
The target had only been D-Rank.
Yet the strange object wasn’t merely carrying the dead Orc’s accumulated energy.
It contained something deeper.
Something their instincts understood even if their minds didn’t.
"A desire to evolve..."
One of the C-Rank Orcs unconsciously muttered those words.
