chapters.title: Chapter 365: Emberlyn’s Goodwill Toward Luke Suddenly Drops!
paragraphs: Above the battlefield, the four Titan spirits had also become silent.
Nyx stared at the crimson sphere while Caelith’s earlier smile disappeared, and even Myrkhal stopped moving around as Sevaroth focused completely upon what "The Eternal Origin Zero" had just created.
They understood far more than the Orcs below.
That sphere wasn’t simply condensed blood.

The technique had taken everything useful belonging to the dead Orc—his bloodline, vitality, soul, spirit, mind, karma, destiny, and the other aspects connected to his existence—before refining all of it into a form suitable for Luke’s evolution.
"This really is an EX-Rank technique..."
Nyx’s voice carried genuine disbelief.
They had once stood among Eternal beings themselves, and as Forbidden Titans, each of them had been extraordinarily powerful even among existences of that realm.
Yet they had never stood above the universe itself.

What they were witnessing now felt fundamentally different, because something that should have belonged only to the authority of the universe was being reproduced before them through a cultivation technique.
Emberlyn’s reaction was completely different.
The calm expression she usually carried had disappeared as she stared at the crimson sphere floating above the battlefield, while an uncomfortable suspicion slowly entered her mind.
’A demonic ritual...?’
Her expression darkened.
’Or some kind of forbidden witchcraft?’
She looked toward Luke, who was still standing among the Orc army with Paragon resting casually in his hand.
’Where did Luke learn something like this?’
Another thought immediately followed, and this one bothered her even more.
’Was this how he became stronger so quickly?’
Emberlyn’s gaze remained fixed on him.
’Has he used this on innocent beings before?’

Many questions immediately surfaced in Emberlyn’s mind, because after learning that she had originally been intended to marry this supposedly talentless Hero, she had naturally investigated Luke and followed some of his recent accomplishments.

She remembered clearly how news of him reaching E-Rank had spread throughout the human territories like wildfire, yet the Luke standing before her now had already reached D-Rank despite barely any time having passed.
That difference made her suspicion deepen.
’Was he really forced to use some kind of dark method because of his lack of talent?’
Emberlyn couldn’t think of many other explanations, especially since the Church itself had been the one, who announce to everyone, that Luke possessed almost no cultivation talent.
"Could this really be true...?"
She muttered under her breath, and the small amount of goodwill she had gradually developed toward Luke weakened considerably.

Emberlyn wasn’t some saint who treasured every mortal life equally, nor would she hesitate to kill enemies when necessary, but that didn’t mean she approved of indiscriminate slaughter or cultivation methods built upon sacrificing others.
More importantly, methods like these were dangerous even for the cultivator.

The more someone relied upon blood, souls, and slaughter to advance, the easier it became for that person’s mind and spirit to deteriorate until killing stopped being a means to grow and instead became something they craved.

The Demon Whisperer cults were infamous for exactly that kind of practice, sacrificing living beings to increase their realms at unnatural speeds, although whatever Luke had just used appeared considerably more refined than those crude rituals.
That only made Emberlyn more uneasy.

Meanwhile, below the tree, silence had spread across the battlefield as thousands of Orcs stared greedily at the thumb-sized crimson sphere floating in the air, momentarily forgetting about the person responsible for creating it.
Luke himself was also staring at it with curiosity.
’So this is what the System meant when it explained how the technique would absorb them?’
He was certain the Orc had died.
His sword had completely severed the creature’s neck, yet instead of the head falling away normally, it had somehow remained connected long enough for the strange transformation to begin.
Even more strangely, Paragon’s Judgment hadn’t absorbed anything from the body despite being the weapon Luke had used to kill it.
Before Luke could think further, the surrounding Orcs finally recovered from their trance.
"That thing is mine! Don’t any of you dare touch it!"
One Orc roared before launching himself toward the crimson pill.
Nobody listened.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!

Several more Orcs instantly leaped after him with speed far beyond what ordinary D-Rank warriors should have possessed, and Luke immediately noticed the crimson tattoos covering their bodies beginning to glow.
’So those tattoos aren’t just decoration.’
The sudden increase in their speed made the answer obvious.
"Mine!"
One Orc stretched his hand toward the floating pill, his fingertips almost touching it, when the sphere abruptly shifted several feet through the air.
His expression changed in disbelief, while the Orcs behind him immediately grinned upon seeing his failure and rushed forward to claim it themselves.
Before any of them could succeed, however, the blood pill suddenly accelerated toward Luke.
It slipped past every reaching hand with ease before striking his chest and disappearing directly into his body as though it had never existed.
For several seconds, nobody moved.
The Orcs stared at Luke while trying to understand what they had just witnessed, and even Emberlyn watched more carefully from above.
Luke glanced down at his chest before breaking the silence himself.
"Ahh, looks like the heavenly elixir chose me instead. How lucky."
He casually patted his chest before looking toward the surrounding Orcs with a mocking smile.
"It really feels good having the Goddess of Luck backing you."
This time, the silence wasn’t caused by fear or greed.
Everyone simply looked at him speechlessly.
They had all seen the crimson sphere return to Luke by itself, making it obvious that the object had some connection to him, so none of them understood why a Goddess had suddenly become involved.
Several Orcs’ mouths twitched.
Then their confusion turned into anger.
"Kill him! The blood pill is still inside his body!"
The same Orc who had first tried to claim it shouted loudly, and the rest immediately snapped out of their stunned state.
"Yes! Kill him!"
"We wants to see blood!"
Luke’s smile widened slightly.
"Then you will."
He raised Paragon’s Judgment just as the surrounding Orcs rushed toward him again.
SLASH—!
Luke’s sword swept through the first group, and more than five Orc heads were sent spinning through the air before their bodies had even finished moving forward.
He immediately shifted his footing and thrust Paragon straight ahead.
PUCHI—!
The blade pierced through one Orc before driving into another behind him, and with Luke’s Early C-Rank physical strength behind the attack, even their reinforced bodies couldn’t stop the sword.
The Orcs continued coming from every direction, yet their numbers did little to slow him down.
Whenever Luke swung, several bodies fell.
Whenever he thrust, multiple Orcs were pierced in a single line.
Even after the crimson tattoos covering their bodies activated, the increase still wasn’t enough to close the gap between them.
’About twice their normal strength.’
Luke quickly estimated the effect while continuing through the crowd.
The tattoos appeared capable of roughly doubling the physical ability of these D-Rank Orcs, which was impressive, but still far below what was needed to threaten his current body.
Then something strange happened behind him.
One of the severed Orc heads suddenly stopped rolling.
Luke sensed movement and glanced back just in time to see the head rise from the ground before shooting toward its original body.
The severed neck connected perfectly.
"...What?"
Several nearby Orcs froze.

chapters.title: Chapter 366: The Orcs Stop Fighting for Glory—Now They Want Revenge!
paragraphs: The same phenomenon immediately began occurring to every other corpse Luke had created.

Pieces of flesh scattered across the ground lifted into the air, severed limbs returned toward their bodies, and even droplets of blood that had splattered across nearby plants and soil began flowing backward.
Nothing appeared to be left behind.
Then the first Orc suddenly opened his eyes.
"AAAAAHHHH!"
The scream that followed wasn’t one of revival.
His entire body began collapsing inward just as the previous Orc’s had, with muscle, bone, blood, organs, and every other part of his existence compressing toward a single point.
Around him, the same thing began happening to the others.
"AAAAHHH!"
"AAAAAHHH!"
"AAAAHHHH!"
The battlefield filled with agonized cries as the reconstructed Orcs were compressed one after another, and none of them managed to say anything beyond those screams.
It looked as though they were experiencing unimaginable pain while every part of their existence was stripped away and condensed.
One crimson pill appeared.
Then another.
Then ten more.
Soon, dozens of blood-red spheres were floating across the battlefield, each releasing dense vitality while slowly rotating in the air.
Yet what Luke and the Orcs were seeing wasn’t the entire process.
"The Eternal Origin Zero" wasn’t merely rebuilding their physical bodies before refining them.
The moment Luke personally killed someone, that existence became marked by the technique.

Even if the corpse had been destroyed or scattered, every remaining fragment was drawn back together until the target was once again complete, as though not even the smallest piece was permitted to escape.
Only after restoring the target to a complete state did the technique begin its true refinement.

Blood, flesh, soul, spirit, mind, karma, destiny, and everything else belonging to that existence were compressed into a single vessel before "The Eternal Origin Zero" purified it further, ensuring that nothing capable of contaminating Luke’s own mind or spirit remained.
That was also why Emberlyn’s fear that Luke would eventually become a bloodthirsty maniac wouldn’t apply in the way she imagined.
If the technique allowed the resentment, madness, memories, or spiritual corruption of everything Luke devoured to accumulate inside him, it could never have been worthy of EX-Rank.
There was, however, an even stranger part to the process.
Under ordinary circumstances, a cultivation method that completely erased someone’s existence should have triggered a reaction from Valtharion itself.
Yet "The Eternal Origin Zero" avoided even that.
When Luke killed someone, Valtharion first recognized the death normally and collected the soul according to the world’s natural reincarnation cycle.
From Valtharion’s perspective, everything proceeded exactly as it should.
The soul had died.
The world had received it.
The cycle of reincarnation had begun.
However, just before that soul could truly enter the reincarnation pool, "The Eternal Origin Zero" silently pulled it back.
In the next instant, the soul was refined together with everything else belonging to the dead existence and completely erased.
Valtharion never reacted.
As far as the world’s laws were concerned, that soul had already entered the reincarnation process and was therefore no longer something the world needed to track.
That was the terrifying difference between an ordinary forbidden cultivation method and an EX-Rank technique.
It didn’t openly oppose the laws of the world.
It simply passed through them.

And even if Valtharion somehow examined everything that had happened here afterward, it still wouldn’t be able to discover what "The Eternal Origin Zero" had truly done, because above Valtharion itself stood the universe and the technique was also at that rank.

Rather than directly opposing Valtharion’s laws, the technique seemed to be using some hidden authority belonging to the universe itself, So making Valtharion perceive the complete erasure of those existences as an action sanctioned by something above its own authority, if it ever tried to examine this.
Therefore, if the universe itself had erased an existence, then there was nothing Valtharion could do about it.
That loophole was exactly what made Luke safe while using the technique.
"More blood pills!"
The moment the Orcs saw several more crimson spheres appear, whatever hesitation remained among them disappeared almost instantly.

They didn’t seem to care that those pills had been created from members of their own species who had been fighting beside them only moments earlier, because companionship held far less importance within their culture than strength and respect.
For most Orcs, becoming stronger was what mattered.
The moment they sensed that the crimson pills could accelerate their growth, their expressions once again filled with greed as dozens rushed toward the floating spheres.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
Several hands reached them almost simultaneously, yet the exact same thing happened again.
The blood pills abruptly changed direction, slipping between fingers and avoiding every Orc trying to seize them before accelerating toward Luke.
One Orc actually managed to close his entire hand around a pill.
His face immediately brightened.
"I got—"
Before he could finish celebrating, something passed straight through his tightly clenched fingers.
"...What?"
The crimson pill had already escaped.
It shot toward Luke alongside the others before all of them struck his body and vanished inside him.
The Orc slowly opened his empty hand while those around him stared in disbelief.
"How did it escape from his hand?"
None of them understood that once "The Eternal Origin Zero" refined an existence into one of those crimson pills, the result already belonged completely to Luke.
The beings he personally killed had been marked by the technique, and everything refined from those marked existences remained bound to him afterward.
Unless the universe itself interfered, nobody else within that universe could steal one of those pills from him.
Luke, however, was concerned about something completely different.
’Hmm... I don’t feel anything.’
His lips twitched slightly in annoyance.

The moment each pill entered his body, "The Eternal Origin Zero" had already begun working silently, distributing and refining everything it contained while activating the seven internal reformations required for his new Titan foundation.

His blood was already being rewritten as each newly refined portion was inscribed with the principles belonging to every Titan he had currently unlocked, while the remaining transformations continued alongside it without requiring Luke to consciously control them.
Yet despite everything happening inside his body, he couldn’t feel any noticeable increase in strength.
’This is an EX-Rank technique, and I can’t even feel it working?’
Luke clicked his tongue before dismissing the thought.
’Whatever.’
When he looked around again, he found hundreds of Orcs staring at him with such intense hatred that their expressions looked strangely personal.
Luke became silent for a second.
’Why are they looking at me like I slept with all their wives?’
His mouth twitched.
The more he looked at them, the more certain he became that their expressions somehow gave exactly that impression.
"Kill that bastard!"
One furious Orc finally roared, and the others immediately answered with equally enraged shouts as their earlier excitement for battle transformed into genuine hatred toward Luke.
Luke glanced upward briefly.
’System... you’re seeing this too, right? They really look like I did something to their wives.’
Luke waited for a response for half a second before deciding he didn’t want to hear whatever the System was about to say.
Instead, he tightened his grip around Paragon and charged directly into the crowd.
The situation immediately reversed.

sentences.text: The same phenomenon immediately began occurring to every other corpse Luke had created.

Pieces of flesh scattered across the ground lifted into the air, severed limbs returned toward their bodies, and even droplets of blood that had splattered across nearby plants and soil began flowing backward.
Nothing appeared to be left behind.
Then the first Orc suddenly opened his eyes.
"AAAAAHHHH!"
The scream that followed wasn’t one of revival.
His entire body began collapsing inward just as the previous Orc’s had, with muscle, bone, blood, organs, and every other part of his existence compressing toward a single point.
Around him, the same thing began happening to the others.
"AAAAHHH!"
"AAAAAHHH!"
"AAAAHHHH!"
The battlefield filled with agonized cries as the reconstructed Orcs were compressed one after another, and none of them managed to say anything beyond those screams.
It looked as though they were experiencing unimaginable pain while every part of their existence was stripped away and condensed.
One crimson pill appeared.
Then another.
Then ten more.
Soon, dozens of blood-red spheres were floating across the battlefield, each releasing dense vitality while slowly rotating in the air.
Yet what Luke and the Orcs were seeing wasn’t the entire process.
"The Eternal Origin Zero" wasn’t merely rebuilding their physical bodies before refining them.
The moment Luke personally killed someone, that existence became marked by the technique.

Even if the corpse had been destroyed or scattered, every remaining fragment was drawn back together until the target was once again complete, as though not even the smallest piece was permitted to escape.
Only after restoring the target to a complete state did the technique begin its true refinement.

Blood, flesh, soul, spirit, mind, karma, destiny, and everything else belonging to that existence were compressed into a single vessel before "The Eternal Origin Zero" purified it further, ensuring that nothing capable of contaminating Luke’s own mind or spirit remained.
That was also why Emberlyn’s fear that Luke would eventually become a bloodthirsty maniac wouldn’t apply in the way she imagined.
If the technique allowed the resentment, madness, memories, or spiritual corruption of everything Luke devoured to accumulate inside him, it could never have been worthy of EX-Rank.
There was, however, an even stranger part to the process.
Under ordinary circumstances, a cultivation method that completely erased someone’s existence should have triggered a reaction from Valtharion itself.
Yet "The Eternal Origin Zero" avoided even that.
When Luke killed someone, Valtharion first recognized the death normally and collected the soul according to the world’s natural reincarnation cycle.
From Valtharion’s perspective, everything proceeded exactly as it should.
The soul had died.
The world had received it.
The cycle of reincarnation had begun.
However, just before that soul could truly enter the reincarnation pool, "The Eternal Origin Zero" silently pulled it back.
In the next instant, the soul was refined together with everything else belonging to the dead existence and completely erased.
Valtharion never reacted.
As far as the world’s laws were concerned, that soul had already entered the reincarnation process and was therefore no longer something the world needed to track.
That was the terrifying difference between an ordinary forbidden cultivation method and an EX-Rank technique.
It didn’t openly oppose the laws of the world.
It simply passed through them.

And even if Valtharion somehow examined everything that had happened here afterward, it still wouldn’t be able to discover what "The Eternal Origin Zero" had truly done, because above Valtharion itself stood the universe and the technique was also at that rank.

Rather than directly opposing Valtharion’s laws, the technique seemed to be using some hidden authority belonging to the universe itself, So making Valtharion perceive the complete erasure of those existences as an action sanctioned by something above its own authority, if it ever tried to examine this.
Therefore, if the universe itself had erased an existence, then there was nothing Valtharion could do about it.
That loophole was exactly what made Luke safe while using the technique.
"More blood pills!"
The moment the Orcs saw several more crimson spheres appear, whatever hesitation remained among them disappeared almost instantly.

They didn’t seem to care that those pills had been created from members of their own species who had been fighting beside them only moments earlier, because companionship held far less importance within their culture than strength and respect.
For most Orcs, becoming stronger was what mattered.
The moment they sensed that the crimson pills could accelerate their growth, their expressions once again filled with greed as dozens rushed toward the floating spheres.
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
Several hands reached them almost simultaneously, yet the exact same thing happened again.
The blood pills abruptly changed direction, slipping between fingers and avoiding every Orc trying to seize them before accelerating toward Luke.
One Orc actually managed to close his entire hand around a pill.
His face immediately brightened.
"I got—"
Before he could finish celebrating, something passed straight through his tightly clenched fingers.
"...What?"
The crimson pill had already escaped.
It shot toward Luke alongside the others before all of them struck his body and vanished inside him.
The Orc slowly opened his empty hand while those around him stared in disbelief.
"How did it escape from his hand?"
None of them understood that once "The Eternal Origin Zero" refined an existence into one of those crimson pills, the result already belonged completely to Luke.
The beings he personally killed had been marked by the technique, and everything refined from those marked existences remained bound to him afterward.
Unless the universe itself interfered, nobody else within that universe could steal one of those pills from him.
Luke, however, was concerned about something completely different.
’Hmm...
I don’t feel anything.’
His lips twitched slightly in annoyance.

The moment each pill entered his body, "The Eternal Origin Zero" had already begun working silently, distributing and refining everything it contained while activating the seven internal reformations required for his new Titan foundation.

His blood was already being rewritten as each newly refined portion was inscribed with the principles belonging to every Titan he had currently unlocked, while the remaining transformations continued alongside it without requiring Luke to consciously control them.
Yet despite everything happening inside his body, he couldn’t feel any noticeable increase in strength.
’This is an EX-Rank technique, and I can’t even feel it working?’
Luke clicked his tongue before dismissing the thought.
’Whatever.’
When he looked around again, he found hundreds of Orcs staring at him with such intense hatred that their expressions looked strangely personal.
Luke became silent for a second.
’Why are they looking at me like I slept with all their wives?’
His mouth twitched.
The more he looked at them, the more certain he became that their expressions somehow gave exactly that impression.
"Kill that bastard!"

’System... you’re seeing this too, right?
They really look like I did something to their wives.’

Instead, he tightened his grip around Paragon and charged directly into the crowd.
The situation immediately reversed.

chapters.title: Chapter 367: The Dragon Princess Begins Feeling Sorry for Luke?!
paragraphs: The thousands of Orcs who had rushed outside expecting to slaughter a lone young dragon suddenly found themselves becoming the ones being hunted, while Luke moved through their formation like a wolf entering a herd of sheep.
SLASH—!
Paragon swept horizontally through three Orcs before Luke twisted his body and drove the blade through another warrior approaching from behind.
PUCHI!

He pulled the sword free and immediately stepped aside as a metal hammer slammed into the ground where he had been standing, sending dirt outward before Luke’s return slash opened the attacker’s throat.
Another Orc rushed from his left.
Luke shifted one step forward, avoided the descending club, and drove his elbow into the warrior’s chest hard enough to send the nine-foot Orc crashing backward through several others.
Before the fallen bodies could even settle, the Orcs Luke had killed began reconstructing behind him.

Severed limbs flew backward, spilled blood returned from the ground, and scattered fragments of flesh rejoined their original bodies before the reconstructed Orcs released agonized screams and collapsed inward.
One after another, crimson pills formed across the battlefield.
The four Titan spirits floating above watched the process with increasing amazement.
Even during their primes, none of them had possessed a method capable of creating something like this.

To refine an entire existence into a single evolutionary resource required far more than control over flesh and blood, because the technique was simultaneously handling the soul, spirit, life, death, fate, destiny, karma, and numerous other aspects that together formed a complete being.
Calling the resulting object a blood pill was almost misleading.
What "The Eternal Origin Zero" was producing went beyond ordinary creation.
It was a condensed resource for evolution itself, something that even among the highest existences of their original universe had only ever been discussed as an almost mythical possibility.
Sevaroth stared at one of the crimson pills for several seconds before speaking.
"How is that technique doing this?"
His attention wasn’t even focused upon the energy inside it.
He was looking at the structure holding everything together.

There were seals woven throughout the pill, yet their arrangement was so intricate that even Sevaroth, whose understanding of sealing had once stood at a level few beings could approach, couldn’t completely understand what he was seeing.
For the first time in a long while, his own knowledge of seals seemed almost primitive in comparison.
Nyx remained silent for several seconds before finally murmuring, "Is this really only a fraction of what the universe itself can do?"
That thought struck all of them differently.

They had been born from their universe and had eventually risen until almost nobody within it could stand above them, so over time, it had become natural for them to compare their own achievements against the universe that had created them.

Whenever they accomplished something unprecedented and received rewards or acknowledgement from the universe, they had interpreted those responses as proof that they were gradually approaching its level.
Only now did Nyx begin to understand how wrong that assumption might have been.
What they once considered recognition could just as easily have been affection.
The universe had watched them grow, celebrated their accomplishments, and rewarded them whenever they surpassed another boundary, almost like a mother watching her children succeed.
Yet those children had mistaken that kindness for equality.
Nyx released a quiet sigh.
"I think I’m finally beginning to understand."
There was regret in his voice.

During their era, they had constantly struggled to surpass the universe that gave birth to them, believing that reaching higher and higher realms would eventually allow them to stand beside it, yet they had rarely stopped to consider why it continued helping them along the way.
Even after they crossed the Warden Rank, they still hadn’t truly understood the distance separating them from their creator.
Then those beings arrived.

Their universe was destroyed, and the mother they had spent so long trying to surpass was killed, while Nyx and the others survived only because their Eternal existences had already spread their respective aspects beyond a single universe.
Their enemies couldn’t completely erase them, so imprisonment became the only practical solution.
In the end, the enemy had still won.
Their mother was gone.
They remained.
Sevaroth’s reaction to those memories was considerably different.
Unlike Nyx, he didn’t feel the same regret toward the universe that had created the others, because a part of him still carried resentment toward her for sealing him.
He understood the reason behind it better now.

Someone else had interfered with what the universe had originally created, altering him so deeply that the existence he had once been was effectively erased and replaced by something new, and the universe had responded by placing a curse upon that changed existence before sealing him away.
Perhaps she had simply been furious that something had tampered with her creation.
Perhaps she no longer regarded the resulting Sevaroth as her child at all.
Even Sevaroth didn’t know the complete truth.

What he also didn’t know was that Luke was already aware of part of this history, because the System had revealed enough through Sevaroth’s descriptions for Luke to realize that the Crypt Titan standing beside him wasn’t exactly the same existence that had originally been born.
Nyx and Caelith remained unaware of that detail.
Myrkhal, meanwhile, showed no visible reaction at all.

His featureless face had no eyes, mouth, or other expression to read, and recently he had spoken even less than usual, leaving everyone completely unable to tell what thoughts were passing through his mind.
Below them, Emberlyn’s expression only became darker as the battle continued.
From her perspective, what she was witnessing looked completely different from what the Titan spirits understood.
Luke wasn’t merely killing the Orcs.
His strange technique appeared to reconstruct their corpses, force them through unbearable pain, devour their souls, and compress everything into blood-colored pills that then entered his own body.
Disgust should have been the strongest emotion she felt toward him.
Instead, strangely enough, part of that disgust gradually turned into pity.

Emberlyn had heard stories about cultivators who turned toward forbidden methods after being pushed into desperation, especially those who had suffered some unbearable loss or discovered that ordinary cultivation would never allow them to reach the strength they desperately wanted.
Luke had been declared talentless.
Among all the summoned Heroes, he was supposed to be the one destined to remain weak while the others continued climbing toward realms he could never reach.
Yet now he had somehow risen from an ordinary mortal to D-Rank within an incredibly short period.
Looking at the crimson pills disappearing into his body, Emberlyn began constructing an explanation that seemed increasingly reasonable in her mind.
’Maybe he didn’t have another choice.’
Her gaze remained fixed upon Luke as he moved through the Orc army.
’Maybe this was the only way he found to remove that talentless label from himself.’
And with that thought, the suspicion she felt toward him didn’t disappear, but it became mixed with something she hadn’t expected to feel.
Pity.

chapters.title: Chapter 368: Orc Thought : “Why Did a Monster Like This Appear Here?!”
paragraphs: "Elgrun, should we intervene?"
One of the C-Rank Orcs turned toward the Shaman, whose expression had grown increasingly ugly after watching Luke slaughter hundreds of D-Rank warriors within such a short period.
Elgrun remained silent for a few seconds before shaking his head.
"No, let him continue. The more he fights, the more tired he’ll become."
He tightened his grip around the staff in his hand while continuing to watch Luke from the top of the earthen wall.
"That young dragon is only releasing a D-Rank aura right now, which means he still hasn’t revealed his dragon form."

The other C-Rank Orcs immediately understood what he meant, because if Luke truly was a young dragon, then the moment he transformed into his true body, he would gain flight along with whatever racial abilities his dragon bloodline possessed.
If they attacked too early and failed to surround him properly, even the slightest mistake could allow him to escape into the sky, so exhausting him first was undoubtedly the safer choice.
With that decision made, the higher-ranked Orcs continued observing while the battle below dragged on.
Nearly an hour passed.
Luke released a long breath and slowly looked around the battlefield.
There wasn’t a single corpse lying near him despite the number of Orcs he had already killed, although bloodstains covered patches of grass, broken roots, and sections of the churned ground.

Any blood belonging to someone Luke had killed had already been pulled back into its original body before that existence was refined into a blood pill, which meant the remaining blood belonged entirely to the Orcs who had been wounded but were still alive.
Luke himself remained almost completely unharmed.

No D-Rank warrior present possessed enough attack power to properly damage a body whose physical durability had already reached C-Rank, so although his upper clothes had been torn apart during the prolonged battle, exposing his chest and several shallow marks left upon his skin, none of those attacks had caused any real injury.
Fortunately, his pants had somehow survived the battle in one piece, although several sections had already been ripped.
"This monster..."
The Orc who had first attempted to steal one of the blood pills was still alive, although that survival had more to do with caution and luck than strength.

Unlike many others, he had rarely attacked Luke directly from the front and instead waited for opportunities to strike from supposed blind spots, which had allowed him to survive despite the numerous wounds now covering his body.
The remaining D-Rank Orcs weren’t in much better condition.

Their earlier confidence had disappeared after watching thousands of their own warriors vanish one after another, because of the original eight thousand D-Ranks stationed in the outpost, Luke had already killed more than three thousand.
Only around five thousand remained.

Until now, the Orcs below D-Rank had stayed away from the battle, since throwing weaker warriors against someone capable of slaughtering D-Ranks so easily had seemed pointless, but Elgrun had finally decided that numbers themselves could still serve a purpose.
Even if those weaker Orcs couldn’t injure Luke, they could force him to expend more stamina.
An order soon echoed from the outpost wall.
"Everyone, move out! Kill that young dragon, and whoever contributes the most will receive a reward!"
"HAAAAH!"
"HE’S MINE!"
"CRUSH HIM!"
THUD! THUD! THUD!
DUDUDUDUDUDU—!
CLANK! CLANK!
"RAAAAGH!"

The outpost erupted into another wave of war cries as the remaining D-Rank warriors charged forward, but this time they were joined by thousands upon thousands of E-Rank and F-Rank Orcs carrying clubs, swords, axes, hammers, and whatever other weapons they could obtain.

Their combined footsteps rolled through the forest like continuous thunder as weapons struck against shields and pieces of armor, while the sheer number of bodies pouring through the outpost entrance quickly spread across the surrounding ground.
None of them appeared frightened despite having already watched Luke slaughter thousands of their stronger warriors.
Orcs were a race raised around battle, where retreating from an enemy was easily interpreted as weakness, and very few Orcs willingly accepted being considered weak.
Luke watched the new crowd approaching and clicked his tongue in annoyance.
The problem wasn’t their numbers.
It was their realms.

"The Eternal Origin Zero" could currently only refine beings at D-Rank or above into cultivation resources for his present stage, which meant the E-Rank and F-Rank Orcs rushing toward him were completely useless for his cultivation.
"Sigh... I should finish this quickly. I still have more outposts to deal with."

His casual words immediately caused several nearby D-Rank Orcs to tense, because the calmness in Luke’s voice gave them an unpleasant feeling that he had never considered this battle particularly difficult in the first place.
Up on the wall, however, Elgrun and the other C-Rank Orcs reacted differently.
Their expressions brightened.
"He’s finally going to transform."
Elgrun leaned slightly forward, convinced that his plan had worked.
He was right about one thing.
Luke was indeed going to transform.
Unfortunately for them, what emerged wouldn’t be a dragon.
Luke lowered Paragon slightly while looking toward the approaching army, then spoke in a quiet voice that was nearly drowned beneath the Orcs’ war cries.
"Cosmic Heart Titan."
The instant those words left his mouth, his body rippled.
Golden-white light spread across him as Elythos formed over his changing physique, wrapping his body in the Armor of the Cosmic Heart while his height rapidly increased.
His limbs lengthened, his frame expanded, and within only a short time, the human-sized figure standing before the Orc army had become a twenty-foot-tall Titan covered in shimmering gold-white armor.
Then his aura changed.
BOOM—!
The pressure spreading from Luke no longer belonged anywhere near D-Rank.
Early B-Rank.
The transformation was so sudden that the Orc army’s charge visibly faltered, while those standing upon the walls stared at Luke with horror.
Even Yarvokh, who was still seated deeper inside the outpost and watching the captured serpent women dance, abruptly stopped drinking when the distant B-Rank presence swept across the camp.
"What is—"
Outside, Elgrun tried to speak as well, but his words stopped the moment another phenomenon appeared above Luke.
Space seemed to distort across the sky as several celestial bodies manifested one after another, forming a miniature cosmic system above the battlefield.
Among them burned a crimson star that resembled a condensed ball of fire, while the surrounding celestial bodies began moving into orbit around it.
"What kind of sorcery is that young dragon using?!"
Several C-Rank Orcs shouted from the wall as they stared upward.
Elgrun didn’t respond.

His feet had already dropped firmly against the surface of the wall as he looked at Luke in disbelief, because as a Shaman who had spent much of his life studying magic, he couldn’t understand what he was witnessing.
A being emitting a D-Rank aura had suddenly transformed and reached B-Rank combat power, yet that wasn’t even the strangest part.
The same person was now manifesting celestial bodies above an entire battlefield as though stars and planets were simply another form of magic he could summon.
Then Luke’s voice reached them.
"Cosmos Manifestation..."
The celestial bodies overhead shifted.
"A Solar System.
RUUUUMMMBLE—!
The entire battlefield sank.

The moment Luke completed the technique, every manifested celestial body released its gravitational influence at once, and the combined pressure slammed downward across the battlefield with enough force to instantly break the weaker Orcs beneath it.

The charging F-Ranks and E-Ranks didn’t even have time to scream properly before their bodies were crushed against the ground, flesh and bone collapsing beneath the sudden gravitational force until many were reduced into bloody paste.
The D-Rank Orcs resisted for slightly longer, yet their knees still slammed downward before their entire bodies were forced flat against the earth.
Some tried desperately to push themselves upward.
None succeeded.
Their faces pressed into the soil while their weapons slipped from their hands, and several stared forward in disbelief as they realized they couldn’t even lift their heads.
The C-Rank Orcs fared better, but not by much.
Elgrun and the others were forced to their knees upon the outpost wall, while several cracked sections of earth beneath their feet as their bodies were continuously dragged downward.
Even their crimson tattoos reacted instinctively.

The markings covering their bodies blazed with red light as they attempted to amplify their physical strength, yet the increased power did little against the gravitational field pressing over the entire area.
Their tattoos continued burning brighter, but their bodies refused to rise.
Elgrun planted both hands against his staff and tried to force himself upward, only for his legs to sink deeper into the earthen wall.
It was then that the same realization appeared across the faces of nearly every Orc still conscious.
’Why did a monster like this appear at the edge of the Dragon Continent?!’
Above the battlefield, the Titan spirits watched the scene with considerably different expressions.
Luke’s transformation itself wasn’t anything surprising to them, yet the precision with which the gravitational force had spread across such a wide area immediately caught their attention.
"His control over gravity has improved."
Nyx spoke while watching the Orc army pinned beneath the manifested Solar System.
Sevaroth gave a small nod, while Caelith looked particularly pleased as she studied the way Luke maintained the gravitational field without allowing it to affect the area where Emberlyn was sitting.
For Caelith, seeing Luke improve his control over a power born from the Cosmic Heart Titan naturally carried a different kind of satisfaction.
Emberlyn, meanwhile, had become completely silent.
She was still seated upon the thick tree branch overlooking the battlefield, yet the suspicion that had filled her mind only moments earlier had been replaced by disbelief.
She had heard reports that Luke possessed some kind of giant transformation.
What she was seeing now was entirely different from what she had imagined.
Luke hadn’t merely transformed his body.
His combat power had jumped across two major ranks, and the gravitational field spreading beneath the celestial bodies above him was strong enough to suppress thousands of Orcs simultaneously.
"And this gravity..."

Emberlyn could feel the force pressing over the battlefield even from where she sat, although her own aura prevented it from affecting her body, while the same protection naturally extended over the tree branch beneath her.
She remained silent for another moment before looking toward the twenty-foot figure standing beneath the miniature Solar System.
"Not even demonic cultivation should be able to give someone this kind of strength."
Her earlier theory suddenly seemed far less convincing.
If Luke’s rapid growth had truly come from some crude sacrificial method similar to those used by Demon Whisperer cultists, then how was he producing power like this?
Emberlyn continued staring at him as another question replaced the suspicions she had formed earlier.
"Then how did Luke obtain this power?"

The Orc who had first attempted to steal one of the blood pills was still alive, although that survival had more to do with caution and luck than strength.

Unlike many others, he had rarely attacked Luke directly from the front and instead waited for opportunities to strike from supposed blind spots, which had allowed him to survive despite the numerous wounds now covering his body.
The remaining D-Rank Orcs weren’t in much better condition.

Their earlier confidence had disappeared after watching thousands of their own warriors vanish one after another, because of the original eight thousand D-Ranks stationed in the outpost, Luke had already killed more than three thousand.
Only around five thousand remained.

Until now, the Orcs below D-Rank had stayed away from the battle, since throwing weaker warriors against someone capable of slaughtering D-Ranks so easily had seemed pointless, but Elgrun had finally decided that numbers themselves could still serve a purpose.
Even if those weaker Orcs couldn’t injure Luke, they could force him to expend more stamina.
An order soon echoed from the outpost wall.
"Everyone, move out!
Kill that young dragon, and whoever contributes the most will receive a reward!"
"HAAAAH!"
"HE’S MINE!"
"CRUSH HIM!"
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
DUDUDUDUDUDU—!
CLANK!
CLANK!
"RAAAAGH!"

The outpost erupted into another wave of war cries as the remaining D-Rank warriors charged forward, but this time they were joined by thousands upon thousands of E-Rank and F-Rank Orcs carrying clubs, swords, axes, hammers, and whatever other weapons they could obtain.

Their combined footsteps rolled through the forest like continuous thunder as weapons struck against shields and pieces of armor, while the sheer number of bodies pouring through the outpost entrance quickly spread across the surrounding ground.
None of them appeared frightened despite having already watched Luke slaughter thousands of their stronger warriors.
Orcs were a race raised around battle, where retreating from an enemy was easily interpreted as weakness, and very few Orcs willingly accepted being considered weak.
Luke watched the new crowd approaching and clicked his tongue in annoyance.
The problem wasn’t their numbers.
It was their realms.

"The Eternal Origin Zero" could currently only refine beings at D-Rank or above into cultivation resources for his present stage, which meant the E-Rank and F-Rank Orcs rushing toward him were completely useless for his cultivation.
"Sigh...
I should finish this quickly.
I still have more outposts to deal with."

His casual words immediately caused several nearby D-Rank Orcs to tense, because the calmness in Luke’s voice gave them an unpleasant feeling that he had never considered this battle particularly difficult in the first place.
Up on the wall, however, Elgrun and the other C-Rank Orcs reacted differently.
Their expressions brightened.
"He’s finally going to transform."
Elgrun leaned slightly forward, convinced that his plan had worked.
He was right about one thing.
Luke was indeed going to transform.
Unfortunately for them, what emerged wouldn’t be a dragon.
Luke lowered Paragon slightly while looking toward the approaching army, then spoke in a quiet voice that was nearly drowned beneath the Orcs’ war cries.
"Cosmic Heart Titan."
The instant those words left his mouth, his body rippled.
Golden-white light spread across him as Elythos formed over his changing physique, wrapping his body in the Armor of the Cosmic Heart while his height rapidly increased.
His limbs lengthened, his frame expanded, and within only a short time, the human-sized figure standing before the Orc army had become a twenty-foot-tall Titan covered in shimmering gold-white armor.
Then his aura changed.
BOOM—!
The pressure spreading from Luke no longer belonged anywhere near D-Rank.
Early B-Rank.
The transformation was so sudden that the Orc army’s charge visibly faltered, while those standing upon the walls stared at Luke with horror.
Even Yarvokh, who was still seated deeper inside the outpost and watching the captured serpent women dance, abruptly stopped drinking when the distant B-Rank presence swept across the camp.
"What is—"
Outside, Elgrun tried to speak as well, but his words stopped the moment another phenomenon appeared above Luke.
Space seemed to distort across the sky as several celestial bodies manifested one after another, forming a miniature cosmic system above the battlefield.
Among them burned a crimson star that resembled a condensed ball of fire, while the surrounding celestial bodies began moving into orbit around it.
"What kind of sorcery is that young dragon using?!"
Several C-Rank Orcs shouted from the wall as they stared upward.
Elgrun didn’t respond.

His feet had already dropped firmly against the surface of the wall as he looked at Luke in disbelief, because as a Shaman who had spent much of his life studying magic, he couldn’t understand what he was witnessing.
A being emitting a D-Rank aura had suddenly transformed and reached B-Rank combat power, yet that wasn’t even the strangest part.
The same person was now manifesting celestial bodies above an entire battlefield as though stars and planets were simply another form of magic he could summon.
Then Luke’s voice reached them.
"Cosmos Manifestation..."
The celestial bodies overhead shifted.
"A Solar System.
RUUUUMMMBLE—!
The entire battlefield sank.

The moment Luke completed the technique, every manifested celestial body released its gravitational influence at once, and the combined pressure slammed downward across the battlefield with enough force to instantly break the weaker Orcs beneath it.

The charging F-Ranks and E-Ranks didn’t even have time to scream properly before their bodies were crushed against the ground, flesh and bone collapsing beneath the sudden gravitational force until many were reduced into bloody paste.
The D-Rank Orcs resisted for slightly longer, yet their knees still slammed downward before their entire bodies were forced flat against the earth.
Some tried desperately to push themselves upward.
None succeeded.
Their faces pressed into the soil while their weapons slipped from their hands, and several stared forward in disbelief as they realized they couldn’t even lift their heads.
The C-Rank Orcs fared better, but not by much.
Elgrun and the others were forced to their knees upon the outpost wall, while several cracked sections of earth beneath their feet as their bodies were continuously dragged downward.
Even their crimson tattoos reacted instinctively.

The markings covering their bodies blazed with red light as they attempted to amplify their physical strength, yet the increased power did little against the gravitational field pressing over the entire area.
Their tattoos continued burning brighter, but their bodies refused to rise.
Elgrun planted both hands against his staff and tried to force himself upward, only for his legs to sink deeper into the earthen wall.
It was then that the same realization appeared across the faces of nearly every Orc still conscious.
’Why did a monster like this appear at the edge of the Dragon Continent?!’
Above the battlefield, the Titan spirits watched the scene with considerably different expressions.
Luke’s transformation itself wasn’t anything surprising to them, yet the precision with which the gravitational force had spread across such a wide area immediately caught their attention.
"His control over gravity has improved."
Nyx spoke while watching the Orc army pinned beneath the manifested Solar System.
Sevaroth gave a small nod, while Caelith looked particularly pleased as she studied the way Luke maintained the gravitational field without allowing it to affect the area where Emberlyn was sitting.
For Caelith, seeing Luke improve his control over a power born from the Cosmic Heart Titan naturally carried a different kind of satisfaction.
Emberlyn, meanwhile, had become completely silent.
She was still seated upon the thick tree branch overlooking the battlefield, yet the suspicion that had filled her mind only moments earlier had been replaced by disbelief.
She had heard reports that Luke possessed some kind of giant transformation.
What she was seeing now was entirely different from what she had imagined.
Luke hadn’t merely transformed his body.
His combat power had jumped across two major ranks, and the gravitational field spreading beneath the celestial bodies above him was strong enough to suppress thousands of Orcs simultaneously.
"And this gravity..."

Emberlyn could feel the force pressing over the battlefield even from where she sat, although her own aura prevented it from affecting her body, while the same protection naturally extended over the tree branch beneath her.
She remained silent for another moment before looking toward the twenty-foot figure standing beneath the miniature Solar System.
"Not even demonic cultivation should be able to give someone this kind of strength."
Her earlier theory suddenly seemed far less convincing.
If Luke’s rapid growth had truly come from some crude sacrificial method similar to those used by Demon Whisperer cultists, then how was he producing power like this?
Emberlyn continued staring at him as another question replaced the suspicions she had formed earlier.
"Then how did Luke obtain this power?"

chapters.title: Chapter 369: The Surface Became Barren—So They Went Below?!
paragraphs: "Playtime is over."
Luke muttered those words before releasing the asteroids that had been rotating throughout his manifested Solar System, sending them raining toward every part of the battlefield.

The Orcs trapped beneath the gravitational pressure immediately widened their eyes, and whatever courage they had maintained until now finally collapsed when they saw the approaching celestial bodies.
"No!"
"Captain, save us!"
"CAPTAIN!"
Their terrified voices carried toward the inner section of the outpost, where Yarvokh had been sitting only moments earlier.
Inside the large tent, the captured serpent women also heard those desperate cries, and their faces turned pale when they sensed the numerous projectiles descending outside.
"What is this?"

Yarvokh abruptly rose from his seat and looked upward, confusion appearing across his face when he sensed the miniature Solar System hanging over the battlefield and the numerous objects now falling from it.
The moment he realized those projectiles were heading directly toward his army, his expression changed.
"Don’t you dare!"
BOOM—!
Yarvokh kicked against the ground and launched himself forward like a cannonball, while the force behind his movement tore apart the tent behind him and blasted everything nearby away.
Several of the captured serpent women were only F-Rank and E-Rank, and the shockwave struck them before they could protect themselves, shredding their bodies apart and killing them instantly.

A few prisoners positioned farther away were thrown across the ground instead, and when they saw their companions, friends, and loved ones—who had already suffered humiliation at the Orcs’ hands—suddenly torn apart by Yarvokh’s careless movement, their screams of grief and fury echoed through the ruined tent.
"AAAAH!"
Yarvokh didn’t even turn around.
He was already rushing toward the C-Rank section of the battlefield, because after judging the distance between himself and the Orc army outside, he knew there was no possibility of saving everyone.
By the time he reached the D-Ranks, the asteroids would already have landed.
So he chose the group he could still protect.
"HAAH!"
Yarvokh reached the C-Rank Orcs just as the first celestial projectiles descended and immediately unleashed a barrage of punches.
BANG! BOOM! BAM!

Every punch shattered an incoming asteroid before it could strike the wall, scattering burning fragments and broken pieces of cosmic matter through the air while the C-Rank Orcs beneath him finally felt a trace of relief.
"Captain!"
Several called toward him excitedly, while others remained unable to properly react because Luke’s gravitational pressure was still weighing heavily upon their bodies.
Yarvokh ignored their voices and turned toward the battlefield outside.
His expression immediately became ugly.
BOOM!
Another asteroid crashed into the Orc army.
BOOM—!
Then another.

Different elemental energies erupted wherever the celestial bodies landed, and groups of D-Rank Orcs vanished beneath the explosions while those still alive could do little more than press themselves against the ground and watch the next projectile descend toward them.
"AAAAH!"
"Save me!
"Captain, please save us!"
They couldn’t even properly move beneath the gravity, so every bit of strength they had left was spent forcing those desperate cries from their mouths.
Unfortunately, Yarvokh was too far away.
BOOOOM—!
Another asteroid struck the battlefield and wiped out hundreds more Orcs at once.
Yarvokh clenched his fists hard enough for the muscles along his arms to bulge, then turned toward the distant figure responsible for everything.

Luke remained standing calmly beneath his manifested Solar System, his twenty-foot Titan body covered by Elythos while the golden-white armor reflected the light coming from the celestial bodies overhead.
"You aren’t a dragon."
Yarvokh finally spoke before taking one step forward.
Then another.
His B-Rank body crossed the distance rapidly, and within moments, he appeared directly in front of Luke.

By then, the remaining D-Rank Orcs had already been killed, while Luke had deliberately removed the gravitational pressure affecting the C-Rank Orcs, leaving the two strongest figures on the battlefield facing each other without interference.
Luke looked down slightly.

Yarvokh stood around twelve feet tall, which would have made him imposing compared with most humanoid races, yet beside Luke’s current twenty-foot Titan form, the Orc Captain was forced to raise his head.
"I am something far more dangerous than a dragon."
Luke answered calmly.
Yarvokh looked confused.
’More dangerous than a dragon?’

Although the Orc tribe still understood very little about the civilizations beyond the Endless Forest, everything they had learned since arriving here suggested that Dragons and Demons stood among the strongest races of the outside world.
He couldn’t understand what kind of species this young man believed himself to be.
After a few seconds, Yarvokh shook the thought away.
"Whatever you are, kid, since you’ve already come this far, I’ll give you two choices."
The anger that had covered his face only moments earlier disappeared, replaced by a broad smile that immediately made Luke suspicious.
"Join us..."
Yarvokh paused before his smile widened.
"...or die."
Luke stared at him.
Far in the distance, Emberlyn also became silent.
’Weren’t they trying to murder each other a moment ago?’
Luke genuinely couldn’t understand how Yarvokh had switched from wanting his head to offering him recruitment within such a short period.
Emberlyn’s reaction wasn’t much different, because she had just watched Luke slaughter thousands of Orcs, yet their captain was now casually asking the person responsible to join them.
Yarvokh didn’t care about his speechless reactions.
Once he realized Luke wasn’t a dragon, his thinking had immediately changed.

Dragons were notoriously proud and difficult to control, while this unknown race appeared capable of transforming into giants, wielding strange celestial powers, and allowing someone whose normal aura belonged to D-Rank to suddenly display B-Rank combat strength.
If Yarvokh could bring someone like that into the tribe instead of killing him, the reward could be far greater.

"Joining us will bring you tremendous benefits," Yarvokh continued confidently. "The force you’ve seen here, along with the other Orcs currently operating the edges of Dragon Continent, is nothing more than a scouting force."
The lie came from his mouth without even the slightest hesitation.
Luke blinked.
’A scouting force?’
From what Emberlyn had already told him, several million Orcs had entered Dragon territory, and among them were even A-Rank existences.
However, neither Emberlyn nor Rhaenyra had encountered anything at S-Rank or higher.
Noticing the change in Luke’s expression, Yarvokh immediately assumed his lie had worked.
"Our true forces are still within the Endless Forest, and among them are many powerful existences, including demi-gods..."
He paused deliberately before revealing his final claim.
"...and even gods."
"O_O"
Luke’s expression froze.
’Gods?’
For a moment, the information he had accumulated about Valtharion felt as though it had been thrown into complete disorder.

From everything Luke currently understood, the known civilized world of Valtharion was dominated by only several major intelligent races, excluding whatever unknown civilizations might exist deep within the Endless Forest or beyond the Endless Seas.

There were the Dragons of Kharenthyr, the Elves, the demi-human races belonging to the Beast Empire, the Marinthian sea races, the Vampires, the Humans, along with the Demons who occupied their own continent.

The Marinthians themselves only controlled regions near the safer portions of Valtharion’s seas, because travelling too far beyond those areas became dangerously unpredictable, and even demi-gods could become lost after crossing beyond the protected regions surrounding the known world.
The same mystery surrounded the Endless Forest.

Because the civilizations of these known races occupied only the safer and more explored territories of Valtharion, many people collectively referred to those connected lands as the Mainland, separating them from the unexplored regions extending far beyond established civilization.
Luke had always known that the Endless Forest could hide unknown species and powerful beings.
But gods?
That was something completely different.

As for Goblins, Luke hadn’t encountered any on the Mainland, although large portions of its wilderness were filled with beasts whose true origin remained unknown, with most races simply assuming that many of them had originally emerged from the Endless Forest.

That alone was enough for everyone to understand that the Endless Forest concealed far more than ordinary monsters, because forgotten races, hidden tribes, and countless other mysteries were believed to exist within its depths.

Decades ago, that belief had been proven in the worst possible way when a group of demi-gods ventured deep into the Endless Forest and later encountered the corpse of a true god, only for every one of them to die after that corpse awakened.
’Maybe they really were killed by a god... or perhaps there are other demi-gods living down there as well.’

For the first time since arriving in Valtharion, Luke genuinely felt as though everything he knew about this world barely scratched its surface, especially now that someone was claiming living gods might still exist somewhere beneath it.
Whether Yarvokh’s words were actually true was another matter.
Luke looked directly at him.
"Are there really gods among your race?"
"Of course there are."
Yarvokh answered without hesitation, then added, "We simply don’t know whether they are capable of coming up to the surface anymore."
He didn’t seem concerned about revealing that much, because anyone reckless enough to travel deep into the Endless Forest could eventually learn similar information for themselves.
"Our ancestors said the upper surface became barren long ago, which was why many of them entered the Endless Forest and developed their civilizations there."

chapters.title: Chapter 370: Yarvokh Freezes After Hearing Luke’s Title!
paragraphs: What Yarvokh conveniently chose not to mention was that his own group belonged to only one ordinary Orc tribe, one that wasn’t even considered particularly noble among their race and had eventually been defeated by stronger tribes before fleeing toward the Dragon Continent.
Still, he wasn’t lying about everything.
The Orc race truly did possess gods somewhere within the Endless Forest, even if those gods had nothing to do with Yarvokh’s personal ancestry.
High above the battlefield, Emberlyn had been listening to their conversation from the tree branch, and Yarvokh’s claim left her visibly stunned.
’Gods are still living inside Valtharion?’
Another possibility quickly entered her mind.
’Or are they refugees from the Twilight Era?’

According to what her grandfather had taught her, the great conflict among the gods had ended with Valtharion removing them from the world so that it could recover from the damage caused during that era.
Yet Yarvokh’s claim that the upper surface had once become barren made Emberlyn consider another possibility.
’Maybe Valtharion didn’t expel every one of them.’
She remained silent while thinking through the possibility.
’Maybe some gods left by themselves because there was nothing left here for them after the war.’
That explanation wasn’t impossible.

If Valtharion had truly been devastated during the Twilight Era and much of its resources had been exhausted, then perhaps some gods had simply abandoned the world in search of richer places rather than being personally forced out.
It even raised another uncomfortable possibility.
’Was that shortage of resources part of the reason the gods started fighting in the first place?’
Emberlyn couldn’t be certain, and the more she thought about it, the more questions appeared.
’If some of them really went outside, then why haven’t they returned back to the Valatharion?’
That question reminded her of another strange detail from the current Hero Era.
No genuine god had been born on Valtharion during this era.
Powerful beings had reached the demi-god stage, yet all of them appeared to stop there regardless of how long they cultivated.
’Is Valtharion preventing them from becoming gods, or does reaching godhood require something that this world no longer possesses?’

Emberlyn finally shook her head and forced herself to stop thinking about it, because the disappearance of the gods and the true history of the previous eras clearly contained far more mysteries than what had been passed down through ordinary records.
Below her, Luke had reached a similar problem from a much more practical perspective.

Even if everything the orc captain said was true, those gods apparently couldn’t freely come to the surface, which meant attacking these Orcs wouldn’t immediately bring a god crashing down upon his head.
Still, if Luke eventually entered the Endless Forest himself, slaughtering part of their race now could easily make those hidden powers his enemies later.
’A god is still way too much for me right now.’
Luke sighed inwardly.
He now had two realistic choices.
Kill them.
Or spare them.
Joining them wasn’t even worth considering.
’Heh, I also have a goddess behind me.’
A faint sense of pride appeared in Luke’s thoughts, although he immediately remembered that the Goddess of Light still hadn’t actually given him the blessing he was supposed to receive.
Instead, most of what he had gotten from her involvement so far consisted of troublesome trials, dangerous situations, and the Origin Fragments that nearly killed him several times.
’Well... I guess those still count as gifts in their own way.’
Joining an Orc tribe after becoming the Hero of Light probably wasn’t the brightest idea either, especially if the Saintess eventually heard about it and decided to personally come after him.
At that moment, a familiar System screen appeared before his eyes.
[Luke, think about the present.]

[You currently need those kills if you want to reach C-Rank. If you keep hesitating over enemies who may or may not become a problem in the distant future, you won’t even be able to compete with the other Heroes.]
The System paused before adding another line.
[And you can forget about conquering that dragon wife of yours as well.]
Luke’s expression immediately changed.
’...You really know where to hit.’
Still, he couldn’t deny the logic.

Even if killing these Orcs made enemies for him later, the gods he mentioned apparently couldn’t come to the surface freely, while any demi-gods attempting to invade the Mainland would still have to deal with the established demi-gods already protecting the different races.
A foreign demi-god couldn’t simply walk into another race’s territory without provoking retaliation.
Luke gave a small nod.
’You’re right. Getting stronger matters more right now.’
Once his decision was made, he looked back toward Yarvokh and smiled.
"Sorry, dude, but I already have a goddess behind me."
Yarvokh’s expression immediately changed.
’A goddess... on the surface?’
Before he could ask anything, Luke casually added the next sentence.
"I’m the Hero of Light."
Yarvokh froze.
For several seconds, he simply stared at Luke as though the figure standing before him had suddenly transformed into something far more dangerous than the giant he had already witnessed.
’A Hero... one of their puppets!’
Ancient warnings immediately surfaced in his mind.
The prophecies weren’t known only among Orcs, because many races living deep within the Endless Forest had preserved similar stories across generations.
’History will repeat itself when the puppets of those beings descend upon Valtharion again.’
’The outsiders who don’t belong to this world.’
Those stories had never described the Heroes as saviors.
To many of the races living within the Endless Forest, their previous arrival had marked the beginning of disasters that eventually claimed countless lives, including the deaths of gods.
Yarvokh’s expression turned increasingly ugly as he finally understood what Luke’s presence meant.
’So they’ve already started bringing them back.’
His earlier thoughts about recruitment disappeared completely.
’No wonder the royal Orc tribes never bothered conquering the surface and instead kept strengthening themselves below.’
For the first time, Yarvokh began wondering whether those higher-ranking Orcs had known this moment was coming long before his own tribe ever reached the Dragon Continent.
Perhaps they hadn’t ignored the surface because they were afraid of Dragons.
Perhaps they were simply waiting.
’The countdown has already begun.’
Killing intent gradually filled Yarvokh’s gaze as he looked toward Luke.
If Luke truly served one of the divine beings outside Valtharion, then he wasn’t merely an outsider anymore.
He belonged to the enemy.

Yarvokh remembered the teachings passed down from his ancestors, according to which the gods who remained within the Endless Forest were the ones who had stayed behind to protect Valtharion, while those who abandoned the world and fled beyond it were remembered as traitors.
’Those traitors...’
Luke noticed the abrupt change in Yarvokh’s expression and became confused.
’Is this because I mentioned the Goddess?’
He had unknowingly guessed correctly, although he had no way of understanding the deeper reason yet.
Luke tilted his head slightly.
"No more recruitment?"
Yarvokh didn’t answer immediately.
The crimson tattoos covering his body suddenly ignited with brilliant red light, spreading across his skin as his aura surged upward and the ground beneath his feet began cracking under the pressure.
When he finally spoke, his voice carried none of the friendliness from moments earlier.
"YOU WILL DIE HERE!"
The surrounding air trembled as Yarvokh raised his head and roared directly at Luke.
"AND I, YARVOKH, THE ORC CAPTAIN OF THIS OUTPOST, WILL BE THE ONE WHO SLAUGHTERS THE TRAITOR’S PUPPET!"

Still, he wasn’t lying about everything.
The Orc race truly did possess gods somewhere within the Endless Forest, even if those gods had nothing to do with Yarvokh’s personal ancestry.
High above the battlefield, Emberlyn had been listening to their conversation from the tree branch, and Yarvokh’s claim left her visibly stunned.
’Gods are still living inside Valtharion?’
Another possibility quickly entered her mind.
’Or are they refugees from the Twilight Era?’

According to what her grandfather had taught her, the great conflict among the gods had ended with Valtharion removing them from the world so that it could recover from the damage caused during that era.
Yet Yarvokh’s claim that the upper surface had once become barren made Emberlyn consider another possibility.
’Maybe Valtharion didn’t expel every one of them.’
She remained silent while thinking through the possibility.
’Maybe some gods left by themselves because there was nothing left here for them after the war.’
That explanation wasn’t impossible.

If Valtharion had truly been devastated during the Twilight Era and much of its resources had been exhausted, then perhaps some gods had simply abandoned the world in search of richer places rather than being personally forced out.
It even raised another uncomfortable possibility.
’Was that shortage of resources part of the reason the gods started fighting in the first place?’
Emberlyn couldn’t be certain, and the more she thought about it, the more questions appeared.
’If some of them really went outside, then why haven’t they returned back to the Valatharion?’
That question reminded her of another strange detail from the current Hero Era.
No genuine god had been born on Valtharion during this era.
Powerful beings had reached the demi-god stage, yet all of them appeared to stop there regardless of how long they cultivated.
’Is Valtharion preventing them from becoming gods, or does reaching godhood require something that this world no longer possesses?’

Emberlyn finally shook her head and forced herself to stop thinking about it, because the disappearance of the gods and the true history of the previous eras clearly contained far more mysteries than what had been passed down through ordinary records.
Below her, Luke had reached a similar problem from a much more practical perspective.

Even if everything the orc captain said was true, those gods apparently couldn’t freely come to the surface, which meant attacking these Orcs wouldn’t immediately bring a god crashing down upon his head.
Still, if Luke eventually entered the Endless Forest himself, slaughtering part of their race now could easily make those hidden powers his enemies later.
’A god is still way too much for me right now.’
Luke sighed inwardly.
He now had two realistic choices.
Kill them.
Or spare them.
Joining them wasn’t even worth considering.
’Heh, I also have a goddess behind me.’
A faint sense of pride appeared in Luke’s thoughts, although he immediately remembered that the Goddess of Light still hadn’t actually given him the blessing he was supposed to receive.
Instead, most of what he had gotten from her involvement so far consisted of troublesome trials, dangerous situations, and the Origin Fragments that nearly killed him several times.
’Well...
I guess those still count as gifts in their own way.’
Joining an Orc tribe after becoming the Hero of Light probably wasn’t the brightest idea either, especially if the Saintess eventually heard about it and decided to personally come after him.
At that moment, a familiar System screen appeared before his eyes.
[Luke, think about the present.]
[You currently need those kills if you want to reach C-Rank.
If you keep hesitating over enemies who may or may not become a problem in the distant future, you won’t even be able to compete with the other Heroes.]
The System paused before adding another line.
[And you can forget about conquering that dragon wife of yours as well.]
Luke’s expression immediately changed.
’...You really know where to hit.’
Still, he couldn’t deny the logic.

Even if killing these Orcs made enemies for him later, the gods he mentioned apparently couldn’t come to the surface freely, while any demi-gods attempting to invade the Mainland would still have to deal with the established demi-gods already protecting the different races.
A foreign demi-god couldn’t simply walk into another race’s territory without provoking retaliation.

’You’re right.
Getting stronger matters more right now.’

"Sorry, dude, but I already have a goddess behind me."

’A goddess... on the surface?’
Before he could ask anything, Luke casually added the next sentence.
"I’m the Hero of Light."
Yarvokh froze.
For several seconds, he simply stared at Luke as though the figure standing before him had suddenly transformed into something far more dangerous than the giant he had already witnessed.
’A Hero... one of their puppets!’
Ancient warnings immediately surfaced in his mind.
The prophecies weren’t known only among Orcs, because many races living deep within the Endless Forest had preserved similar stories across generations.
’History will repeat itself when the puppets of those beings descend upon Valtharion again.’
