chapters.title: Chapter 371: Yarvokh Summons the Wrath of an Orc Ancestor!
paragraphs: Yarvokh let out a furious shout, and the red tattoo across his body suddenly flared with crimson light as a surge of energy erupted from him, gathering above his head before taking the shape of a fifty-foot-tall Orc phantom.
The entire phantom was formed from red energy, resembling an Orc warrior, except that two horns protruded from either side of its head, giving it a rather intimidating appearance.
"Feel the wrath of the Orc ancestor!" Yarvokh declared, and under Luke’s curious gaze, his body slowly floated upward before merging directly into the chest of the towering phantom.
"A summoning skill?" Luke muttered with interest, observing the transformation as Yarvokh’s aura continued rising until it reached the peak of Early B-Rank.
’It seems almost everyone at higher ranks possesses some kind of technique that can temporarily increase their strength beyond their actual realm.’

"Whatever," Luke murmured without showing much concern, although his nonchalant attitude only angered Yarvokh further, causing both his eyes and those of the ancestral phantom to glow a deeper shade of red.
"Insolent!"

A heavy voice suddenly thundered from the phantom’s mouth, although Luke couldn’t quite distinguish whether it belonged to Yarvokh or the ancestral figure, since their presences now seemed almost completely merged.

Before Luke could examine this strange connection any further, Yarvokh suddenly threw a punch toward him, and the fifty-foot-tall phantom immediately followed the exact same movement without the slightest delay, sending its giant fist straight toward Luke.
FWOOOOSH!
Seeing the incoming attack, Luke calmly raised his own fist and punched forward, meeting the phantom’s much larger fist head-on.
BOOOOOOM!

The collision produced a powerful shockwave that swept across the surrounding clearing, scattering loose stones and dust while shaking the nearby trees, and under the force of the impact, both Luke and the Orc phantom were pushed several steps backward.
THUD! THUD! THUD!
"How is this possible?!" Yarvokh exclaimed in disbelief, unable to understand why he still couldn’t overpower a mere D-Rank opponent even after invoking the power of his Orc ancestor.
Meanwhile, Luke casually shook his hand a few times, acknowledging that the previous punch had carried considerable force, before a thought suddenly entered his mind.
’Should I use the inner Cosmic System as well?’
He considered the idea for a moment, since he was currently relying only on his Cosmic Heart Titan form and the buffs provided by his Titan body and armor, without activating any fusion.

Although Titan Fusion could increase his strength considerably, Luke didn’t want to become overly dependent on it, especially since enemies who became familiar with his fighting methods might eventually discover weaknesses they could exploit.
That was also why he had been deliberately practicing with his individual Titan forms, attempting to improve their combat effectiveness without constantly relying on fusion.
"Let’s do it."

Having made his decision, Luke began constructing a Cosmic System within his body while simultaneously withdrawing the one he had manifested outside, causing the celestial bodies that had been floating above the battlefield to gradually disappear.
Yarvokh immediately noticed the change, and after looking upward and finding that the strange celestial bodies were gone, a confused expression appeared on his face.
"Are you giving up already, Hero of Light?" he asked, wondering why Luke would suddenly withdraw something that had seemingly been supporting his strength.
Hearing those words, Luke simply smiled before answering in his usual carefree manner.
"Nah, I’m just making it more fun."

With that, he suddenly kicked the ground beneath his feet, releasing enough force to split the earth apart as fractures rapidly spread outward, tearing through the surrounding soil and stone until the cracks extended across a hundred meters.
RRRRRUUUUMBLE!!!

Because of the sudden fracture spreading beneath them, Yarvokh’s footing shifted for the briefest instant, and that tiny imbalance was all Luke needed, because the moment the Orc phantom’s weight dipped to one side, he shot forward like a released arrow.
FWOOOSH!

His figure blurred across the torn ground, and before Yarvokh could fully steady the giant phantom, Luke had already arrived in front of it and drove a straight punch into its abdomen, while the inner cosmic system within his body rotated in perfect coordination, causing a surge of force to flow through his arm, shoulder, spine, and legs all at once.
BOOOOM!

The red phantom’s entire torso bent inward from the impact, and the shockwave that followed blasted outward in a rough circle, uprooting trees and sending broken bark, dust, and loose stones flying across the battlefield, while the cracked earth within a hundred meters caved further under the pressure.
"GRAAAH!"

Yarvokh roared and retaliated at once, as the phantom’s oversized elbow came crashing down toward Luke’s back, yet Luke twisted his body with calm precision, slid half a step to the side, and let the strike smash into the ground instead.
KRAAAAAK!

The earth burst apart, and a jagged trench spread outward as rock fragments shot into the air, but Luke had already turned with the motion and drove his knee into the phantom’s ribs, following it with a left hook that snapped its head to the side before the first impact had even settled.
BAAAM! BOOOM!
The two consecutive blows made the red energy body ripple violently, and even the horns atop its head trembled as the force traveled through it.

At the rear, the surrounding C-Rank Orcs stared with tightening expressions, because none of them had expected Yarvokh, after invoking the ancestor phantom, to be driven back like this by a D-Rank giant relying purely on physical combat.
"How is he still matching Lord Yarvokh?"
"That giant strength rose again..."
"It is not just strength, his movements also changed."
Their unease spread quickly, especially when they saw Luke take the next counterattack head-on.

With a furious bellow, Yarvokh swung both arms together, and the phantom copied him perfectly, bringing down a two-fisted hammer strike that carried enough force to flatten boulders, yet Luke planted his feet, tightened his stance, and raised both arms upward, while the celestial bodies within his inner cosmic system shifted once more and reinforced his stability so thoroughly that his body seemed rooted into the land itself.
BOOOOOOM!

The collision made the surrounding forest shudder, and the ground beneath Luke’s feet sank several inches, but his body did not bend, his knees did not collapse, and after receiving the full weight of the strike, he simply exhaled through clenched teeth and pushed upward.
"HAAAH!"

The red phantom’s arms were forced back, and Luke stepped forward through the lingering shockwave before slamming a shoulder bash into its chest, then followed with a short-range punch into its jaw that lifted the giant head slightly upward.
THUD! BAAAM!

Yarvokh’s expression twisted within the phantom’s chest, because he could now feel the difference more clearly than anyone else, as Luke’s raw power had not merely become heavier, but more complete, with each movement carrying sharper control, stronger footing, tighter force transmission, and far less waste than before.

Not far away, Nyx watched with visible interest, his eyes fixed on Luke’s posture and sequence of strikes. "He is learning quickly," he said, as his gaze followed the way Luke shifted force through his frame. "At first he was simply strong, but now he is starting to use that strength properly."

Caelith gave a slow nod, her attention remaining on Luke’s shoulders, hips, and legs as he fought. "The inner system is helping him redistribute power through the body," she said. "His punches are not only harder, they are cleaner, and even his grip and balance have improved."

Sevaroth floated nearby and observed the red phantom with an unreadable look, though his interest soon returned to Luke. "He is also becoming more comfortable fighting without relying on fusion," he murmured. "That is better for him in the long run."
Myrkhal, as usual, said nothing, and simply watched in silence.

chapters.title: Chapter 372: Luke Finally Responds to the ‘Puppet of the Gods’ Accusation!
paragraphs: Meanwhile, Emberlyn’s icy-blue draconic eyes remained fixed on the battlefield, and the surprise on her face became harder and harder to conceal, because she had already known Luke was strong for his rank, but seeing him physically overpower a B-Rank Orc using a transformed battle state still felt absurd.
’He was not this stable before...’

That was the part that drew her attention the most, because Luke was not flailing around with borrowed strength, nor was he pushing himself recklessly for a single clash, and instead seemed to be growing more precise with every exchange, as though he were gradually adjusting his body to a new and more dangerous standard.
So seeing this she became confused, because she didn’t know, that Luke was using inner cosmic system.
Yarvokh clearly realized it as well, which was why his anger became more violent.
"ROOOOAR!"

The phantom lunged forward and threw a barrage of punches, and this time Luke did not meet every strike directly, but moved into the attack pattern itself, slipping past one fist, deflecting the next with his forearm, ducking beneath a sweeping backhand, and driving an elbow into the giant arm joint before spinning out of range and kicking the phantom’s knee.
BAAAM! THUD! KRAK!

The phantom staggered half a step, and before it could recover, Luke pivoted on his heel and launched a roundhouse kick into its ribs with enough force to unleash another shockwave across the battlefield.
BOOOOM!
Several nearby trees snapped from the pressure alone, while others bent sharply before collapsing sideways into the fractured terrain.

Yarvokh snarled, then suddenly clasped both hands together and brought them down like a giant axe strike, forcing Luke to cross his arms and block. The impact still pushed him backward this time, dragging his boots through the dirt for dozens of meters, yet even while sliding, Luke remained balanced, and the inner cosmic system within him continued rotating with cold efficiency.
SHRIIIIK!
His feet carved two long lines across the ruined ground, and once the backward momentum weakened, he pressed down, halted instantly, and burst forward again.
FWOOOSH!

He crossed the distance in a breath and seized the phantom’s forearm with both hands. The moment his grip tightened, the miniature celestial bodies inside him shifted again, causing the muscles of his arms, shoulders, and back to tense under a fresh surge of force.
Yarvokh’s expression changed.
Because Luke did not merely stop the arm.
He twisted it.
KRRRRRK!
The red energy limb warped unnaturally, and cracks of unstable light spread from Luke’s hands along the phantom’s arm all the way to the shoulder.
"GHHHAAAH!"
Yarvokh’s pained roar echoed from within the chest of the giant phantom, and before he could pull away, Luke stepped in and slammed his forehead into the phantom’s face.
BAAAM!
The head jerked backward, one horn partly fractured, and Luke immediately followed with three brutal body blows, each one landing lower than the last.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOOOM!
The first crushed the chest inward.
The second made the torso convulse.
The third sent a wave of crimson cracks racing through the phantom’s entire frame.
At this point, even the C-Rank Orcs could no longer hide their alarm.
"It is breaking!"
"Lord Yarvokh’s ancestor form is breaking!"
"How can a D-Rank body endure this?"

Their voices carried panic now, because the battlefield had long since expanded beyond the initial area, with torn trenches, shattered boulders, and uprooted trees already stretching well beyond a hundred meters, while several heavier collisions had sent damage rippling across nearly five hundred meters of land, and although Yarvokh’s attacks were powerful enough to leave deep marks across the battlefield, the wider destruction was clearly being driven by Luke’s side of the exchange.
Yarvokh himself felt it more bitterly than any observer.

Every time he struck Luke, the giant either endured it as though it were tolerable or redirected the force before countering with something heavier, sharper, and more punishing, and the longer the fight continued, the more he felt as though he were not battling a normal giant at all, but some compact monster wearing the giant skin.
"No..." Yarvokh growled through blood-stained teeth. "No, this should not be possible..."

Luke did not answer immediately, because in the middle of battle, he had no interest in wasting his breath on words that would change nothing, and after avoiding another clawed swing from the phantom, he stepped inside its reach, drove his fist upward into its chin, and then spoke only once the giant body reeled backward.
"It is possible," he said calmly, "because you are not the only one getting stronger."
The next instant, Luke bent his knees and exploded upward.
BOOOOM!

The ground beneath him collapsed in a burst of dirt and rock, and he rose high enough to reach the phantom’s upper chest before drawing back his right arm, while inside him the inner cosmic system rotated to a sharper rhythm, causing the aligned force of his body to condense into that single fist.
Even Nyx’s expression shifted at that.
Caelith’s gaze sharpened.
Sevaroth fell silent.
And Emberlyn’s breath caught for a moment.
Luke’s punch came down.
BAAAAAAAAAAM!

The blow landed directly against the center of the red phantom’s chest, right where Yarvokh’s body was fused within it, and the impact this time was different from the previous ones, because rather than merely knocking the giant backward, it sent a dense wave of force straight through the entire construct.
For half a second, everything seemed to freeze.
Then the cracks spread.
KRRRRAAAAAK!

They raced from the point of impact to the shoulders, down both arms, across the torso, through the legs, and up toward the horned head, until the entire fifty-foot phantom became a web of crimson fractures.
Yarvokh’s eyes widened.
But Luke did not stop.
With his left hand, he caught the giant by the neck, pulled the collapsing phantom slightly forward, and then drove a final punch into the already-broken chest.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The ancestor phantom exploded.

A storm of shattered red energy erupted across the battlefield like broken glass made of light, and the blast flattened the remaining trees closest to them while loose boulders were hurled away and chunks of earth rolled across the ruined ground.

At the center of that destruction, Yarvokh’s real body was blasted out of the phantom’s chest and thrown through the air like a broken rag, his entire frame bloodied, his skin cracked in multiple places, and his mouth spilling a spray of blood before he crashed across the torn battlefield.
THUD! THUD! SKRRAAAK!

His body bounced once, then dragged violently across the fractured earth before finally coming to a stop amid broken stone and uprooted roots, while the last fragments of the destroyed phantom dissolved into the air above him.
"Ugghh... It can’t be..." Yarvokh muttered in disbelief while clutching his fractured, bloodied chest, struggling to comprehend how he had been defeated so thoroughly.
"I was meant to be supreme."
His breathing grew increasingly ragged as blood continued leaking from his wounds, yet the unwillingness in his eyes remained.
"I was supposed to bring glory to my tribe."
THUD.
At that moment, the sound of footsteps reached him, and Yarvokh slowly raised his head, finding Luke approaching through the ruined battlefield.
THUD. THUD.
With each approaching step, different emotions passed through Yarvokh’s bloodied eyes as he stared at the twenty-foot-tall armored figure.
’If I had been as strong as him, would we still have been forced to flee our home?’

Unfortunately, no matter how much he wished otherwise, the reality was already before him, and realizing how powerless he had been against Luke, Yarvokh couldn’t help letting out a self-mocking laugh.
"Heh... The puppets of those gods really are strong."
"COUGH! COUGH!"
Before he could say anything further, another violent coughing fit seized him, causing fresh blood to spill from his mouth while his already deteriorating condition worsened.
THUD.
Luke continued approaching without showing any concern for his condition, and after finally arriving before the wounded Orc, he stopped and looked down at him.
"I don’t know shit about these puppets of the gods," Luke said casually, making Yarvokh raise his head to look directly at the armored giant towering above him.

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Emberlyn’s icy-blue draconic eyes remained fixed on the battlefield, and the surprise on her face became harder and harder to conceal, because she had already known Luke was strong for his rank, but seeing him physically overpower a B-Rank Orc using a transformed battle state still felt absurd.
’He was not this stable before...’

That was the part that drew her attention the most, because Luke was not flailing around with borrowed strength, nor was he pushing himself recklessly for a single clash, and instead seemed to be growing more precise with every exchange, as though he were gradually adjusting his body to a new and more dangerous standard.
So seeing this she became confused, because she didn’t know, that Luke was using inner cosmic system.
Yarvokh clearly realized it as well, which was why his anger became more violent.
"ROOOOAR!"

The phantom lunged forward and threw a barrage of punches, and this time Luke did not meet every strike directly, but moved into the attack pattern itself, slipping past one fist, deflecting the next with his forearm, ducking beneath a sweeping backhand, and driving an elbow into the giant arm joint before spinning out of range and kicking the phantom’s knee.
BAAAM!
THUD!
KRAK!

The phantom staggered half a step, and before it could recover, Luke pivoted on his heel and launched a roundhouse kick into its ribs with enough force to unleash another shockwave across the battlefield.
BOOOOM!
Several nearby trees snapped from the pressure alone, while others bent sharply before collapsing sideways into the fractured terrain.
Yarvokh snarled, then suddenly clasped both hands together and brought them down like a giant axe strike, forcing Luke to cross his arms and block.

The impact still pushed him backward this time, dragging his boots through the dirt for dozens of meters, yet even while sliding, Luke remained balanced, and the inner cosmic system within him continued rotating with cold efficiency.
SHRIIIIK!
His feet carved two long lines across the ruined ground, and once the backward momentum weakened, he pressed down, halted instantly, and burst forward again.
FWOOOSH!
He crossed the distance in a breath and seized the phantom’s forearm with both hands.
The moment his grip tightened, the miniature celestial bodies inside him shifted again, causing the muscles of his arms, shoulders, and back to tense under a fresh surge of force.
Yarvokh’s expression changed.
Because Luke did not merely stop the arm.
He twisted it.
KRRRRRK!
The red energy limb warped unnaturally, and cracks of unstable light spread from Luke’s hands along the phantom’s arm all the way to the shoulder.
"GHHHAAAH!"
Yarvokh’s pained roar echoed from within the chest of the giant phantom, and before he could pull away, Luke stepped in and slammed his forehead into the phantom’s face.
BAAAM!
The head jerked backward, one horn partly fractured, and Luke immediately followed with three brutal body blows, each one landing lower than the last.
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOOOM!
The first crushed the chest inward.
The second made the torso convulse.
The third sent a wave of crimson cracks racing through the phantom’s entire frame.
At this point, even the C-Rank Orcs could no longer hide their alarm.
"It is breaking!"
"Lord Yarvokh’s ancestor form is breaking!"
"How can a D-Rank body endure this?"

Their voices carried panic now, because the battlefield had long since expanded beyond the initial area, with torn trenches, shattered boulders, and uprooted trees already stretching well beyond a hundred meters, while several heavier collisions had sent damage rippling across nearly five hundred meters of land, and although Yarvokh’s attacks were powerful enough to leave deep marks across the battlefield, the wider destruction was clearly being driven by Luke’s side of the exchange.
Yarvokh himself felt it more bitterly than any observer.

Every time he struck Luke, the giant either endured it as though it were tolerable or redirected the force before countering with something heavier, sharper, and more punishing, and the longer the fight continued, the more he felt as though he were not battling a normal giant at all, but some compact monster wearing the giant skin.
"No..." Yarvokh growled through blood-stained teeth.
"No, this should not be possible..."

Luke did not answer immediately, because in the middle of battle, he had no interest in wasting his breath on words that would change nothing, and after avoiding another clawed swing from the phantom, he stepped inside its reach, drove his fist upward into its chin, and then spoke only once the giant body reeled backward.
"It is possible," he said calmly, "because you are not the only one getting stronger."
The next instant, Luke bent his knees and exploded upward.
BOOOOM!

The ground beneath him collapsed in a burst of dirt and rock, and he rose high enough to reach the phantom’s upper chest before drawing back his right arm, while inside him the inner cosmic system rotated to a sharper rhythm, causing the aligned force of his body to condense into that single fist.
Even Nyx’s expression shifted at that.
Caelith’s gaze sharpened.
Sevaroth fell silent.
And Emberlyn’s breath caught for a moment.
Luke’s punch came down.
BAAAAAAAAAAM!

The blow landed directly against the center of the red phantom’s chest, right where Yarvokh’s body was fused within it, and the impact this time was different from the previous ones, because rather than merely knocking the giant backward, it sent a dense wave of force straight through the entire construct.
For half a second, everything seemed to freeze.
Then the cracks spread.
KRRRRAAAAAK!

They raced from the point of impact to the shoulders, down both arms, across the torso, through the legs, and up toward the horned head, until the entire fifty-foot phantom became a web of crimson fractures.
Yarvokh’s eyes widened.
But Luke did not stop.
With his left hand, he caught the giant by the neck, pulled the collapsing phantom slightly forward, and then drove a final punch into the already-broken chest.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The ancestor phantom exploded.

A storm of shattered red energy erupted across the battlefield like broken glass made of light, and the blast flattened the remaining trees closest to them while loose boulders were hurled away and chunks of earth rolled across the ruined ground.

At the center of that destruction, Yarvokh’s real body was blasted out of the phantom’s chest and thrown through the air like a broken rag, his entire frame bloodied, his skin cracked in multiple places, and his mouth spilling a spray of blood before he crashed across the torn battlefield.
THUD!
THUD!
SKRRAAAK!

His body bounced once, then dragged violently across the fractured earth before finally coming to a stop amid broken stone and uprooted roots, while the last fragments of the destroyed phantom dissolved into the air above him.
"Ugghh...
It can’t be..." Yarvokh muttered in disbelief while clutching his fractured, bloodied chest, struggling to comprehend how he had been defeated so thoroughly.
"I was meant to be supreme."
His breathing grew increasingly ragged as blood continued leaking from his wounds, yet the unwillingness in his eyes remained.
"I was supposed to bring glory to my tribe."
THUD.
At that moment, the sound of footsteps reached him, and Yarvokh slowly raised his head, finding Luke approaching through the ruined battlefield.
THUD.
THUD.
With each approaching step, different emotions passed through Yarvokh’s bloodied eyes as he stared at the twenty-foot-tall armored figure.
’If I had been as strong as him, would we still have been forced to flee our home?’

Unfortunately, no matter how much he wished otherwise, the reality was already before him, and realizing how powerless he had been against Luke, Yarvokh couldn’t help letting out a self-mocking laugh.
"Heh...
The puppets of those gods really are strong."
"COUGH!
COUGH!"
Before he could say anything further, another violent coughing fit seized him, causing fresh blood to spill from his mouth while his already deteriorating condition worsened.
THUD.
Luke continued approaching without showing any concern for his condition, and after finally arriving before the wounded Orc, he stopped and looked down at him.
"I don’t know shit about these puppets of the gods," Luke said casually, making Yarvokh raise his head to look directly at the armored giant towering above him.

chapters.title: Chapter 373: “This Power Doesn’t Belong to Any God.”
paragraphs: His gaze moved toward Luke’s face, which was covered by the plain looking but flawless helmet of his knight armor, before gradually shifting across the rest of his golden-white armored body.
And then he noticed something that made his expression freeze.
’Not a single scratch?’
Despite unleashing everything he had, including the strength of his ancestral phantom, Yarvokh hadn’t managed to leave even the slightest scratch on Luke’s armor.
Realizing this, he let out another bitter laugh, mocking himself for believing that he had actually been fighting on equal footing with this monster.
’Heh... Was that even a fight for him?’
While Yarvokh was still drowning in his thoughts, Luke finally finished speaking.
"But this power doesn’t belong to any god."
He offered no further explanation and simply raised his hand, causing cosmic energy to gather above his palm before taking the shape of a long, sharp spear.
Seeing the weapon forming, Yarvokh immediately understood that his end had arrived, although there was surprisingly no fear left in his bloodied eyes.
Instead, he stared at Luke with the last remnants of his hatred and declared, "You will die for th-!"
PUCHI!

Unfortunately, Luke had no interest in listening to his baseless threats and directly thrust the cosmic spear through Yarvokh’s throat, piercing it completely and cutting off whatever else the Orc might have wanted to say.

After all, from what Yarvokh had revealed earlier, even the gods residing within the Endless Forest apparently couldn’t freely descend upon the surface, so Luke saw little reason to fear them merely because he had killed an Orc Captain.
’Well, unless those gods have some other method of attacking me, like placing a curse.’
That possibility briefly crossed his mind, although Luke soon dismissed it, since worrying about what some distant gods might or might not do wasn’t going to help him right now.
Instead, his attention returned to Yarvokh’s body, which had already begun undergoing the familiar transformation brought about by "The Eternal Origin Zero".
The remaining blood flowed back into the corpse as the body gradually dissolved, and within a short time, a crimson Blood Essence Pill appeared before Luke.
Compared to the D-Rank pills he had previously obtained, this one was slightly larger, while the alluring sensation it released was also noticeably stronger.
Interestingly, despite being able to sense that attraction, Luke himself didn’t feel any desire to consume it, unlike the Orcs who had previously been drawn toward these blood pills.
FWOOOSH!
The next instant, the crimson pill dissolved into a stream of blood-colored energy before entering his body, where it was immediately absorbed by his cultivation technique.
"Good." Luke nodded with satisfaction before turning his attention toward the surrounding battlefield, intending to eliminate the remaining C-Rank Orcs and collect their Blood Essence as well.
However, after sweeping his gaze across the broken walls, shattered ground, and ruined surroundings, he suddenly realized something was wrong.
"Huh? Where are they?"
Luke looked around again, only to discover that every C-Rank Orc who had previously been present in the outpost had disappeared.
"Sigh... Bad luck."
He shook his head regretfully, feeling rather unfortunate that so many valuable cultivation resources had managed to escape while he was occupied with Yarvokh.
Moreover, those surviving Orcs would undoubtedly inform the rest of their tribe about him, although what Luke didn’t know was that his assumption was already becoming reality.
"Run faster!"

Some distance away from the destroyed outpost, Elgrun was hurriedly making his way through the forest, pushing aside bushes and avoiding fallen branches while the remaining C-Rank Orcs followed closely behind him.
"That monster! We have to bring this information back to our tribe!" Elgrun muttered anxiously, occasionally glancing behind him to ensure that the terrifying giant hadn’t decided to pursue them.
"One of the puppets of those traitorous gods has appeared here, right at the edge of the Dragon Continent!"

His expression remained ugly as he recalled the battle he had witnessed, especially how Yarvokh’s ancestral phantom had been completely overwhelmed despite possessing the strength of a Peak Early B-Rank existence.
Meanwhile, one of the C-Rank Orcs running behind him suddenly spoke.
"Elgrun, isn’t running away from battle an act of cowardice? Our warriors have always considered retreating from an enemy dishonorable.
Hearing those words, Elgrun’s mouth twitched violently.
’Battle? That was a freaking massacre!’

He nearly shouted those words aloud, although he managed to restrain himself, since explaining the difference between courage and stupidity to these muscle-headed warriors would probably take longer than escaping the forest itself.

After all, Elgrun had always believed that Orc Shamans like himself, who spent their lives studying magic and ancient knowledge, possessed considerably more intelligence than ordinary Orc warriors, whose first solution to almost every problem was to rely on their physical strength.
Even after witnessing their Captain getting thoroughly beaten, these fools were somehow still concerned about whether escaping would damage their honor.
Still, Elgrun knew exactly how to handle them.

"No, we aren’t running away from battle," he explained with a perfectly serious expression while continuing to push through the forest. "We are carrying important information back to our tribe, and once our leaders learn about the appearance of this enemy, our actions will bring us great honor."
The C-Rank Orcs exchanged surprised looks, although Elgrun wasn’t finished yet.
"Besides, Captain Yarvokh wanted us to do this, which is why he personally stayed behind to hold that monster back while we escaped with the information."
Naturally, Elgrun was lying through his teeth, but his confident explanation immediately convinced the other Orcs, who had never imagined that Yarvokh had been thinking so far ahead.
"Oh! So Captain Yarvokh planned this?"

"Of course! Otherwise, why would he fight that monster alone while allowing us to leave?" Elgrun replied without the slightest hesitation, although inwardly he was already cursing these fools for making him waste precious time.
Hearing his explanation, the C-Rank Orcs finally nodded in understanding, and their earlier concerns about dishonor quickly disappeared.
"Then we must hurry! We cannot let Captain Yarvokh’s sacrifice go to waste!"
"Yes, we have to deliver his message!"
Elgrun nodded approvingly before increasing his pace, and the other Orcs immediately followed him through the dense forest, determined to reach their main tribe as quickly as possible.

Their destination was the main territory of their tribe, where the three A-Rank Orcs resided, and Elgrun was already preparing himself to explain how a single Hero of Light had destroyed their entire forward outpost.

chapters.title: Chapter 374: The Survivors Blame Emberlyn for Everything?!
paragraphs: "Whatever," Luke muttered without much concern, even considering that he could probably deal with all of them together, unless some higher-ranked beings decided to intervene.
After dismissing those thoughts, he looked around the devastated battlefield, only to hear several cries of grief coming from deeper inside the Orc outpost.
"AAAH!"
"No! That devil killed my sister!"
Hearing those desperate cries, Luke turned toward their source and took a step forward, instantly appearing within the inner section of the outpost.

There, he discovered numerous beings who resembled demi-humans, possessing snake-like features, although their bodies also carried certain draconic characteristics, including patches of scales covering different parts of their skin.
However, their current condition was anything but pleasant.

Fragments of bodies lay scattered across the bloodstained ground, while several snake women were being held in the arms of their male companions, their bodies covered in wounds and cracks that continued bleeding.
Judging by their injuries, Luke could tell that some of them wouldn’t survive much longer, especially since several other snake women were already in similarly terrible conditions.

"You shall live happily without me..." One of the dying women whispered to her lover, who was desperately holding her bloodied body, although despite her worsening condition, she still managed to maintain a gentle smile on her face.

"Why did this happen to us?! We were just living our normal lives!" The man gritted his teeth as tears continued streaming down his face, unable to understand what they had done to deserve such suffering.

At that moment, Emberlyn also appeared beside Luke, and upon seeing the miserable condition of the surviving prisoners, her usually calm expression remained unchanged, although a faint trace of sadness appeared in her icy-blue eyes.

Naturally, the appearance of two newcomers immediately attracted everyone’s attention, and the surviving snake people turned toward them, only to experience an instinctive urge to lower their heads upon noticing Emberlyn.
It was an instinct originating from their bloodlines, making them feel as though they were standing before a being belonging to a superior species.
"A pure dragon..." Someone muttered in astonishment, causing several others to immediately recognize Emberlyn’s identity.
However, rather than feeling relieved, the expressions of many survivors turned ugly, while several of the men even looked at her with undisguised hatred.
"You were supposed to protect us!" One of them suddenly shouted, his voice trembling with anger.
"Weren’t we your subjects?! Why did you allow those monsters to do this to us?!"
Hearing his accusations, the dying wife in his arms hurriedly reached for his hand, looking at him with obvious worry, because provoking a pure dragon could easily result in their deaths.
Unfortunately, after witnessing his wife’s condition and everything that had happened to their people, the man had already lost his composure and no longer cared about the consequences.

The expressions of the other survivors also changed, and although they didn’t openly accuse Emberlyn, the resentment in their eyes made it clear that many of them held her responsible for failing to protect them.
"Sigh..."
Seeing their reactions, Emberlyn could only release a quiet sigh, since she understood why they were so angry, although there was little she could do about what had already happened.

After all, she had only arrived in this region some time ago and had already discovered that the invading Orcs were capturing members of the surrounding demi-human races, even personally rescuing several prisoners during her explorations.

Unfortunately, the Orcs were spread across too many locations for her to eliminate every group by herself, especially since her father had already refused to let her assist her elder sister in dealing with the invasion.
Still, before Emberlyn could say anything in response to their accusations, a loud voice suddenly interrupted everyone.
"Shut up!"
BOOM!
Luke released a portion of his aura along with those words, causing the surviving prisoners to immediately fall silent as the overwhelming pressure descended upon them.
Their faces turned pale with horror, and only now did several of them properly notice the twenty-foot-tall giant standing beside Emberlyn, whose entire body was covered in golden-white knight armor.

Realizing that they had been shouting accusations in front of another powerful existence, the survivors hurriedly lowered their heads, while the anger they had displayed earlier was quickly overwhelmed by fear.
Even the man who had openly accused Emberlyn became silent, instinctively tightening his hold around his dying wife as he looked toward Luke with a frightened expression.
Meanwhile, several of the wounded snake women also became terrified, believing that the armored giant had become offended by their companions’ behavior and was now preparing to kill them.
Even Emberlyn couldn’t help having a similar thought, especially after witnessing how Luke had previously slaughtered the Orcs and refined their bodies into Blood Essence Pills.
’Is he going to kill them as well and use their bodies for cultivation?’
That possibility made her expression change slightly, although before she could decide whether to intervene, Luke had already raised his right hand toward the injured survivors.
Under Emberlyn’s watchful gaze and the frightened eyes of everyone present, he calmly muttered a few words.
"Seal of Closure."

The moment those words escaped Luke’s mouth, the fourth sealing ability of Sevaroth activated, causing numerous thin silver chains to emerge from the air before spreading toward the wounded snake people gathered throughout the outpost.

Seeing the chains approaching them, several survivors instinctively tried to retreat, while those holding their dying loved ones became even more frightened, believing that the armored giant was about to finish them off.
However, before anyone could react further, the silver chains reached their bodies and began wrapping around their open wounds, forming small glowing seals wherever blood was escaping.
OHMMMM!

Under everyone’s astonished gazes, the bleeding suddenly stopped as the torn flesh began drawing together, gradually closing the wounds until even the deep cuts that had previously exposed the flesh beneath their scales were completely sealed.

The same phenomenon occurred throughout the surrounding area, affecting every injured snake woman, while even the men who had suffered cuts and other external injuries from the Orcs’ beatings found their wounds closing before their eyes.
"Huh? What is happening to my body?" One of the wounded men exclaimed in disbelief, hurriedly touching his chest, where a deep cut had disappeared moments earlier.

Meanwhile, the man who had been holding his dying lover suddenly noticed that the blood flowing from her body had stopped, and when he looked down, he discovered that the terrible wounds covering her body were gradually disappearing beneath the silver sealing marks.
"Darling! Your wounds are healing!" he exclaimed excitedly, his earlier grief turning into disbelief as he watched the last of the wounds close.
The snake woman herself seemed equally shocked, and although her body remained weak from the blood she had already lost, the pain from her open wounds had diminished considerably.
"I... I’m still alive?" she whispered, slowly raising her trembling hand toward her lover’s face.
"Yes! You’re alive!" The man immediately embraced her, although he was careful not to squeeze her injured body too tightly.

Similar scenes unfolded among the other survivors as they inspected their newly closed wounds, and once they finally realized what had happened, their gazes gradually returned to the twenty-foot-tall armored giant standing before them.
After a brief hesitation, the man who had previously been crying over his lover lowered his head toward Luke.
"Thank you, my lord! Thank you for saving her life!" he said sincerely, while his lover also struggled to express her gratitude.
Soon, the other survivors followed their example, thanking Luke one after another, although those who had suffered serious injuries still needed support from their companions.
Meanwhile, Emberlyn stood beside Luke with a slightly changed expression, her icy-blue eyes moving between the surviving snake people and the armored figure responsible for saving them.
She had genuinely expected Luke to kill these people, especially considering the terrifying cultivation technique she had witnessed him using against the Orcs.
Instead, he had used one of his abilities to save people who couldn’t offer him anything in return.
’So he really isn’t killing everyone just because he can...’
Thinking this, Emberlyn’s earlier impression of Luke changed slightly, although she still had reservations about his strange cultivation technique.

As for Luke himself, his expression remained as calm as before, seemingly unconcerned by the gratitude directed toward him, while the remaining silver sealing marks gradually faded from the survivors’ bodies.
"Let’s go to the next outpost," Luke said, turning toward Emberlyn after taking one final look at the surviving snake people.

Hearing his words, Emberlyn finally came out of her thoughts and nodded without saying anything, before her body slowly floated upward and she began ascending toward the sky, preparing to lead him toward another Orc outpost.
At the same time, a pair of wings emerged from Luke’s upper back, and with a powerful flap, his twenty-foot-tall armored body rose into the air before he followed Emberlyn.
FWOOOSH!

Watching the two figures gradually disappear into the distant sky, the surviving snake people couldn’t help raising their heads, while one of the men who had previously thanked Luke suddenly muttered.
"Is that young lord going to save more of our people?"
Unfortunately, no one could answer his question, and after a brief silence, they simply continued watching the two disappearing figures with gratitude in their eyes.

Unfortunately, the Orcs were spread across too many locations for her to eliminate every group by herself, especially since her father had already refused to let her assist her elder sister in dealing with the invasion.
Still, before Emberlyn could say anything in response to their accusations, a loud voice suddenly interrupted everyone.
"Shut up!"
BOOM!
Luke released a portion of his aura along with those words, causing the surviving prisoners to immediately fall silent as the overwhelming pressure descended upon them.
Their faces turned pale with horror, and only now did several of them properly notice the twenty-foot-tall giant standing beside Emberlyn, whose entire body was covered in golden-white knight armor.

Realizing that they had been shouting accusations in front of another powerful existence, the survivors hurriedly lowered their heads, while the anger they had displayed earlier was quickly overwhelmed by fear.
Even the man who had openly accused Emberlyn became silent, instinctively tightening his hold around his dying wife as he looked toward Luke with a frightened expression.
Meanwhile, several of the wounded snake women also became terrified, believing that the armored giant had become offended by their companions’ behavior and was now preparing to kill them.
Even Emberlyn couldn’t help having a similar thought, especially after witnessing how Luke had previously slaughtered the Orcs and refined their bodies into Blood Essence Pills.
’Is he going to kill them as well and use their bodies for cultivation?’
That possibility made her expression change slightly, although before she could decide whether to intervene, Luke had already raised his right hand toward the injured survivors.
Under Emberlyn’s watchful gaze and the frightened eyes of everyone present, he calmly muttered a few words.
"Seal of Closure."

The moment those words escaped Luke’s mouth, the fourth sealing ability of Sevaroth activated, causing numerous thin silver chains to emerge from the air before spreading toward the wounded snake people gathered throughout the outpost.

Seeing the chains approaching them, several survivors instinctively tried to retreat, while those holding their dying loved ones became even more frightened, believing that the armored giant was about to finish them off.
However, before anyone could react further, the silver chains reached their bodies and began wrapping around their open wounds, forming small glowing seals wherever blood was escaping.
OHMMMM!

Under everyone’s astonished gazes, the bleeding suddenly stopped as the torn flesh began drawing together, gradually closing the wounds until even the deep cuts that had previously exposed the flesh beneath their scales were completely sealed.

The same phenomenon occurred throughout the surrounding area, affecting every injured snake woman, while even the men who had suffered cuts and other external injuries from the Orcs’ beatings found their wounds closing before their eyes.
"Huh?
What is happening to my body?" One of the wounded men exclaimed in disbelief, hurriedly touching his chest, where a deep cut had disappeared moments earlier.

Meanwhile, the man who had been holding his dying lover suddenly noticed that the blood flowing from her body had stopped, and when he looked down, he discovered that the terrible wounds covering her body were gradually disappearing beneath the silver sealing marks.
"Darling!
Your wounds are healing!" he exclaimed excitedly, his earlier grief turning into disbelief as he watched the last of the wounds close.
The snake woman herself seemed equally shocked, and although her body remained weak from the blood she had already lost, the pain from her open wounds had diminished considerably.
I’m still alive?" she whispered, slowly raising her trembling hand toward her lover’s face.
"Yes!
You’re alive!" The man immediately embraced her, although he was careful not to squeeze her injured body too tightly.

Similar scenes unfolded among the other survivors as they inspected their newly closed wounds, and once they finally realized what had happened, their gazes gradually returned to the twenty-foot-tall armored giant standing before them.
After a brief hesitation, the man who had previously been crying over his lover lowered his head toward Luke.
"Thank you, my lord!
Thank you for saving her life!" he said sincerely, while his lover also struggled to express her gratitude.
Soon, the other survivors followed their example, thanking Luke one after another, although those who had suffered serious injuries still needed support from their companions.
Meanwhile, Emberlyn stood beside Luke with a slightly changed expression, her icy-blue eyes moving between the surviving snake people and the armored figure responsible for saving them.
She had genuinely expected Luke to kill these people, especially considering the terrifying cultivation technique she had witnessed him using against the Orcs.
Instead, he had used one of his abilities to save people who couldn’t offer him anything in return.
’So he really isn’t killing everyone just because he can...’
Thinking this, Emberlyn’s earlier impression of Luke changed slightly, although she still had reservations about his strange cultivation technique.

As for Luke himself, his expression remained as calm as before, seemingly unconcerned by the gratitude directed toward him, while the remaining silver sealing marks gradually faded from the survivors’ bodies.
"Let’s go to the next outpost," Luke said, turning toward Emberlyn after taking one final look at the surviving snake people.

Hearing his words, Emberlyn finally came out of her thoughts and nodded without saying anything, before her body slowly floated upward and she began ascending toward the sky, preparing to lead him toward another Orc outpost.
At the same time, a pair of wings emerged from Luke’s upper back, and with a powerful flap, his twenty-foot-tall armored body rose into the air before he followed Emberlyn.
FWOOOSH!

Watching the two figures gradually disappear into the distant sky, the surviving snake people couldn’t help raising their heads, while one of the men who had previously thanked Luke suddenly muttered.
"Is that young lord going to save more of our people?"
Unfortunately, no one could answer his question, and after a brief silence, they simply continued watching the two disappearing figures with gratitude in their eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 375: The Orc Tribe’s Three Strongest Leaders Are Revealed!
paragraphs: 33 days later...
1st Day of Aestas, the Eighth Month of Year 50,001.
BANG!
"WHY ARE WE LOSING SO MANY OUTPOSTS?!"
An enraged shout echoed throughout a large tent, accompanied by the sound of a fist slamming against a wooden table, causing several of the B-Rank Orcs standing nearby to lower their heads.
The one responsible was Gorzak, an extremely muscular, bald Orc with broad tusks protruding from his lower jaw, who also happened to be the Chieftain of their entire tribe.
Despite his furious questioning, none of the B-Rank Orcs dared to answer, mainly because they themselves had no idea what was happening to their scattered outposts.

Over the past month, reports of disappearing Orc forces had continued arriving one after another, yet no one had managed to discover who was responsible or what had happened to the warriors stationed there.

Meanwhile, seated at the center of three large chairs was Kroghar, the Grand Warlord of the tribe, whose tall, lean physique, missing tusk, and scarred jaw made him easily distinguishable from the other Orcs present.

Gorzak occupied the chair on one side of him, while the remaining seat belonged to Vradok, the Great Shaman, an ancient-looking Orc with deep-set red eyes and a scalp covered in intricate crimson tattoos.

These three were the only A-Rank existences within their tribe, although their current conditions were far from perfect, since all three were still recovering from the internal injuries they had suffered during their previous battle against Rhaenyra.
While Gorzak continued glaring at the B-Rank commanders, Kroghar finally turned toward an Orc Captain standing among the scouts.
"Tell me exactly what happened to our outposts," Kroghar ordered in a calm but commanding voice.
The Scout Captain became startled upon suddenly being addressed by the Grand Warlord, although he quickly lowered his head respectfully before answering.
"Grand Warlord, after receiving reports that several outposts had been destroyed, we immediately dispatched scouts to investigate their conditions, but..."
His voice gradually weakened as he reached the final word, clearly worried that revealing what they had discovered might provoke the same anger Gorzak had been displaying.
"Continue," Kroghar instructed without changing his expression.
Hearing that, the Scout Captain nodded and hurriedly continued.

"However, when our scouts reached those locations, they discovered that the outposts had been completely destroyed, while every Orc stationed there had disappeared without leaving behind a single corpse or even a drop of blood."
The report caused several commanders to exchange confused looks, although the Scout Captain continued before anyone could interrupt him.

"At first, we suspected that the surviving warriors might have abandoned their positions and retreated elsewhere, but we couldn’t find any evidence supporting that possibility, even after searching the surrounding areas."
Hearing this, Kroghar’s expression became more serious, while Gorzak and Vradok also turned their attention toward the Scout Captain.
’Not a single corpse or drop of blood?’
All three found that detail particularly strange, since even if an outpost had been attacked and its warriors slaughtered, there should have been at least some traces of the battle left behind.
As for those lower rank orcs running away? they didn’t belived it.

"Furthermore, our scouts attempted to locate the natives who previously inhabited those territories, but they had also disappeared," the Scout Captain added, keeping his head lowered. "We believe that after witnessing our earlier capture of their people, most of the surviving natives abandoned their settlements and fled toward the inner regions of the Dragon Continent."

After finishing his report, the Scout Captain immediately fell silent and waited for the expected reprimand, although before anyone could question him further, a hurried shout suddenly came from outside the tent.
"GRAND WARLORD! GREAT SHAMAN! ORC CHIEFTAIN! I HAVE BROUGHT IMPORTANT INFORMATION!
The sudden interruption drew everyone’s attention toward the entrance, where an Orc Shaman stood alongside several C-Rank warriors.

Their appearances were rather miserable, with mud covering much of their bodies, their clothes torn in several places, and numerous wounds visible across their exposed skin, making it obvious that their journey hadn’t been particularly peaceful.
Unfortunately, before the newcomers could explain themselves, Gorzak’s already terrible mood became even worse.
"WHO DARED TO LET THESE C-RANK BEGGARS INSIDE?!" he roared, glaring at the group as though their mere presence had personally offended him.
Elgrun, who had finally reached the main tribe after a month of traveling, immediately felt the corners of his mouth twitch.

He had originally expected to receive praise for delivering such important information, especially considering the dangers he and the other survivors had endured along the way, yet the first thing he received was an angry insult from his own Chieftain.
’Damn it! We nearly died bringing this information here, and this is how we’re welcomed?’
Naturally, he didn’t dare voice those thoughts, especially since he knew Gorzak’s personality quite well.

The Orc Chieftain had always been a hot-headed, warlike individual who preferred solving problems through overwhelming physical strength, and in Elgrun’s opinion, the muscles covering Gorzak’s body had probably left very little room for his brain.
"Calm down, Gorzak," Kroghar finally intervened, stopping the Chieftain from continuing his outburst before gesturing toward the newly arrived Shaman.
"You said you brought important information, so tell us what you discovered."
"Thank you, Grand Warlord."

Elgrun immediately bowed respectfully, feeling relieved that at least one of their leaders was willing to listen, before straightening his body and revealing the information he had traveled all this way to deliver.
"A puppet of one of the traitor gods has appeared on the Dragon Continent."
An unusual silence immediately descended upon the entire tent.
For several seconds, none of the Orcs present said anything, while their expressions gradually changed as they processed what Elgrun had just revealed.
’A puppet?’
’One of the traitor gods?’
Those words immediately reminded them of the teachings passed down by their ancestors, particularly the ancient prophecies concerning the gods who had abandoned Valtharion during its darkest era.

According to those teachings, the gods who had fled the world when it needed them most were remembered as traitors, and their eventual return through summoned puppets had been warned about for generations.
Now, hearing that one of those very puppets had appeared near their territory, the Orc commanders could hardly believe what they were being told.
"HOW DARE THOSE TRAITORS RETURN HERE?!"
Unsurprisingly, Gorzak was the first to break the silence, his furious roar shaking the tent as he slammed his fist against the armrest of his chair.
In his anger, he seemed to have completely forgotten that the beings he was insulting were gods, existences whose true strength was far beyond anything he could personally challenge.
However, that thought clearly didn’t concern him, because he immediately turned toward Elgrun and demanded an answer.
"WHERE IS THAT PUPPET?! TELL ME WHERE HE IS, AND I WILL PERSONALLY SLAUGHTER HIM!"
Elgrun’s mouth twitched again, and he couldn’t help wondering why this muscle-headed Chieftain insisted on making everything so difficult.
’How the hell am I supposed to know where that Hero is right now?’

After all, he had fled the outpost specifically to bring this information back to the tribe, and nearly an entire month had passed during his journey, so expecting him to know the Hero’s current whereabouts was simply ridiculous.
Still, before Elgrun could figure out how to answer without angering Gorzak further, the Scout Captain standing nearby suddenly spoke.
"Grand Warlord, could the disappearances of our outposts have something to do with this puppet?"

Hearing that suggestion, Kroghar turned toward the Scout Captain with a thoughtful expression, while Vradok remained silent in his seat, carefully listening to the conversation without offering his opinion.
However, before Kroghar could respond, Elgrun suddenly interrupted them.
"Other outposts? Wait, are you saying that the destroyed outposts had no corpses or even a single drop of blood left behind?"
The Scout Captain looked toward him in surprise before nodding.
"Yes, that is correct. Our scouts searched those locations thoroughly, but they couldn’t find a single corpse belonging to our warriors."
Hearing his confirmation, Elgrun’s expression immediately turned ugly as he recalled the horrifying scene he had witnessed before fleeing Yarvokh’s outpost.
’That damned Hero!’

"It’s the Hero of Light!" Elgrun exclaimed, attracting everyone’s attention as he hurriedly explained what he knew. "That puppet is using some kind of heinous cultivation technique to turn our fallen kin into Blood Essence Pills, which he then devours to increase his own strength!"
"What?!"
"HE’S DEVOURING OUR KIN?!"
The revelation immediately caused an uproar among the B-Rank Orcs, whose earlier confusion was replaced by anger as they stared at Elgrun in disbelief.
After all, dying in battle was considered honorable among their race, and warriors who fell while fighting stronger opponents were generally respected for their courage.

However, having their bodies turned into cultivation resources and devoured by the very enemy who killed them was an entirely different matter, especially since such an act was practically an insult to their fallen warriors.
"Are you certain about what you witnessed?" Kroghar asked, his expression becoming increasingly serious.

"Absolutely, Grand Warlord!" Elgrun answered without hesitation, recalling the terrible screams that had echoed throughout the outpost. "I personally witnessed that monster slaughtering our warriors before turning their bodies into blood pills, and I even heard their screams as they were being devoured!"
His expression twisted with anger before he added, "Only the puppets of those traitorous gods would possess such a disgusting cultivation technique!"

chapters.title: Chapter 376: Luke Has Become a Prize for the Endless Forest?!
paragraphs: "HOW DARE HE?!"
Gorzak erupted once again, his muscular arms trembling with fury as he rose from his chair and turned toward Kroghar.
"KROGHAR, LET ME GO! I WILL PERSONALLY SLAUGHTER THAT BASTARD AND DESTROY THE TEMPLES OF THOSE TRAITOR GODS!"
Unfortunately, Kroghar completely ignored his furious shouting, since he was already considering the implications of everything Elgrun had revealed.

If the destroyed outposts truly belonged to the same attacker, then the number of their fallen warriors had already become considerable, and judging by the complete absence of corpses, many of them might have been devoured through that strange cultivation technique.
Moreover, if the Hero continued attacking at his current pace, their losses would only increase.
However, despite understanding the seriousness of the situation, Kroghar had no intention of personally leading an attack right now.
"We aren’t going anywhere until our injuries have recovered," he finally declared, causing Gorzak to turn toward him with an ugly expression.
"But Kroghar, are we supposed to sit here while that bastard continues slaughtering our warriors?!"

"Do you want to die that badly?" Kroghar asked, giving him a stern look before continuing. "If the three of us leave this place while we’re still injured and that crimson dragon appears again, do you think we’ll be fortunate enough to escape a second time?"
Hearing those words, Gorzak’s expression became even uglier, although he couldn’t immediately refute Kroghar’s reasoning.

After all, their previous encounter with Rhaenyra had already left all three of them suffering from internal injuries, and although Gorzak hated admitting defeat, he understood that fighting her again in their current condition would be extremely dangerous.

More importantly, the three of them were the strongest existences within their tribe, and if they died, the remaining Orcs would have little hope of surviving against the stronger tribes or the Dragons occupying this continent.

As for the dishonor associated with retreating from battle, none of the three particularly cared about such things when their own lives were at stake, since those expectations were generally imposed upon lower-ranked warriors.
Just as Gorzak was reluctantly accepting Kroghar’s decision, a calm, aged voice suddenly came from the remaining chair.
"We will set a trap for this Hero of Light and kill him in one attack."
Hearing those words, everyone immediately turned toward Vradok, the Great Shaman, who had remained silent throughout most of their discussion.
He slowly raised his head and looked across the gathered commanders before continuing.
"We will prepare a ritual formation and gather ninety percent of our forces to eliminate him, including one hundred B-Rank warriors."
For a moment, none of the Orc commanders knew how to respond, because the number Vradok had proposed was far beyond anything they had expected.

Gathering ninety percent of their forces would require mobilizing Orcs from across their scattered territories, potentially bringing millions of their kin together, while also recalling the warriors stationed at their remaining outposts.

If they actually followed such an arrangement, most of their conquered territories would be left without proper protection, and everything they had gained through their recent invasion of the Dragon Continent could easily fall back into the hands of the natives.
Naturally, several commanders became hesitant upon realizing how much territory they might have to abandon.
Noticing their expressions, Vradok calmly explained his reasoning.

"We cannot afford to underestimate the puppets of those traitors, especially when this one has already demonstrated the ability to destroy our outposts without leaving behind any survivors or corpses."

He paused briefly before adding, "Besides, if we manage to capture or kill this Hero of Light and present his head to the royal Orcs, the rewards we receive could be far more valuable than these territories."
Hearing that, the expressions of several commanders immediately changed as they remembered something important.

According to the ancient prophecies preserved within the Endless Forest, the royal families of various races had long considered the puppets of the traitor gods their enemies, and rewards had been promised to those capable of capturing or killing such beings.

Since the royal tribes themselves rarely ventured onto the surface, presenting them with the head of a Hero could bring extraordinary benefits, perhaps even allowing their defeated tribe to rebuild its former strength and regain a place among the more powerful Orc factions.
Thinking about those possibilities, the B-Rank commanders gradually became excited, although Vradok wasn’t finished explaining his plan.

"Since the three of us won’t be participating personally, we must use sufficient force to ensure that this Hero cannot escape," he continued, looking toward Kroghar and Gorzak before returning his attention to the gathered commanders.
"After all, if we fail to eliminate him and word of his existence spreads throughout the Endless Forest, the other tribes will undoubtedly become interested."
His voice grew slightly lower as he explained the consequence they should be most concerned about.
"If those tribes discover that we have already encountered a puppet of the traitor gods, they will certainly join the hunt, and whoever captures him first will be the one to claim the reward."

Upon hearing those words, the expressions of the gathered Orcs immediately turned ugly, since none of them wanted to share such a valuable opportunity with the very tribes that had previously driven them from their home.
Even Gorzak, who had been furious about the decision to remain behind, gradually calmed down after considering the benefits they could obtain from killing the Hero.
Kroghar also appeared satisfied with the proposal, since it would allow them to deal with their enemy without risking the lives of their three strongest leaders while they were still recovering.
Seeing that no one had any further objections, Vradok finally gave his order.
"Then go and begin preparing the trap immediately. Recall our warriors, gather the B-Rank commanders, and make sure everything is ready before that Hero discovers what we’re planning."
"YES, GREAT SHAMAN!"
The assembled Orcs immediately bowed before the three A-Rank leaders, after which they began leaving the tent one after another to carry out their orders.

Elgrun also followed the departing commanders, feeling rather satisfied that his information had finally received the attention it deserved, although he couldn’t help wondering whether even such a large force would truly be enough to eliminate that monster.
Once everyone had departed, only Kroghar, Gorzak, and Vradok remained seated within the tent, where they continued discussing the arrangements for the upcoming operation.
