Gathering ninety percent of their forces would require mobilizing Orcs from across their scattered territories, potentially bringing millions of their kin together, while also recalling the warriors stationed at their remaining outposts.

If they actually followed such an arrangement, most of their conquered territories would be left without proper protection, and everything they had gained through their recent invasion of the Dragon Continent could easily fall back into the hands of the natives.
Naturally, several commanders became hesitant upon realizing how much territory they might have to abandon.
Noticing their expressions, Vradok calmly explained his reasoning.

"We cannot afford to underestimate the puppets of those traitors, especially when this one has already demonstrated the ability to destroy our outposts without leaving behind any survivors or corpses."

He paused briefly before adding, "Besides, if we manage to capture or kill this Hero of Light and present his head to the royal Orcs, the rewards we receive could be far more valuable than these territories."
Hearing that, the expressions of several commanders immediately changed as they remembered something important.

According to the ancient prophecies preserved within the Endless Forest, the royal families of various races had long considered the puppets of the traitor gods their enemies, and rewards had been promised to those capable of capturing or killing such beings.

Since the royal tribes themselves rarely ventured onto the surface, presenting them with the head of a Hero could bring extraordinary benefits, perhaps even allowing their defeated tribe to rebuild its former strength and regain a place among the more powerful Orc factions.
Thinking about those possibilities, the B-Rank commanders gradually became excited, although Vradok wasn’t finished explaining his plan.

"Since the three of us won’t be participating personally, we must use sufficient force to ensure that this Hero cannot escape," he continued, looking toward Kroghar and Gorzak before returning his attention to the gathered commanders.
"After all, if we fail to eliminate him and word of his existence spreads throughout the Endless Forest, the other tribes will undoubtedly become interested."
His voice grew slightly lower as he explained the consequence they should be most concerned about.
"If those tribes discover that we have already encountered a puppet of the traitor gods, they will certainly join the hunt, and whoever captures him first will be the one to claim the reward."

Upon hearing those words, the expressions of the gathered Orcs immediately turned ugly, since none of them wanted to share such a valuable opportunity with the very tribes that had previously driven them from their home.
Even Gorzak, who had been furious about the decision to remain behind, gradually calmed down after considering the benefits they could obtain from killing the Hero.
Kroghar also appeared satisfied with the proposal, since it would allow them to deal with their enemy without risking the lives of their three strongest leaders while they were still recovering.
Seeing that no one had any further objections, Vradok finally gave his order.
"Then go and begin preparing the trap immediately.
Recall our warriors, gather the B-Rank commanders, and make sure everything is ready before that Hero discovers what we’re planning."
"YES, GREAT SHAMAN!"
The assembled Orcs immediately bowed before the three A-Rank leaders, after which they began leaving the tent one after another to carry out their orders.

Elgrun also followed the departing commanders, feeling rather satisfied that his information had finally received the attention it deserved, although he couldn’t help wondering whether even such a large force would truly be enough to eliminate that monster.
Once everyone had departed, only Kroghar, Gorzak, and Vradok remained seated within the tent, where they continued discussing the arrangements for the upcoming operation.

chapters.title: Chapter 377: “THE MONSTER IS HERE!”
paragraphs: 20th day of Aestas, the Eight month of year 50,001.
BOOOOM!
A thunderous explosion shook the surrounding forest as another outpost belonging to the Zhurkhal Tribe collapsed, sending broken timber, shattered stones, and thick clouds of dust into the air.
“Done.”
Luke exhaled and surveyed the destruction beneath the afternoon sunlight, although instead of looking satisfied with another successful raid, he seemed rather disappointed.
“Why haven’t these recent outposts had any higher-ranked Orcs? I’m starting to wonder where they’ve all gone.”
Emberlyn, who had just landed beside him, glanced toward the ruined outpost and found herself wondering the same thing.

The Orcs had fought stubbornly to conquer these territories, and considering how much effort they had invested in their invasion, it was difficult to believe they would suddenly abandon their positions without a proper reason.
Yet over the past several days, the number of D-Rank and higher Orcs stationed at the outposts had noticeably decreased, with some locations containing almost nothing but ordinary warriors.
“An ambush, perhaps?” Nyx suggested while floating near Luke’s shoulder, prompting the other Titan spirits to consider the possibility as well.
Luke rubbed his chin thoughtfully, remembering the group of Orcs he had allowed to escape more than a month ago.
“Hmm, now that you mention it, those scouts have also been getting more annoying. They keep watching us from a distance, but whenever I try approaching them, they run away.”

During the past month, Luke had destroyed numerous Orc outposts and killed many warriors ranging from D-Rank to B-Rank, although his progress had gradually slowed as the stronger Orcs became increasingly difficult to locate.
Another thing he had noticed was the declining number of native prisoners, since the more outposts he cleared, the fewer captives he encountered.
‘Maybe they’ve started moving the prisoners somewhere else.’
Thinking about all these unusual changes, Luke increasingly suspected that the Zhurkhal Tribe was preparing something for him.

Unfortunately for the Orcs, he had no intention of abandoning his hunt merely because an ambush might be waiting ahead, especially when his cultivation still required a considerable amount of Blood Essence.
‘As long as those A-Rank monsters don’t show up, I should be fine.’
With that thought, Luke gestured toward Emberlyn, and the two departed for the next outpost.
However, this time, his confidence would prove to be a serious mistake.
THUD!
Luke landed on a rocky hill overlooking a medium-sized Orc outpost, while Emberlyn descended a short distance beside him.
Below them, wooden watchtowers rose above reinforced earthen walls, and several dark banners bearing the Zhurkhal Tribe’s insignia fluttered in the wind.

Compared to the smaller outposts they had recently destroyed, this one appeared considerably better defended, with Orc guards patrolling the walls and several buildings concentrated around a broad central clearing.

Luke had originally hoped that raiding so many outposts would provide him with valuable resources, but most of what he had discovered so far consisted of raw materials such as ores, which occupied far too much space in his storage rings.
Rather than wasting his limited storage capacity, he had decided to prioritize strengthening himself, since obtaining better treasures would become easier once his cultivation improved.
Emberlyn quietly observed the outpost, paying particular attention to its guards and the activity near the central clearing.
Nothing appeared especially unusual, since the Orcs were performing their duties normally, while the center of the outpost seemed rather crowded.
“Finally, an outpost with some decent Orcs.”
Luke’s disappointment immediately disappeared as he sensed several B-Rank auras coming from below, and a pleased smile gradually appeared on his face.
After spending so much time clearing smaller outposts, he was more than ready to hunt stronger enemies.
“All right, be careful,” Emberlyn reminded him before moving toward a distant tree, where she settled onto one of its thicker branches to observe the coming battle.
By now, this arrangement had become familiar to them both, since Luke generally handled the Orcs himself while Emberlyn remained nearby in case something unexpected happened.
Moreover, her earlier suspicions about his cultivation technique had almost completely disappeared over the past month.

Although she had personally witnessed Luke turning the bodies of slain Orcs into Blood Essence Pills, he had never attempted to use that technique on innocent captives, and what surprised her even more was that she couldn’t detect any accumulated bloodlust or negative aura around him.
For someone practicing such a disturbing cultivation method, his condition was unusually clean.
Meanwhile, Luke rolled his shoulders, flexed his fingers, and looked down toward the outpost’s main entrance.
“All right, let’s get started.”
BANG!
With a powerful kick against the rocky ground, he launched himself down the hillside, leaving a shallow depression beneath his feet before landing directly in front of the outpost’s main gate.
The impact sent dust rolling across the entrance, while the nearby wooden barricades rattled and several guards standing on the walls stumbled.
“What was that?!”
“INTRUDER!”
The Orc guards immediately raised their weapons, although the moment they sensed a living presence within the dust cloud, their expressions changed.

During the past month, rumors had spread throughout the Zhurkhal Tribe about a mysterious individual who was destroying entire outposts, and according to the surviving scouts, the attacker had been operating alone.
Now, with a single person suddenly appearing outside their gates, the guards couldn’t help remembering those reports.
“Don’t tell me he’s the one...”
“GO! INFORM THE COMMANDERS!”
Instead of rushing forward to attack, several guards immediately abandoned their positions and hurried toward the inner section of the outpost.
Luke, who had expected the usual reckless charge, couldn’t help raising his eyebrows at their reaction.
“Oh? Looks like I’ve become pretty famous.”
Previously, the Orcs would immediately attack him after recovering from their initial surprise, but this time, their first instinct was to run and alert their superiors.
Before Luke could think much further, a deep sound suddenly echoed from somewhere inside the outpost.
DUM! DUM! DUM! — DUM-DUM-DUM! — DUM! DUM! DUM!
War drums!
The heavy, rhythmic beating spread across the outpost, followed by hurried footsteps and shouted commands as the Orcs began responding to the warning.
“INTRUDER AT THE MAIN GATE!”
“EVERYONE, GET INTO FORMATION!”
Luke could hear the commotion beyond the walls, along with the clattering of weapons and the sound of Orcs rushing across the packed earth.
However, rather than worrying about their preparations, his attention shifted toward something much more interesting.
‘Hmm, which Titan should I use today? Or should I try another fusion?’
He considered the possibility briefly before shaking his head.
‘Nah, a fusion would be too much. Let’s go with Voltrax.’
A smile appeared on his face as he raised his head toward the open sky.
“Thunder Titan Ascension!”
KRRRRRRAAAAAK—BOOOOOOM!
A violent crack of thunder erupted overhead, causing the guards on the watchtowers to instinctively look upward.
Without warning, a thick bolt of lightning tore through the daylight and descended directly toward Luke, illuminating the walls and surrounding trees in a brilliant flash.
BOOOOM!
The lightning struck his body, sending a circular shockwave across the entrance and throwing loose stones and dust outward.
However, instead of being injured, Luke’s body began expanding within the brilliant electrical radiance, his flesh transforming as black, armor-like plates spread across his growing physique.
KRRRKKK! ZZZZK—CRACKLE!

His arms thickened, his shoulders broadened, and the ground beneath his feet gradually fractured under his increasing weight, while arcs of lightning raced across his body before gathering around the horns protruding from his head.
Those horns curved upward in the shape of a crown, their edges glowing with concentrated electrical energy as the last traces of the descending lightning disappeared.
When the blinding radiance finally faded, a fifty-foot-tall Thunder Titan stood before the outpost.
His black, plated body towered above the entrance, while thin streams of lightning continued traveling across his armor-like skin and crackling around his crown-shaped horns.
The guards on the watchtowers stared at him in horror, with several instinctively retreating from the wooden railings.
“W-What kind of monster is that?!”
Luke ignored their frightened voices and slowly clenched his right fist, causing the lightning around his arm to flicker as his muscles tightened.
“HAAH!”
He stepped forward and drove his fist directly into the reinforced gate.
BAAAAAAANG!
The wooden doors burst apart under the impact, while the packed earth and supporting timbers surrounding them cracked and collapsed as the force traveled through the entire entrance.
KRRRRAAACK! THUD! CRASH!
Broken planks flew into the outpost, and chunks of earth scattered across the ground, forcing several nearby guards to throw themselves aside as the gate’s remains crashed around them.
A thick cloud of dust immediately rolled through the opening, accompanied by frightened shouts from the Orcs inside.
“AAAAH! THE MONSTER IS HERE!”
Luke slowly lowered his fist and stepped through the ruined entrance, expecting to find the usual group of Orc warriors charging toward him with their weapons raised.
Instead, something rather strange greeted him.

The guards who had been stationed near the entrance were retreating toward the center of the outpost, while others were hurriedly moving toward the outer sections, leaving the broad clearing unusually open.
‘What are they doing?’
Luke became suspicious as he looked around, because the Orcs weren’t behaving like warriors preparing to defend their base.
More importantly, eight figures were waiting near the center of the clearing, standing confidently with their arms folded or weapons resting beside them.
Unlike the retreating guards, none of them seemed particularly frightened by his fifty-foot Titan body.
Luke immediately recognized the strength of their auras.
‘Peak B-Rank?’

chapters.title: Chapter 378: Even Surrounded by Enemies, Luke Still Attracts Trouble With Women!
paragraphs: All eight were Peak B-Rank Orc commanders, whose appearances and equipment clearly distinguished them from the ordinary warriors stationed throughout the outpost.

Among them stood Gurvak, a broad-shouldered Orc with a broken right tusk, whose powerful physique was well suited for grappling and close combat, while beside him was Brakka, a female Orc with braided black hair, a scar crossing her left eye, and two battleaxes resting within easy reach.

Uzgor stood slightly apart from the others, his tall, lean body and unusually long arms giving him a rather distinctive appearance, while Drukon, an elderly-looking Shaman wearing necklaces made from bones, calmly observed Luke with his ritual staff in hand.

The remaining four were Molgar, a barrel-chested warrior with a thick neck and missing left ear; Vargut, whose body bore deep scars and whose face had only one functioning eye; Brukha, a female commander with bronze rings piercing her tusks; and Garzun, a heavily built Orc carrying a shield and mace.
What Luke didn’t know was that these eight commanders had been deliberately gathered here after the tribe’s leaders learned about his peculiar transformations.

According to the reports they had received, the Hero of Light possessed several methods of temporarily raising his apparent strength to Early B-Rank, while his actual fighting ability could reach approximately Mid B-Rank.
For eight Peak B-Rank commanders, facing such an opponent should have been manageable, especially when they were also relying on an ancestral formation prepared by their three A-Rank leaders.

Their confidence wasn’t entirely unreasonable, since despite Luke’s unusual abilities, his true cultivation was still D-Rank, and he lacked several qualities possessed by genuine higher-ranked existences.
However, Luke himself knew none of these arrangements.
He merely stared at the eight Peak B-Rank Orcs, whose combined auras were pressing against his enormous body, and felt his earlier excitement gradually disappear.
’Is this the ambush? Eight Peak B-Rank Orcs against one D-Ranker? Isn’t that a little excessive?!’
He cursed his luck inwardly, wondering what he had done to make the Zhurkhal Tribe take him so seriously.
A single Peak B-Rank opponent was already strong enough to force him into an extremely difficult battle, yet eight of them had been gathered here specifically to deal with him.
’Seriously, couldn’t they have sent them one at a time?’
Unfortunately, Luke had no idea that the eight commanders standing before him were merely the first part of the trap.
Another hundred B-Rank Orcs were waiting nearby, concealed from his senses, while millions of lower-ranked warriors had already been positioned throughout the surrounding region.
If he had known the full extent of their preparations, he would probably have cursed whoever had devised this ridiculous plan.
Meanwhile, Emberlyn, who had been watching from her distant tree branch, also became increasingly concerned after sensing the eight Peak B-Rank auras.
"Eight Peak B-Rank commanders?"
Her expression changed as she examined the figures waiting in the clearing, unable to understand why the Zhurkhal Tribe had mobilized so many powerful warriors against Luke.
She had expected retaliation after the destruction of their outposts, but such a concentrated deployment seemed far too excessive for an ordinary hunt.
’Each of those commanders could oversee an entire territory, yet they’ve gathered eight of them in one place...’
An unpleasant suspicion suddenly crossed her mind.
’Have they brought their entire army here?’
Her gaze immediately shifted toward the surrounding forest, although she couldn’t detect anything that confirmed her suspicion.
’Is this because Luke is connected to that goddess?’
That explanation seemed possible, considering how strongly the Orcs hated the gods they regarded as traitors.
However, even such hatred shouldn’t have been enough to convince their leaders to risk so many high-ranking warriors unless there was something valuable to be gained from capturing him.
As Emberlyn continued considering those possibilities, one of the commanders finally broke the silence below.
"Tch! They dragged me all the way here just to fight a D-Ranker?"
Gurvak sneered at Luke, showing little concern for the Thunder Titan standing before him.
Although Luke’s transformed body radiated an Early B-Rank aura, further enhanced by his Nullex armor, the commanders already knew that his true cultivation was far lower.
They had received enough information from their scouts to understand that his apparent realm was the result of temporary enhancements, rather than genuine advancement.
Brakka, meanwhile, appeared far more interested in Luke’s imposing Titan physique.
"Sigh, what a waste. If you weren’t one of those traitor gods’ puppets, I might have considered claiming you for myself."
She slowly looked him up and down before licking her lips, her expression becoming increasingly enthusiastic.
"With a body like yours, our children would probably be born stronger than most of the warriors in this tribe."
The other commanders barely reacted to her declaration, apparently accustomed to her peculiar interests.
Brakka was a battle maniac who greatly admired physical strength, and among Orcs, seeking a powerful mate was hardly an unusual desire.
Luke, however, was momentarily speechless.
’What the hell?’

He glanced toward Brakka, whose twelve-foot-tall body was muscular without being excessively bulky, with the clothing covering her chest and lower body leaving much of her toned arms and abdomen exposed.
For some reason, her appearance reminded him of an extremely dedicated female gym enthusiast, although the two battleaxes beside her made the comparison rather unpleasant.
Before Brakka could say anything else, Brukha finally interrupted.
"All right, that’s enough. Let’s finish this before those three lose their patience."
Hearing her words, the other commanders exchanged glances before nodding.
"Fine, let’s get it over with."
However, instead of immediately attacking, they remained where they stood.
And then...
THUD! THUD! THUD! THUD!
Heavy footsteps suddenly echoed from several directions.
Luke turned his head as figures began emerging from the spaces between the surrounding buildings, followed by another group appearing near the broken gate.
Within seconds, a hundred additional B-Rank Orcs, ranging from Early to High B-Rank, had entered the clearing.

Their green skin bore crimson tattoos, and each carried a weapon while moving into position around Luke, gradually forming an encirclement that left him with fewer and fewer directions in which to retreat.
’Another hundred?!’
Luke’s expression stiffened.
He had barely finished counting the newcomers when something even more disturbing happened.
The air beyond the outpost suddenly rippled.
At first, the disturbance resembled an ordinary distortion caused by heat, but the ripples soon spread across the surrounding forest, passing over trees, hills, and empty stretches of ground.
VMMMMMM...
Luke turned toward the strange phenomenon, sensing that something was wrong, although he couldn’t immediately identify its cause.
Then the scenery began changing.
Sections of the apparently empty forest flickered, and several distant hills seemed to tremble before the illusion concealing them finally broke apart.
What appeared beneath it caused Luke’s thoughts to freeze.
Orcs.

An army of Orcs stretched across the surrounding land, filling the spaces between the trees and covering the distant hillsides, with their weapons catching the daylight as the concealed formations gradually became visible.

There were millions of them, ranging from F-Rank to C-Rank, and nearly every direction Luke looked was occupied by green-skinned warriors staring toward the solitary Titan standing inside the outpost.
Their expressions were filled with anticipation and greed, as though the person surrounded by their forces was already a reward waiting to be claimed.
’What...’
Luke slowly turned his head, trying to find a gap in the encirclement.
However, before he could properly comprehend the number of enemies around him, a strange vibration spread beneath his feet.
VMMMMMMMM—!
The ground throughout the surrounding region began glowing with faint crimson lines, which gradually connected into intricate patterns extending far beyond the outpost.
Some markings appeared beneath the Orc army, while others emerged across the distant hills, their light intensifying as the formation drew power from the surrounding area.
Luke lowered his gaze toward the glowing lines.
’A formation?’
A deep, unfamiliar resonance suddenly echoed through the air, accompanied by a pressure that made even his Thunder Titan body feel unusually heavy.
OHHHHMMMMM!
The crimson patterns flared simultaneously.
A column of dark red light shot upward from the outer perimeter, followed by several more rising at different points around the battlefield.
As they reached the sky, the columns curved inward, spreading into a vast network of glowing lines that began joining together above the assembled army.
Within seconds, a circular barrier started forming around the entire region.

The light traveled across its surface in expanding waves, gradually creating a dome that stretched for miles, enclosing the outpost, the surrounding forest, and every living being caught within its boundaries.
WHOOOOOM!
The final sections connected overhead, producing a low, thunderous vibration that rolled across the battlefield.
For an instant, the entire interior was illuminated crimson as the dome’s surface flashed, before its radiance dimmed into a dark red glow.
Luke looked upward, watching strange ancient markings slowly rotate across the barrier.
He could still hear the distant movement of the Orc army, the occasional rattle of weapons, and the wind moving through the trees, yet something about the atmosphere had changed.
The space surrounding him felt strangely restricted, as though an invisible pressure had settled over the entire region.
’What kind of formation is this?’
Unfortunately, no one answered his question.
Instead, a familiar blue screen suddenly appeared before his eyes.

Their confidence wasn’t entirely unreasonable, since despite Luke’s unusual abilities, his true cultivation was still D-Rank, and he lacked several qualities possessed by genuine higher-ranked existences.
However, Luke himself knew none of these arrangements.
He merely stared at the eight Peak B-Rank Orcs, whose combined auras were pressing against his enormous body, and felt his earlier excitement gradually disappear.
’Is this the ambush?
Eight Peak B-Rank Orcs against one D-Ranker?
Isn’t that a little excessive?!’
He cursed his luck inwardly, wondering what he had done to make the Zhurkhal Tribe take him so seriously.
A single Peak B-Rank opponent was already strong enough to force him into an extremely difficult battle, yet eight of them had been gathered here specifically to deal with him.
’Seriously, couldn’t they have sent them one at a time?’
Unfortunately, Luke had no idea that the eight commanders standing before him were merely the first part of the trap.
Another hundred B-Rank Orcs were waiting nearby, concealed from his senses, while millions of lower-ranked warriors had already been positioned throughout the surrounding region.
If he had known the full extent of their preparations, he would probably have cursed whoever had devised this ridiculous plan.
Meanwhile, Emberlyn, who had been watching from her distant tree branch, also became increasingly concerned after sensing the eight Peak B-Rank auras.
"Eight Peak B-Rank commanders?"
Her expression changed as she examined the figures waiting in the clearing, unable to understand why the Zhurkhal Tribe had mobilized so many powerful warriors against Luke.
She had expected retaliation after the destruction of their outposts, but such a concentrated deployment seemed far too excessive for an ordinary hunt.
’Each of those commanders could oversee an entire territory, yet they’ve gathered eight of them in one place...’
An unpleasant suspicion suddenly crossed her mind.
’Have they brought their entire army here?’
Her gaze immediately shifted toward the surrounding forest, although she couldn’t detect anything that confirmed her suspicion.
’Is this because Luke is connected to that goddess?’
That explanation seemed possible, considering how strongly the Orcs hated the gods they regarded as traitors.
However, even such hatred shouldn’t have been enough to convince their leaders to risk so many high-ranking warriors unless there was something valuable to be gained from capturing him.
As Emberlyn continued considering those possibilities, one of the commanders finally broke the silence below.
"Tch!
They dragged me all the way here just to fight a D-Ranker?"
Gurvak sneered at Luke, showing little concern for the Thunder Titan standing before him.
Although Luke’s transformed body radiated an Early B-Rank aura, further enhanced by his Nullex armor, the commanders already knew that his true cultivation was far lower.
They had received enough information from their scouts to understand that his apparent realm was the result of temporary enhancements, rather than genuine advancement.
Brakka, meanwhile, appeared far more interested in Luke’s imposing Titan physique.
"Sigh, what a waste.
If you weren’t one of those traitor gods’ puppets, I might have considered claiming you for myself."
She slowly looked him up and down before licking her lips, her expression becoming increasingly enthusiastic.
"With a body like yours, our children would probably be born stronger than most of the warriors in this tribe."
The other commanders barely reacted to her declaration, apparently accustomed to her peculiar interests.
Brakka was a battle maniac who greatly admired physical strength, and among Orcs, seeking a powerful mate was hardly an unusual desire.
Luke, however, was momentarily speechless.
’What the hell?’

He glanced toward Brakka, whose twelve-foot-tall body was muscular without being excessively bulky, with the clothing covering her chest and lower body leaving much of her toned arms and abdomen exposed.
For some reason, her appearance reminded him of an extremely dedicated female gym enthusiast, although the two battleaxes beside her made the comparison rather unpleasant.
Before Brakka could say anything else, Brukha finally interrupted.
"All right, that’s enough.
Let’s finish this before those three lose their patience."
Hearing her words, the other commanders exchanged glances before nodding.
"Fine, let’s get it over with."
However, instead of immediately attacking, they remained where they stood.
And then...
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
Heavy footsteps suddenly echoed from several directions.
Luke turned his head as figures began emerging from the spaces between the surrounding buildings, followed by another group appearing near the broken gate.
Within seconds, a hundred additional B-Rank Orcs, ranging from Early to High B-Rank, had entered the clearing.

Their green skin bore crimson tattoos, and each carried a weapon while moving into position around Luke, gradually forming an encirclement that left him with fewer and fewer directions in which to retreat.
’Another hundred?!’
Luke’s expression stiffened.
He had barely finished counting the newcomers when something even more disturbing happened.
The air beyond the outpost suddenly rippled.
At first, the disturbance resembled an ordinary distortion caused by heat, but the ripples soon spread across the surrounding forest, passing over trees, hills, and empty stretches of ground.
VMMMMMM...
Luke turned toward the strange phenomenon, sensing that something was wrong, although he couldn’t immediately identify its cause.
Then the scenery began changing.
Sections of the apparently empty forest flickered, and several distant hills seemed to tremble before the illusion concealing them finally broke apart.
What appeared beneath it caused Luke’s thoughts to freeze.
Orcs.

An army of Orcs stretched across the surrounding land, filling the spaces between the trees and covering the distant hillsides, with their weapons catching the daylight as the concealed formations gradually became visible.

There were millions of them, ranging from F-Rank to C-Rank, and nearly every direction Luke looked was occupied by green-skinned warriors staring toward the solitary Titan standing inside the outpost.
Their expressions were filled with anticipation and greed, as though the person surrounded by their forces was already a reward waiting to be claimed.
’What...’
Luke slowly turned his head, trying to find a gap in the encirclement.
However, before he could properly comprehend the number of enemies around him, a strange vibration spread beneath his feet.
VMMMMMMMM—!
The ground throughout the surrounding region began glowing with faint crimson lines, which gradually connected into intricate patterns extending far beyond the outpost.
Some markings appeared beneath the Orc army, while others emerged across the distant hills, their light intensifying as the formation drew power from the surrounding area.
Luke lowered his gaze toward the glowing lines.
’A formation?’
A deep, unfamiliar resonance suddenly echoed through the air, accompanied by a pressure that made even his Thunder Titan body feel unusually heavy.
OHHHHMMMMM!
The crimson patterns flared simultaneously.
A column of dark red light shot upward from the outer perimeter, followed by several more rising at different points around the battlefield.
As they reached the sky, the columns curved inward, spreading into a vast network of glowing lines that began joining together above the assembled army.
Within seconds, a circular barrier started forming around the entire region.

The light traveled across its surface in expanding waves, gradually creating a dome that stretched for miles, enclosing the outpost, the surrounding forest, and every living being caught within its boundaries.
WHOOOOOM!
The final sections connected overhead, producing a low, thunderous vibration that rolled across the battlefield.
For an instant, the entire interior was illuminated crimson as the dome’s surface flashed, before its radiance dimmed into a dark red glow.
Luke looked upward, watching strange ancient markings slowly rotate across the barrier.
He could still hear the distant movement of the Orc army, the occasional rattle of weapons, and the wind moving through the trees, yet something about the atmosphere had changed.
The space surrounding him felt strangely restricted, as though an invisible pressure had settled over the entire region.
’What kind of formation is this?’
Unfortunately, no one answered his question.
Instead, a familiar blue screen suddenly appeared before his eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 379: Millions of Orcs, 100+ B-Ranks, and One Hero! [GT Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Even the System seemed to pity Luke after witnessing the absurd number of enemies gathered against him, while the four Titan spirits, who had been resting within his consciousness, emerged one after another.
Nyx looked toward the surrounding Orc army, then raised his head to examine the crimson dome stretching across the sky.
Caelith and Sevaroth also began studying the formation, while Myrkhal stared at the millions of warriors surrounding Luke with an expression of curosity.
"Isn’t this a little too much?" Luke muttered, his earlier confidence almost completely gone.

He had expected the Orcs to prepare an ambush, but never imagined they would mobilize an army numbering in the millions, along with more than a hundred B-Rank warriors, merely to capture a single D-Rank Hero.
’What the hell are they thinking? Did I personally murder their ancestors or something?!’
For the first time since arriving at the outpost, Luke began feeling genuinely afraid.
He knew his abilities were powerful enough to defeat opponents far above his actual cultivation, but there was a limit to what he could accomplish through transformations and temporary enhancements.
If his Eternal Titan Zero body had already been completed, he might have been capable of surviving such an encirclement, yet his current body was still far from reaching that stage.
Even with all his Titans and Armors, fighting this many enemies simultaneously seemed almost impossible.
’Shit! I might actually die here!’
Meanwhile, Emberlyn, who had remained hidden among the distant trees, was equally stunned by what had just happened.
When the illusion formation disappeared, she finally understood why the surrounding forest had seemed so ordinary despite the unusual concentration of B-Rank auras.
The Orcs had concealed an entire army.
’Millions of Orcs...’
Her expression became increasingly troubled as she examined the crimson dome overhead, realizing that she, too, had been caught inside its boundaries.
Even so, she remained hidden among the branches, and none of the Orcs appeared to have discovered her presence.
High above the battlefield, three figures floated outside the crimson dome, quietly observing the army gathered beneath them.
They were Gorzak, Kroghar, and Vradok, the three A-Rank leaders of the Zhurkhal Tribe.

Even from their position in the sky, the formation’s immense scale was clearly visible, with its dark crimson surface covering several miles of land while ancient markings slowly circulated across its exterior.
Gorzak stared at the tiny figure of Luke standing inside the dome before turning toward Vradok.
"Isn’t this going a little too far? That brat is only D-Rank, and we’ve gathered almost our entire army just to kill him."
He shook his head, clearly finding the arrangement excessive.
"Even one Peak B-Rank commander should be enough to deal with him, so why did you insist on bringing so many warriors?"
"We cannot afford to take any unnecessary risks," Vradok replied calmly, showing little concern for Gorzak’s complaint.

Unlike the hot-headed Orc Chieftain, Vradok had always preferred preparing thoroughly before confronting dangerous enemies, and that cautious nature had saved the Zhurkhal Tribe from destruction on several occasions.
Even Kroghar, who normally oversaw their military operations, had chosen not to interfere with the Great Shaman’s arrangements.
After all, this was no ordinary opponent.

They were dealing with a Hero summoned by one of the gods their ancestors had warned them about, and nobody could say for certain what kind of hidden protections or extraordinary abilities such a person might possess.
However, Kroghar still had one concern.
"Vradok, are you certain this formation can prevent those gods from communicating with him?"
Hearing his question, Vradok looked down at the dark crimson dome before answering.

"Yes. This formation was passed down by our ancestors specifically to interfere with divine connections, and once activated, it can isolate everything within its boundaries from external divine communication."

He paused briefly before adding, "Ordinary sounds and physical disturbances can still pass through the barrier, but the connections those gods rely upon will be severed. Even if the Hero attempts to request their assistance, they won’t be able to reach him through this formation.
Kroghar nodded thoughtfully, while Gorzak returned his attention toward the battlefield, already eager to see how long the young Hero would survive.
What Luke was about to experience was the true value of an ancient race’s inheritance, something that ordinary noble forces such as those belonging to a Viscount could never easily reproduce.
"Sigh, gentlemen, can’t we settle this peacefully?"
Luke looked toward the eight Peak B-Rank commanders waiting in front of him, forcing a somewhat awkward smile onto his face.
"How about we discuss this first? There’s really no need for everyone to get so excited."
Unfortunately, his attempt at negotiation only amused the Orc commanders, several of whom began smiling as they watched the fifty-foot Thunder Titan surrounded by their warriors.
They had already received orders to capture or kill the Hero, although crippling him first would make their task considerably easier.
Luke noticed their expressions and understood that talking was probably useless.
’Fine, then I’ll just leave.’
He immediately concentrated on his Armor.
’Valzareth!’
A dark ripple traveled across his body, causing the Nullex Armor surrounding his transformed physique to distort as its surface began changing.
VMMMM!
The existing armor gradually dissolved into flowing black energy, which spread across his arms, chest, and legs before reforming into the pitch-black plates of Valzareth.

Within seconds, the transformation was complete, and the enormous Thunder Titan now stood covered in Void Armor, its dark surface contrasting sharply with the lightning still flickering around his crown-shaped horns.
The unexpected change immediately attracted the attention of the Orc commanders.
"What kind of armor is that?"
However, Luke had no intention of explaining anything.
"Bye-bye!"
With a cheerful smile, he raised one hand and casually waved toward the commanders, his face still visible beneath the armor since he hadn’t summoned its helmet.
Then he activated Void Step.
’Void Step.’
Luke waited for the familiar spatial distortion to appear around him.
However, the air remained perfectly still, and his body continued standing in exactly the same position.
The Orc commanders exchanged confused looks.
"...What?"
Uzgor, whose unusually long arms hung beside his lean body, frowned as he stared at the giant standing before them.
"What is he trying to do?"
Luke was equally confused, although he quickly tried activating the ability again.
’Void Step.’
Nothing happened.
’What?’
His smile gradually disappeared as he looked toward the surrounding army, then back at the commanders waiting in front of him.
’Come on, Valzareth! Void Step!’
He concentrated more carefully this time, deliberately urging the Armor to activate its spatial movement ability.
Yet the familiar Void fluctuations still refused to appear.
’Void Step!’
’VOID STEP!!!’
Luke’s expression finally changed.
A bad premonition rose in his heart as he slowly raised his head toward the dark crimson dome covering the sky.
The ancient markings continued rotating across its surface, occasionally flashing as energy traveled between them.
’Don’t tell me...’
His gaze followed the strange symbols for a moment before he looked toward the distant boundary.
’Is that thing blocking my Void movement? But how?!’
"Luke, it seems you’ve become rather dependent on your abilities during our absence."
Nyx’s voice suddenly interrupted his thoughts, causing Luke to turn toward the floating Titan spirit.
"What do you mean?"
Nyx glanced toward the crimson dome before explaining.
"Have you forgotten that Valzareth is still a D-Rank Armor? Its Void movement cannot simply ignore restrictions imposed by a sufficiently powerful formation."
Luke’s face immediately became ugly.
He looked toward the dome once again, finally understanding why his repeated attempts had accomplished nothing.
’So this thing isn’t just some ordinary B-Rank formation.’
Considering how easily it had prevented his Void Step from activating, Luke suspected that its quality might have already reached A-Rank, although he couldn’t determine its actual level.
Unfortunately, understanding the problem didn’t make his situation any better.
Instead, it meant that his easiest method of escaping the encirclement had already been rendered useless.
Meanwhile, the eight Orc commanders had been waiting cautiously for Luke to perform whatever mysterious technique he had been preparing.
However, after watching him stand motionless for several seconds, they gradually realized that something had gone wrong.
"Hahaha! I thought this puppet was about to use some extraordinary ability granted by those traitor gods!"
One of the commanders burst into laughter, prompting several others to follow.
Drukon, the elderly Shaman with bone necklaces hanging across his chest, gave Luke a mocking look.
"Does he seriously believe his tricks can overcome a formation prepared by our Great Shaman? He must think far too highly of himself."
Hearing those words, the other B-Rank Orcs began laughing as well, while the lower-ranked warriors watching from the surrounding army gradually relaxed.
Earlier, many of them had been worried that the mysterious Hero might possess some extraordinary ability, especially after witnessing his sudden armor transformation.
Now, seeing that he had accomplished nothing, their confidence returned.
Luke, however, was in no mood to listen to their laughter.
’This is seriously bad.’

chapters.title: Chapter 380: Luke Finds One Last Hope! [GT Bonus - ]
paragraphs: His gaze moved across the surrounding commanders before settling on the vast Orc army beyond them.

Fighting eight Peak B-Rank opponents was already dangerous enough, but with another hundred B-Rank warriors and millions of lower-ranked enemies present, his chances of surviving a prolonged battle were frighteningly low.
’Nyx, Caelith, is there really no way to get through that barrier?’

While waiting for their response, Luke also called upon the System to display his current cultivation progress, hoping that the Blood Essence he had accumulated over the past month might offer some possibility he had overlooked.
A familiar screen immediately appeared before his eyes.
[ETERNAL TITAN ZERO — CULTIVATION STATUS]
Body Reconstruction Progress: 2.30%
Blood Essence Accumulated: \~46,000 / 2,000,000 D-Rank Equivalents
Remaining Requirement: 97.70%
Luke stared at the numbers for several seconds, feeling increasingly annoyed.
Although he had spent more than a month hunting Orcs, most of the outposts he had destroyed contained relatively few D-Rank warriors, while C-Rank and B-Rank enemies were even rarer.
As a result, his cultivation progress remained disappointingly low.
’At this rate, I can’t even properly control more than two clones at the same time.’
He sighed inwardly, realizing that the new body he had been working so hard to construct wasn’t going to help him escape his current predicament.
At that moment, Nyx finally spoke.
"Unfortunately, Luke, we don’t see any reliable way for you to escape through that barrier right now, so you’ll have to fight your way through this situation."
Luke slowly looked toward the surrounding Orcs.
’Fight? Against all of them?’
For a moment, he genuinely wondered whose face he had seen first after waking up that morning, because his luck had apparently reached an entirely new level of misfortune.
However, while Luke was still trying to figure out what to do, an unfamiliar voice suddenly echoed inside Uzgor’s mind.
’Do it.’
The order came from Vradok, who was observing the battlefield from outside the dome.
Uzgor immediately straightened his posture.
’Finally.’
A faint smile appeared on his face as he stepped forward, attracting Luke’s attention.
The other seven commanders also became quieter, while several nearby Orcs began retreating to create more space around the Thunder Titan.
Luke noticed their movements and immediately became suspicious.
’What are they doing now?’
Uzgor raised his staff toward the sky, and a strange crimson glow slowly appeared along its surface.
At first, the light was faint, barely visible beneath the daylight, but as the Orc began channeling his energy into the staff, the ancient markings covering it gradually awakened.
VMMMMMM...
A low vibration spread through the clearing.
Luke looked upward.
The markings moving across the crimson dome had begun changing direction, and several of them were slowly gathering above his position.
’Something’s coming!’
Before he could determine what kind of technique Uzgor was preparing, the Orc began chanting in a deep, unfamiliar language.
"? zh’vhor? m... Kth? zz’? rr... Zhaakh’vrenn!"
The words sounded strange even to Luke, their harsh syllables carrying a peculiar resonance that seemed to linger in the air long after they were spoken.
As the final syllable escaped Uzgor’s mouth, the crimson markings above the outpost suddenly stopped moving.
For a brief instant, the portion of the dome directly overhead became completely still.
Then five dark crimson circles appeared across its inner surface.
OHHHHMMMM!
The circles flared, and the surrounding air trembled as a tremendous amount of energy gathered within them.
Luke’s expression changed.
’Chains?’
FWHIIIIP! FWHIIIIP! FWHIIIIP!
Five thick, dark crimson chains suddenly burst out from the glowing circles, each moving with such speed that the distance between the dome and Luke was crossed before he could even react.
Their links dragged strange red trails through the air, while the violent force of their descent caused sharp whipping sounds to echo across the clearing.
WHOOSH! SKRRRSH! KRRRANG!
"WHAT—?!"
Luke barely managed to raise his head before the first chain struck his right arm.
KRRRANG!
The links coiled around his armored wrist and forearm, tightening instantly with enough force to make the black plates of Valzareth creak.
Before he could pull his arm free, another chain wrapped around his left wrist, followed by two more that shot downward and secured themselves around both legs.
CLANK! KRRRKKK! CLANK!
"UGH!"
Luke tried to move, but the fifth chain had already arrived.
FWHIIIIP!
It curved through the air and wrapped directly around his neck, its dark crimson links grinding against his armor before tightening violently.
KRRRRAAAK!
All five chains suddenly pulled in different directions.

His arms were dragged outward, his legs were forced apart, and the chain around his neck stretched backward, leaving his fifty-foot Titan body suspended in a strained position as though he were a prisoner being displayed before the entire Orc army.
The enormous force nearly lifted his feet from the ground, while the earth beneath him fractured as he struggled to maintain his footing.
"UGGHHH!"
Luke immediately tried pulling his arms inward, causing the muscles beneath his armor to bulge as he exerted the strength of his Thunder Titan body.
However, the chains barely moved.
Instead, their links contracted even further, crushing the armor around his wrists, ankles, and neck before pressing directly against his Titan flesh.
KRRRRK! CLANK!
Cracks began spreading across those sections of Valzareth, while the pressure from the chains continued increasing.
Luke gritted his teeth and attempted another forceful movement.
Yet before he could properly resist, an intense pain suddenly erupted inside his head.
"AAAAARGH!"
His entire body jerked against the restraints.
The pain was different from an ordinary physical injury, since even though the chains were tightening around his limbs, the sensation seemed to penetrate directly into his mind.
It was as though something was squeezing his consciousness from within, making his thoughts scatter whenever he attempted to concentrate.
’W-What... is this?!’
His vision blurred for an instant, and the sound of the surrounding Orc army became strangely distant.
Although he was still standing inside his Titan body, the pain was interfering with his ability to think, making even the simple act of focusing on an ability increasingly difficult.
Meanwhile, Uzgor slowly lowered his staff and smiled with satisfaction.
"Good. We’ve finally captured the puppet."
The other commanders examined the restrained Titan, several of them visibly relaxing now that the first stage of their plan had succeeded.
After all, these crimson chains were being supplied directly by the ancestral dome formation, making them far stronger than an ordinary binding technique.
According to Uzgor’s understanding, even B-Rank warriors would have great difficulty breaking free, since the chains required strength approaching A-Rank to overcome.
And the giant trapped before them was nowhere near that level.
"So that’s it? He’s already captured?"
Vargut, the one-eyed Orc whose scarred body revealed a long history of battles, sounded genuinely disappointed.
He had been hoping to test the Hero’s unusual abilities personally, yet the fight appeared to have ended before he could even swing his weapon.
"How boring. I thought he would put up more resistance after destroying so many of our outposts."
Several of the commanders smiled at his complaint, while the surrounding Orcs began celebrating the apparent success of their trap.
However, Luke could barely hear their voices.
"AAARGHH!"
Another wave of pain assaulted his mind, causing his body to convulse against the chains as dark crimson energy pulsed through the links.
He tried concentrating on his Thunder Titan’s power, but the moment he gathered his thoughts, the pain intensified and scattered them again.
’Shit! I can’t... concentrate!’
His breathing became increasingly strained as he struggled against the restraints, while the pressure around his neck made every movement even more uncomfortable.
"Luke! Come to your senses!"
Nyx’s voice suddenly rang out inside his consciousness, followed by Caelith’s worried shout.
"Luke, you need to resist it! Those chains are interfering with your mind!"
The other Titan spirits also called out to him, trying to break through the growing confusion.
Unfortunately, Luke had never properly trained himself to withstand such persistent mental pain, and the continuous assault was rapidly overwhelming his ability to think clearly.
’Uggh... I... I have to...’
His eyes became bloodshot as he struggled to keep them open, while another painful contraction caused his body to jerk violently.
’AAAAH! Damn it! I have to do something about these chains!’
He attempted to pull his arms free once again, but the chains immediately tightened, sending another crushing wave of pain through his head.
For an instant, Luke nearly lost consciousness.
However, just as his thoughts were beginning to fade, the image of a familiar Titan suddenly appeared within his mind.
’Sevaroth...’
Luke’s breathing caught.
He remembered how Sevaroth had previously broken through powerful seals, and although these chains were different, their purpose was ultimately the same.
They were restraints, maintained through the power of a formation.
’That’s right... Sevaroth broke those seals!’
A trace of hope finally appeared in his bloodshot eyes.

Even though the pain made it difficult to concentrate, Luke desperately clung to that thought, recalling the sealing abilities he had obtained and searching for something capable of dealing with the chains.
The crimson links pulsed again, sending another wave of pain through his body.
"UGGHH!"
Luke clenched his teeth, forced his scattered thoughts together, and finally opened his mouth.
"KIKI!"

sentences.text: His gaze moved across the surrounding commanders before settling on the vast Orc army beyond them.

Fighting eight Peak B-Rank opponents was already dangerous enough, but with another hundred B-Rank warriors and millions of lower-ranked enemies present, his chances of surviving a prolonged battle were frighteningly low.
’Nyx, Caelith, is there really no way to get through that barrier?’

While waiting for their response, Luke also called upon the System to display his current cultivation progress, hoping that the Blood Essence he had accumulated over the past month might offer some possibility he had overlooked.
A familiar screen immediately appeared before his eyes.
[ETERNAL TITAN ZERO — CULTIVATION STATUS]
Body Reconstruction Progress: 2.30%
Blood Essence Accumulated: \~46,000 / 2,000,000 D-Rank Equivalents
Remaining Requirement: 97.70%
Luke stared at the numbers for several seconds, feeling increasingly annoyed.
Although he had spent more than a month hunting Orcs, most of the outposts he had destroyed contained relatively few D-Rank warriors, while C-Rank and B-Rank enemies were even rarer.
As a result, his cultivation progress remained disappointingly low.
’At this rate, I can’t even properly control more than two clones at the same time.’
He sighed inwardly, realizing that the new body he had been working so hard to construct wasn’t going to help him escape his current predicament.
At that moment, Nyx finally spoke.
"Unfortunately, Luke, we don’t see any reliable way for you to escape through that barrier right now, so you’ll have to fight your way through this situation."
Luke slowly looked toward the surrounding Orcs.
’Fight?
Against all of them?’
For a moment, he genuinely wondered whose face he had seen first after waking up that morning, because his luck had apparently reached an entirely new level of misfortune.
However, while Luke was still trying to figure out what to do, an unfamiliar voice suddenly echoed inside Uzgor’s mind.
’Do it.’
The order came from Vradok, who was observing the battlefield from outside the dome.
Uzgor immediately straightened his posture.
’Finally.’
A faint smile appeared on his face as he stepped forward, attracting Luke’s attention.
The other seven commanders also became quieter, while several nearby Orcs began retreating to create more space around the Thunder Titan.
Luke noticed their movements and immediately became suspicious.
’What are they doing now?’
Uzgor raised his staff toward the sky, and a strange crimson glow slowly appeared along its surface.
At first, the light was faint, barely visible beneath the daylight, but as the Orc began channeling his energy into the staff, the ancient markings covering it gradually awakened.
VMMMMMM...
A low vibration spread through the clearing.
Luke looked upward.
The markings moving across the crimson dome had begun changing direction, and several of them were slowly gathering above his position.
’Something’s coming!’
Before he could determine what kind of technique Uzgor was preparing, the Orc began chanting in a deep, unfamiliar language.
"? zh’vhor? m...
Kth? zz’? rr...
Zhaakh’vrenn!"
The words sounded strange even to Luke, their harsh syllables carrying a peculiar resonance that seemed to linger in the air long after they were spoken.
As the final syllable escaped Uzgor’s mouth, the crimson markings above the outpost suddenly stopped moving.
For a brief instant, the portion of the dome directly overhead became completely still.
Then five dark crimson circles appeared across its inner surface.
OHHHHMMMM!
The circles flared, and the surrounding air trembled as a tremendous amount of energy gathered within them.
Luke’s expression changed.
’Chains?’
FWHIIIIP!
FWHIIIIP!
FWHIIIIP!
Five thick, dark crimson chains suddenly burst out from the glowing circles, each moving with such speed that the distance between the dome and Luke was crossed before he could even react.
Their links dragged strange red trails through the air, while the violent force of their descent caused sharp whipping sounds to echo across the clearing.
WHOOSH!
SKRRRSH!
KRRRANG!
"WHAT—?!"
Luke barely managed to raise his head before the first chain struck his right arm.
KRRRANG!
The links coiled around his armored wrist and forearm, tightening instantly with enough force to make the black plates of Valzareth creak.
Before he could pull his arm free, another chain wrapped around his left wrist, followed by two more that shot downward and secured themselves around both legs.
CLANK!
KRRRKKK!
CLANK!
"UGH!"
Luke tried to move, but the fifth chain had already arrived.
FWHIIIIP!
It curved through the air and wrapped directly around his neck, its dark crimson links grinding against his armor before tightening violently.
KRRRRAAAK!
All five chains suddenly pulled in different directions.

His arms were dragged outward, his legs were forced apart, and the chain around his neck stretched backward, leaving his fifty-foot Titan body suspended in a strained position as though he were a prisoner being displayed before the entire Orc army.
The enormous force nearly lifted his feet from the ground, while the earth beneath him fractured as he struggled to maintain his footing.
"UGGHHH!"

CLANK!

chapters.title: Chapter 381: The Crimson Coffin Finally Enters Battle!
paragraphs: "KIKI!"
FWHOOOSH!

The instant Luke shouted that name, the pitch-black armor covering his fifty-foot Thunder Titan body began trembling, its rigid plates suddenly losing their shape as they transformed into a thick, flowing liquid.

Under the astonished gazes of the surrounding Orcs, the black substance slipped through the narrow spaces beneath the crimson chains, separating from Luke’s body before gathering in the air beside him.
Within seconds, the liquid expanded and hardened into a twenty-five-foot-tall crimson coffin, whose front bore a gigantic mouth filled with rows of razor-sharp teeth.
However, the moment Valzareth completely separated from his body, Luke immediately suffered the consequences.
"AAAAARGHH!"

Without the threefold attribute enhancement previously provided by his Armor, his already strained mental resistance weakened considerably, allowing the strange power carried by the crimson chains to penetrate even deeper into his consciousness.
His vision blurred, and the pain pounding through his head became so intense that he could barely distinguish the figures standing around him.
’Shit... I can’t...’
His thoughts were beginning to scatter, while the five chains continued pulling his arms, legs, and neck in different directions, making even the slightest movement painful.
Meanwhile, the eight Peak B-Rank commanders had immediately become alert upon witnessing the sudden appearance of the crimson coffin.
"What is that thing?"
"Another summoned creature?"
Several commanders raised their weapons, expecting the strange coffin to attack them, but what happened next completely overturned their expectations.
"Kiki!"
The crimson coffin abruptly turned toward Luke instead, opening its gigantic mouth before lunging toward the chain restraining his right arm.
KRRRNNNCH!
Its sharp teeth clamped around the dark crimson links.
For an instant, nothing seemed to happen, and Uzgor almost smiled upon seeing the coffin attempting to bite through restraints powered by their ancestral formation.
However, before he could utter a single mocking word, a sharp cracking sound suddenly echoed across the clearing.
KRRRRAAAK!
The chain broke directly between Kiki’s jaws.
CLINK-CLATTER!
The severed links fell toward the ground, their crimson radiance flickering before gradually fading, while Luke’s right arm dropped slightly as the restraint holding it disappeared.
"...What?"
Uzgor’s smile vanished.
The other commanders also froze, unable to believe that something had just destroyed one of the chains supplied by their ancestral dome.
Unfortunately for them, Kiki had no intention of stopping after freeing only one arm.
FWHOOSH!
The coffin twisted toward Luke’s left side, snapping its jaws around the second chain before crushing the links with another powerful bite.
KRRRNNCH! KRAAAK!
"IMPOSSIBLE!"
An alarmed shout escaped one of the commanders as the second restraint broke apart, although Kiki had already lowered its body toward Luke’s legs.
CHOMP! KRRRACK!
The third chain snapped.
CLANK! KRRRNNCH!
The fourth followed immediately, scattering broken links across the ground while the crimson light around Luke’s remaining restraint flickered.
By now, the Orc commanders had finally recovered from their shock.
"STOP THAT THING!" Drukon shouted, gripping his staff as he rushed forward. "DON’T LET IT BREAK THE FINAL CHAIN!
The other seven commanders immediately responded, their Peak B-Rank auras erupting as they kicked against the ground and charged toward the coffin.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Eight figures shot across the clearing, leaving fractured earth and bursts of dust beneath their feet as they attempted to reach Kiki before it could free Luke completely.
However, their reaction had come too late.
Kiki raised its head toward the final chain wrapped around Luke’s neck, and before the nearest commander could close the distance, its gigantic jaws snapped shut.
KRRRRAAAK!
CLINK-CLATTER!
The last chain shattered, releasing Luke’s neck as the force holding his entire body in place suddenly disappeared.
"UGHH!"
THAAAAAM!
Luke dropped onto both knees, his enormous body striking the ground hard enough to fracture the packed earth beneath him, while his freed arms immediately moved toward his aching head.
"Huff... Hahh..."
He desperately drew in several rough breaths, trying to recover from the mental assault that had nearly robbed him of consciousness.
Unfortunately, the eight commanders were already approaching.
Kiki seemed to notice them as well.
"KIKI!"
The coffin turned sharply toward the incoming Orcs, its gigantic mouth opening as its front doors suddenly spread apart.
For an instant, the commanders hesitated, having already witnessed how easily those terrifying jaws had destroyed the crimson chains.
However, what emerged from the coffin wasn’t another biting attack.
FWHIP! FWHIP! FWHIP!
Sixteen dark crimson chains suddenly shot out from within its opened body, each trailing a faint red glow as they rushed toward the approaching commanders.
"What?!"
Before the Orcs could properly react, the chains split into eight pairs and wrapped themselves around their wrists, binding both arms of every commander.
KRRRKKK! CLANK! CLANK!
"UGHH!"
The restraints tightened immediately, interrupting their charge as the Orcs struggled to pull their arms free.
However, the moment the chains secured themselves around their bodies, a familiar mental assault accompanied them.
"AAARGHH!"
All eight commanders cried out as intense pain suddenly struck their consciousness, causing their movements to falter while their previously flaring auras became unstable.

Unlike the chains powered by the ancestral dome, Kiki’s restraints possessed a noticeably weaker crimson radiance, but their sudden appearance and mental interference were enough to disrupt the commanders’ attacks.
Kiki wasn’t finished.
THUD!
Its coffin body dropped heavily onto the ground, and the numerous legs extending beneath it immediately spread outward before stabbing into the packed earth.
KRRRSH! KRRRKKK!
The pointed legs pierced deep into the ground, anchoring the coffin in place as the sixteen chains stretched taut.
"KIKIIII!"
With an excited cry, Kiki began pulling all eight Peak B-Rank commanders toward itself.
The chains tightened around their wrists, dragging their arms forward while the pain interfering with their minds prevented them from immediately exerting their full strength.
"YOU DAMNED THING!"
Gurvak planted his feet into the earth and pulled backward, the muscles along his thick arms bulging as he tried resisting the coffin’s strength.
Several commanders did the same, causing the ground beneath their feet to crack as both sides exerted force through the chains.
KRRRRKKK!
However, every attempt to concentrate was interrupted by another wave of mental pain, leaving their eyes increasingly bloodshot and their expressions twisted with anger.
Meanwhile, Brukha struggled to maintain her focus, forcing herself to look past the crimson chains toward Luke’s kneeling figure.
She could see that he was still recovering from the earlier assault, his enormous chest rising and falling as he tried regaining control of his thoughts.
’We can’t give him time to recover!’
Realizing the danger, she gathered enough strength to shout toward the surrounding army.
"ALL OF YOU, ATTACK HIM! DON’T LET THAT HERO RECOVER!"
Her voice echoed across the clearing, finally snapping the remaining hundred B-Rank Orcs out of their astonishment.
Until now, they had been watching in disbelief as a coffin appeared from Luke’s armor, destroyed the supposedly unbreakable restraints, and then proceeded to capture their eight strongest commanders.
The battle that had seemed completely settled only moments earlier had suddenly turned against them.
"WHAT ARE YOU WAITING FOR?!"
"ATTACK THE HERO!"
The shouted orders quickly spread through the surrounding army, causing the previously stunned Orcs to raise their weapons and prepare their ancestral techniques.
High above the battlefield, Gorzak stared down at the crimson coffin with an expression of utter disbelief.
"Another trump card? Just how many strange things does this brat possess?!"
His gaze shifted toward the broken chains scattered around Luke before returning to Kiki, which was still struggling against the eight commanders.
"Those restraints were supposed to withstand the strength of almost any B-Rank warrior, yet that damned coffin simply bit through them!"
What Gorzak didn’t understand was that Kiki’s ability to break the restrictions had very little to do with overwhelming physical strength.
Unlike Luke’s ordinary Armors, Kiki couldn’t be worn to provide the usual threefold attribute enhancement, since its true specialty lay in understanding and breaking seals.

Its ability could already interfere with restrictions reaching the soul level, a category associated with beings of S-Rank and above, although destroying powerful seals still required the coffin to apply its specialized ability through direct contact.
The ancestral chains had been powerful, but Kiki had attacked their sealing structure rather than attempting to overpower the energy sustaining them.
"Such an artifact must have been given to him by those gods," Kroghar remarked, finding it difficult to believe that a D-Rank mortal could naturally possess something so unusual.
Gorzak’s earlier irritation quickly transformed into a delighted grin.
"Heh! Then capturing him will be even more worthwhile. Once he’s ours, we can take that coffin for ourselves!"
Vradok, however, remained silent.
Although the coffin had surprised him, he was secretly relieved that he had insisted upon gathering so many warriors and deploying the ancestral formation.
Had they relied solely upon the eight commanders, that unexpected ability might already have allowed the Hero to escape.
For now, however, the dome remained intact.
Far away, Emberlyn watched the battle from her concealed position among the trees, her hands slowly tightening into fists as she saw Luke struggling to recover.
’What should I do?’

She knew that Luke had gotten himself into an extremely dangerous situation, especially since the scale of the ambush strongly suggested that the three A-Rank leaders of the Zhurkhal Tribe were involved.
If those three were indeed nearby, revealing herself could easily provoke a direct confrontation.
’If they attack me, Luke won’t survive the aftermath.’
A battle between A-Rank existences would produce destructive forces far beyond what his current body could withstand, especially while he remained trapped inside the dome.
Moreover, there was her father’s order to consider.

Emberlyn had already been forbidden from involving herself in the Orc conflict as that would consider help to Rhaenyra, and if her presence were discovered during a confrontation with the tribe’s leaders, news of her disobedience would almost certainly reach him.
’Damn it...’
She bit her lower lip as she looked toward Luke’s distant figure.
’Please, Luke. Just find a way to escape from that place.’
As long as he managed to distance himself from the A-Rank Orcs, she could still help him, but until then, her intervention might make the situation even worse.
