chapters.title: Chapter 393: Just as Luke Falls... Five Golden Chains Appear!
paragraphs: Gorzak clenched his teeth, although he eventually stopped arguing and returned his attention to the battlefield.
Then a faint sound suddenly reached their ears.
"COUGH! COUGH!"
All three immediately looked toward its source.
The coughing came again, accompanied by a weak groan from somewhere beneath the smoke.
"He's alive!" Gorzak exclaimed, his earlier frustration immediately turning into fierce excitement.
Kroghar also sensed the faint presence coming from the ruined ground, and considering the destructive power of the explosion, he doubted any of their B-Rank warriors could have survived.
The three exchanged glances, each understanding what the discovery meant.
"We've already lost our tribe, so we cannot afford to lose the reward as well," Vradok said, his voice becoming serious.
Gorzak immediately agreed, although Kroghar raised another concern.
"We need to capture him and leave quickly, before that crimson dragon discovers what happened here."
Hearing his warning, the other two nodded.

They had already suffered considerable injuries during their earlier confrontation with Rhaenyra, and none of them wanted to fight that furious Dragon Princess again, especially after losing almost their entire army.
With that, the three restrained their auras and descended toward the faint coughing sounds, eventually discovering Luke's enormous crippled body lying inside a crater.
A tiny crimson coffin was moving across his injuries, weaving golden-white threads over the exposed wounds.
Gorzak's lips curled into a mocking smile.
"Well, well, the puppet of the traitor god is still alive."
His words were filled with amusement, although the hatred in his eyes made it clear that he hadn't forgotten the destruction of his tribe.
Not far from the crater, Emberlyn was also observing the aftermath from her concealed position.
Having survived the explosion through her A-Rank strength, she had been searching for Luke among the ruins, and when she finally sensed his faint presence, relief immediately washed over her.
She was preparing to approach him when three powerful auras suddenly appeared above the crater.
Emberlyn stopped.
'Those three...'
Her expression became increasingly troubled as she recognized the A-Rank leaders of the Zhurkhal Tribe.
'This is bad!'
If she revealed herself now, a confrontation would be unavoidable, and a battle between four A-Rank beings could easily kill Luke through the resulting shockwaves.
Moreover, there was still her father's order to consider.
'Damn it! What should I do?'
She clenched her fists, watching the three Orcs approach Luke's crippled body while struggling to decide whether she should intervene.
Meanwhile, inside the crater, Kiki had already noticed the newcomers.
"KIKI!"
The little crimson coffin immediately stopped weaving its golden-white threads and climbed onto Luke's enormous head, where it raised its tiny body and began hissing toward the intruders.
"KIKIII!"

The sight was rather comical, considering that a one-foot-tall coffin was attempting to intimidate three fifteen-foot-tall A-Rank Orcs while standing on the head of a severely injured seventy-foot Titan.
However, Kiki seemed completely serious about protecting its master.
Gorzak examined the little coffin before chuckling.
"Hah! It's good that this strange treasure survived as well."
Kroghar also glanced toward it, although neither of them felt threatened by its faint energy signature.
After all, Kiki currently possessed so little energy that it could barely maintain its tiny form.
Luke, however, wasn't willing to risk losing it.
'Kiki, go back.'
"Kiki?"
The little coffin turned toward him, apparently unwilling to leave while the three threatening figures remained nearby.
'I'll be fine. Just go.
After a brief hesitation, Kiki finally obeyed.
VMMMM!
Its crimson body dissolved into a faint glow before disappearing.
"Hmm?"
Vradok raised his eyebrows upon seeing the coffin vanish, although he quickly dismissed the matter.
They had already witnessed enough of Luke's unusual abilities to understand that capturing him would likely provide opportunities to uncover his secrets.
However, one particular ability still worried the Great Shaman.
'His spatial movement...'
Although the ancestral dome had been destroyed, Luke had previously demonstrated several methods of teleportation, and allowing him even a brief opportunity to recover could prove troublesome.
Vradok looked down toward his severely injured body.
"So, Hero of Light, I think you've caused us enough trouble for one day."
Luke stared at him without speaking, since with almost all his strength exhausted, he could barely move, much less prepare a technique capable of resisting an A-Rank existence.
Vradok slowly raised his hand.
"You should sleep for now, and when you wake up, you'll find yourself in heaven."
He casually flicked his finger.
BOOOOOOM!
The seemingly insignificant movement released a terrifying shockwave that crossed the short distance between them before Luke could even react.
BAAAAAANG!
The attack struck his chest directly, tearing through the already damaged flesh and nearly splitting his torso apart.
KRRRRAAAACK!
Most of his remaining internal organs ruptured beneath the force, while golden-red blood erupted from the injury and scattered across the surrounding ground.
"UGHH—!"
Luke barely managed to release a pained cry before his consciousness disappeared.
His enormous body jerked backward, striking the bottom of the crater as the remaining strength sustaining his transformation began weakening.
Had he not been maintaining Vorthar's extraordinary physique, the blow would almost certainly have killed him instantly.
Meanwhile, Emberlyn witnessed the attack from her concealed position.
'LUKE!'
Her expression changed completely, and she nearly rushed forward before forcing herself to stop.
'No! If I fight those three now, the shockwaves might kill him!'
She looked toward the Orc leaders, then toward the thick dust rising from Luke's crater, desperately searching for an opportunity to intervene.
Fortunately, before Gorzak could disperse the smoke, something unexpected happened.
CLINK! CLINK! CLINK!
Five golden chains suddenly emerged from within the dust cloud, their radiant links rattling violently as they become visible in the sky.
FWHOOOSH! FWHOOOSH!
The chains extended toward five different directions, making anyone feel, that those chains were crossing the distant sky with extraordinary speed.
However, one of them appeared noticeably shorter than the others, pointing toward a location somewhere within Bravaryn.
"What is that?!" Gorzak exclaimed, instinctively stepping backward.
Kroghar also became cautious, while Vradok stared at the golden chains with growing suspicion.
Although the three possessed A-Rank strength and were far from approaching the level of demigods, they could clearly sense an unfamiliar divinity radiating from those links.
The discovery immediately made them wary.
However, the chains didn't attack.
Instead, they continued extending toward the five wives connected to Luke, carrying an urgent warning about the danger threatening him.
Far away, within the Blackstone Highlands, life had gradually returned to normal following Rhaenyra's departure.

Although rumors about a dragon appearing in the territory continued circulating among the inhabitants, attracting attention from neighboring regions, most people had already resumed their ordinary activities.
At that moment, Aurielle was seated inside the Time Chamber, quietly meditating as she attempted to gather enough energy to advance her cultivation.
Her objective remained unchanged.
She wanted to become strong enough to bring the real Luke back from the Dragon Continent, rather than continuing to depend upon his clone.
However, just as she was concentrating upon the energy circulating through her body, something suddenly disturbed her meditation.
CLINK! CLINK! CLINK!
A golden chain emerged from the region of her heart, its radiant links trembling violently as it extended toward a distant location.
Aurielle's eyes immediately opened.
"What...?"
She looked down toward the chain, only for her expression to change as she sensed the desperate warning being transmitted through it.
"LUKE!"
The name escaped her mouth before she could restrain herself, and she immediately rose from her meditative position.
'What happened to him?!'
Her thoughts became chaotic as she recalled that Luke was currently on the Dragon Continent.
Even though Rhaenyra didn't appear particularly interested in protecting him, Aurielle had still believed that the Dragon Princess wouldn't simply allow something terrible to happen to her husband.
Yet the golden chain was warning her that Luke's life was in danger.
"What happened, darling?"
A familiar voice suddenly came from nearby.
Aurielle turned and saw Luke's clone approaching, but the moment his gaze settled upon the violently rattling chain, his own expression changed.
'The main body is in danger!'
He immediately attempted to establish a connection with Luke's consciousness.
Unfortunately, the result remained the same as his earlier attempts.
There was no response.
The connection between the clone and the main body still couldn't be established.
Aurielle noticed his reaction and hurried toward him.
"Luke! What's happening to my husband?! Tell me what's going on!"
Her voice trembled with anxiety as she looked between the clone and the golden chain.
However, the clone could only shake his head.
"I can't connect to the main body, Aurielle. I've tried, but I'm not receiving any response, so I don't know what's happening to him."
Aurielle stared at him, seemingly unable to accept what she had just heard.
Then her eyes filled with tears.
"Useless!"
The word escaped her mouth in frustration, although the anger she directed toward the clone was also directed toward herself.
If she had been stronger, perhaps she wouldn't have needed to depend upon others to protect Luke, and she could have accompanied him instead of remaining helpless so far away.
Unfortunately, none of those thoughts could change the situation.
Aurielle slowly turned toward the direction in which the golden chain extended, her hands trembling as she clasped them together.
"Please be safe, Luke..."
Her voice became quieter.
"Please... come back to me."
The golden chain continued rattling before her, while she remained standing inside the Time Chamber, helplessly watching the direction in which her husband had disappeared.

The little coffin turned toward him, apparently unwilling to leave while the three threatening figures remained nearby.
'I'll be fine.
Just go.
After a brief hesitation, Kiki finally obeyed.
VMMMM!
Its crimson body dissolved into a faint glow before disappearing.
"Hmm?"
Vradok raised his eyebrows upon seeing the coffin vanish, although he quickly dismissed the matter.
They had already witnessed enough of Luke's unusual abilities to understand that capturing him would likely provide opportunities to uncover his secrets.
However, one particular ability still worried the Great Shaman.
'His spatial movement...'
Although the ancestral dome had been destroyed, Luke had previously demonstrated several methods of teleportation, and allowing him even a brief opportunity to recover could prove troublesome.
Vradok looked down toward his severely injured body.
"So, Hero of Light, I think you've caused us enough trouble for one day."
Luke stared at him without speaking, since with almost all his strength exhausted, he could barely move, much less prepare a technique capable of resisting an A-Rank existence.
Vradok slowly raised his hand.
"You should sleep for now, and when you wake up, you'll find yourself in heaven."
He casually flicked his finger.
BOOOOOOM!
The seemingly insignificant movement released a terrifying shockwave that crossed the short distance between them before Luke could even react.
BAAAAAANG!
The attack struck his chest directly, tearing through the already damaged flesh and nearly splitting his torso apart.
KRRRRAAAACK!
Most of his remaining internal organs ruptured beneath the force, while golden-red blood erupted from the injury and scattered across the surrounding ground.
"UGHH—!"
Luke barely managed to release a pained cry before his consciousness disappeared.
His enormous body jerked backward, striking the bottom of the crater as the remaining strength sustaining his transformation began weakening.
Had he not been maintaining Vorthar's extraordinary physique, the blow would almost certainly have killed him instantly.
Meanwhile, Emberlyn witnessed the attack from her concealed position.
'LUKE!'
Her expression changed completely, and she nearly rushed forward before forcing herself to stop.
'No!
If I fight those three now, the shockwaves might kill him!'
She looked toward the Orc leaders, then toward the thick dust rising from Luke's crater, desperately searching for an opportunity to intervene.
Fortunately, before Gorzak could disperse the smoke, something unexpected happened.
CLINK!
CLINK!
CLINK!
Five golden chains suddenly emerged from within the dust cloud, their radiant links rattling violently as they become visible in the sky.
FWHOOOSH!
FWHOOOSH!
The chains extended toward five different directions, making anyone feel, that those chains were crossing the distant sky with extraordinary speed.
However, one of them appeared noticeably shorter than the others, pointing toward a location somewhere within Bravaryn.
"What is that?!" Gorzak exclaimed, instinctively stepping backward.
Kroghar also became cautious, while Vradok stared at the golden chains with growing suspicion.
Although the three possessed A-Rank strength and were far from approaching the level of demigods, they could clearly sense an unfamiliar divinity radiating from those links.
The discovery immediately made them wary.
However, the chains didn't attack.
Instead, they continued extending toward the five wives connected to Luke, carrying an urgent warning about the danger threatening him.
Far away, within the Blackstone Highlands, life had gradually returned to normal following Rhaenyra's departure.

Although rumors about a dragon appearing in the territory continued circulating among the inhabitants, attracting attention from neighboring regions, most people had already resumed their ordinary activities.
At that moment, Aurielle was seated inside the Time Chamber, quietly meditating as she attempted to gather enough energy to advance her cultivation.
Her objective remained unchanged.
She wanted to become strong enough to bring the real Luke back from the Dragon Continent, rather than continuing to depend upon his clone.
However, just as she was concentrating upon the energy circulating through her body, something suddenly disturbed her meditation.
CLINK!
CLINK!
CLINK!
A golden chain emerged from the region of her heart, its radiant links trembling violently as it extended toward a distant location.
Aurielle's eyes immediately opened.
"What...?"
She looked down toward the chain, only for her expression to change as she sensed the desperate warning being transmitted through it.
"LUKE!"
The name escaped her mouth before she could restrain herself, and she immediately rose from her meditative position.
'What happened to him?!'
Her thoughts became chaotic as she recalled that Luke was currently on the Dragon Continent.
Even though Rhaenyra didn't appear particularly interested in protecting him, Aurielle had still believed that the Dragon Princess wouldn't simply allow something terrible to happen to her husband.
Yet the golden chain was warning her that Luke's life was in danger.
"What happened, darling?"
A familiar voice suddenly came from nearby.
Aurielle turned and saw Luke's clone approaching, but the moment his gaze settled upon the violently rattling chain, his own expression changed.
'The main body is in danger!'
He immediately attempted to establish a connection with Luke's consciousness.
Unfortunately, the result remained the same as his earlier attempts.
There was no response.
The connection between the clone and the main body still couldn't be established.
Aurielle noticed his reaction and hurried toward him.
"Luke!
What's happening to my husband?!
Tell me what's going on!"
Her voice trembled with anxiety as she looked between the clone and the golden chain.
However, the clone could only shake his head.
"I can't connect to the main body, Aurielle.
I've tried, but I'm not receiving any response, so I don't know what's happening to him."
Aurielle stared at him, seemingly unable to accept what she had just heard.
Then her eyes filled with tears.
"Useless!"
The word escaped her mouth in frustration, although the anger she directed toward the clone was also directed toward herself.
If she had been stronger, perhaps she wouldn't have needed to depend upon others to protect Luke, and she could have accompanied him instead of remaining helpless so far away.
Unfortunately, none of those thoughts could change the situation.
Aurielle slowly turned toward the direction in which the golden chain extended, her hands trembling as she clasped them together.
"Please be safe, Luke..."
Her voice became quieter.
"Please... come back to me."
The golden chain continued rattling before her, while she remained standing inside the Time Chamber, helplessly watching the direction in which her husband had disappeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 394: Five Wives, Five Golden Chains, One Dying Husband!
paragraphs: Within Empyrean Academy, Selene was seated inside a luxurious room, reviewing several documents and writing something at her desk.
The room was quiet, with only the faint scratching of her pen disturbing the silence.
However, her concentration was suddenly interrupted.
CLINK! CLINK! CLINK!
A golden chain materialized before her chest, its links rattling with such intensity that the documents lying on her desk trembled beneath the movement.
Selene immediately stopped writing.
"...Luke?"
Her expression changed as she sensed the warning carried by the chain.
"Luke!"
She rose from her chair, immediately abandoning the unfinished documents as she reached toward the golden links.
"What happened to him? Why are you reacting like this?"
Unfortunately, the chain offered no explanation.
It merely continued rattling, its golden radiance flickering as it extended toward a distant location.
Selene attempted to sense something through their connection, but she couldn't determine what danger Luke was facing or who might be responsible.
Her fingers tightened around the chain.
'Darling...'
A worried expression appeared on her face as she looked toward the distant direction indicated by its links.
"Whatever is happening, please survive."
The golden chain continued trembling while Selene stood beside her desk, her earlier work completely forgotten.
Deep within the ocean, Naivara was hunting a powerful sea beast when the golden chain suddenly appeared before her.
CLINK! CLINK! CLINK!
The unexpected rattling immediately interrupted her movements, causing her to stop pursuing the creature as she turned toward the radiant links.
"Huh?"
She stared at the chain for a moment before sensing the urgent warning it carried.
"Luke..."
Her expression immediately became worried.
She couldn't understand why the connection had suddenly become so agitated, especially when she was separated from Luke by such a great distance.
'What happened to him?'
Naivara looked toward the direction indicated by the chain, feeling increasingly uneasy as its links continued trembling.
Unfortunately, she had no way of determining what was happening to him from her current location.
After a moment, she brought her hands together.
"Please, Ocean Mother, protect him."
Her voice carried quiet desperation as she continued gazing toward the distance.
"Whatever danger he's facing, please help him survive."
On the Elf Continent, within a secluded chamber, Elaria was seated in meditation when an unfamiliar rattling suddenly interrupted her concentration.
CLINK! CLINK! CLINK!
Her eyes opened.
"Hmm?"
A golden chain had appeared before her, its radiant links trembling violently while extending toward a distant location.
For a moment, Elaria merely stared at it with confusion.
Then she remembered the strange marriage connection that had been imposed upon her.
"Oh... Luke."
His name escaped her lips in a quiet murmur, although instead of immediately becoming worried, she appeared more interested in the fact that the chain had reminded her of her supposed husband.
'Husband...'
She considered the word briefly.
Even now, Elaria hadn't truly accepted the human as her husband, nor had her opinion of his race changed merely because of their unusual marriage.
However, the chain continued rattling insistently, making it difficult for her to ignore.
"Are you trying to tell me he's in danger?"
She tilted her head slightly, examining the golden links before looking toward the direction in which they extended.
"Should I go and save him?"
For a moment, she genuinely considered the possibility.
Although she didn't particularly like Luke, she wasn't completely opposed to helping him if he encountered danger nearby.
Unfortunately, the distance between them was far too great.
Elaria examined the chain again before shaking her head.
"Well, whatever. He's too far away for me to do anything.
She sighed lightly.
"If something happens to him, it isn't my fault."
However, just as she was preparing to dismiss the matter, she noticed something unusual about the direction indicated by the chain.
'The Dragon Continent?'
Her expression became curious.
'How did he end up there?'
As far as she remembered, Luke had traveled with Aurielle, the human princess, toward the Human Continent.
Yet the golden chain was clearly pointing toward the territory of the dragons.
Elaria considered the strange development for a moment before eventually losing interest.
"Forget it. I'm sure there's some explanation."
She closed her eyes and resumed her meditation, paying little attention to the golden chain that continued rattling before her.
Within Bravaryn, among its highest mountains, an enormous crimson dragon was sleeping peacefully.
Her thousand-meter-long body rested across the mountain peaks, while her enormous wings remained folded against her sides.
HUFFFFFF...
A single breath escaped her nostrils, releasing such intense heat that the nearby snow and portions of the rocky peaks began melting beneath the temperature.
However, the dragon remained asleep, completely unconcerned with the destruction caused by her ordinary breathing.
At least, until something appeared beside her.
CLINK! CLINK! CLINK!
A golden chain suddenly materialized near her enormous head, its radiant links trembling as though urgently attempting to awaken her.
Unlike the other four chains, this one had already determined that the person it was connected to possessed the greatest chance of protecting Luke.
After all, the five golden chains weren't ordinary tracking spells.
They possessed their own limited consciousness, allowing them to recognize danger and respond when the life or freedom of the person they were bound to protect was threatened.
That was why they hadn't appeared during Luke's earlier attack.
At the time, Luke had deliberately released the technique himself, fully aware of its consequences and apparently confident that he possessed some method of surviving.
However, the situation had changed when the three A-Rank Orcs appeared.
Luke had been reduced to a state where he could barely defend himself, and if those Orcs succeeded in taking him away, the consequences could become far worse than his injuries.
The chains had therefore activated, warning the women connected to him while also serving another peculiar purpose.
They were, in a sense, an anti-theft measure, intended to prevent someone from simply taking Luke away from his wives.
Unfortunately, the crimson dragon currently sleeping beneath the mountains knew nothing about their intentions.
CLINK! CLINK! CLINK!
The rattling became increasingly loud, reaching not only her enormous ears but also her consciousness.
"Hmm?"
Rhaenyra finally stirred.
Her gigantic crimson eyes slowly opened, and she raised her head from the mountain peak, looking around with obvious irritation.
"Who dares disturb my sleep?"
The golden chain immediately rattled again.
CLINK-CLINK-CLINK!
Rhaenyra turned toward it.
For a moment, she simply stared at the radiant links.
Then her expression became even more annoyed.
'Oh, this annoying thing again.'
She recognized the chain as the connection that the goddess had attached to her, binding her to an insignificant human who had somehow dared to claim her as his wi—
CLINK! CLINK! CLINK!
"SHUT UP!"
Rhaenyra's furious voice shook the surrounding mountains.
"Can't you see I'm trying to think?!"
The golden chain immediately stopped rattling.
For several moments, it remained unusually quiet, almost as though a small child had been scolded and was now sulking.
Rhaenyra snorted.
"Hmph! That's better."
However, before she could return to sleep, her gaze followed the golden chain toward the distant region of Bravaryn.
Something about its direction and the urgency of its earlier movements made her pause.
'Wait...'
She concentrated upon the connection.
A faint warning immediately reached her consciousness.
'Danger?'
Rhaenyra became confused.
'Is that human in danger?'
However, just as she began interpreting the warning, the golden chain transmitted something more specific.
It wasn't simply telling her that Luke had been injured.
It was warning her that someone was attempting to take him away.
'...Kidnapped?'
Rhaenyra froze.
For a moment, she remained completely silent as she processed the meaning of the warning.
Then her enormous crimson eyes widened.
"WHAT?!"
Her head shot upward.
"SOMEONE DARES TO KIDNAP MY THING?!"
The surrounding mountains trembled beneath her furious voice, while scorching air erupted from her nostrils as her anger rapidly increased.
"HOW DARE THEY?!"
Her enormous wings began spreading, casting broad shadows across the mountain peaks as the surrounding atmosphere trembled beneath the sudden release of her power.
Then Rhaenyra raised her head toward the sky.
"ROOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAARRRR!"
A legendary dragon roar erupted from her throat, spreading across Bravaryn with such terrifying intensity that countless inhabitants instinctively stopped whatever they were doing.
The sound rolled over mountains, forests, and settlements, causing weaker creatures to collapse beneath the pressure while powerful beings immediately recognized the source.
"The Dragon Princess!"
"WHAT HAPPENED?!"
"WHY IS SHE ANGRY?!"
Across Bravaryn, numerous inhabitants turned toward the distant mountains, some lowering their heads in fear while others began praying that the furious crimson dragon would quickly calm down.
Unfortunately, Rhaenyra had no intention of calming herself.
Her gaze remained fixed upon the direction indicated by the golden chain.
"WHOEVER DARES TAKE MY THING WILL REGRET IT!"
FWHOOOOOOOSH!
Her enormous wings swept downward.
BOOOOOOM!

The mountain peak beneath her body shattered as she launched herself into the sky, scattering broken rock across the surrounding slopes while the force of her departure produced a thunderous shockwave.
Within moments, her thousand-meter-long crimson body had accelerated to several times the speed of sound, leaving the devastated mountain behind as she rushed toward Luke's location.
Elsewhere in Bravaryn, within a peaceful treehouse surrounded by ancient branches and lush vegetation, a beautiful young woman was quietly enjoying a cup of tea.
She was Zephyrielle Arkanthyr, the grandmother of Rhaenyra and Emberlyn.
The surrounding forest was peaceful until the distant dragon roar suddenly rolled across the region.
"ROOOOOOOOOAAAAARRRR!"
Zephyrielle paused with her teacup near her lips.
"Hmm?"
She turned toward the distant mountains, immediately recognizing the familiar aura accompanying the roar.
Then a soft chuckle escaped her mouth.
"My, my. Has my little tsundere princess finally started showing her feelings?"
She placed the teacup down, her expression filled with amusement as she sensed Rhaenyra flying away from the mountains at extraordinary speed.
Knowing her granddaughter's personality, Zephyrielle understood that Rhaenyra rarely admitted caring about anyone, especially when doing so might reveal emotions she preferred keeping hidden.
Yet her furious reaction suggested that someone had touched something she considered important.
"How interesting."
However, as Zephyrielle extended her perception toward the direction Rhaenyra was traveling, she discovered another familiar presence near the devastated region.
Her eyebrows rose slightly.
"Oh? Emberlyn is there too?"
She examined the situation for a moment, then chuckled again.
"Hoh? It seems my other princess has also become rather attached to that young man."
The discovery amused her considerably, although she made no attempt to interfere.
After all, both of her granddaughters were capable of making their own decisions, and she was curious to see how the situation would develop.
"Well, I'll leave this to you two."
With that, Zephyrielle picked up her teacup again, her lips carrying a faint smile as she continued enjoying her tea.

chapters.title: Chapter 395: The Wife Who Wants Exclusive Kidnapping Rights!
paragraphs: Meanwhile, back at the devastated battlefield, Gorzak, Kroghar, and Vradok were still examining the five golden chains extending from the dust-covered crater.
Several moments had already passed since their appearance, yet none of the chains had attacked.
Vradok carefully studied their divine radiance before finally relaxing slightly.
"It appears to be some kind of tracking spell."
Hearing his explanation, Gorzak looked toward the distant directions in which the chains extended.
"Then can someone follow those things to find him?"
"Possibly," Vradok replied. "However, once we enter the Endless Forest, very few beings will dare pursue us into that territory."
Kroghar understood his meaning.
The ancient Orc tribes residing within the Endless Forest possessed powerful protectors, including existences that had already reached the realm of true gods.
So Gorzak finally relaxed.
"Good. Then let's take him before that crimson dra—"
"ROOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAARRRR!"
A terrifying dragon roar suddenly echoed across the distant sky.
All three Orc leaders froze.
They recognized that voice immediately.
It belonged to the same crimson dragon who had previously fought and injured them.
Rhaenyra.
"DAMN IT!" Vradok cursed, his expression changing sharply. "HOW DID SHE FIND OUT SO QUICKLY?!"
Gorzak and Kroghar immediately turned toward the direction of the roar, sensing the familiar dragon aura approaching from an enormous distance.
However, even from that far away, they could tell she was moving with frightening speed.
"We need to leave!" Kroghar shouted.
Vradok immediately waved his hand toward the crater.
FWHOOOSH!
A powerful gust swept through the area, dispersing the thick cloud of smoke and dust that had concealed Luke's body.
However, the moment the crater became visible, all three Orcs stopped moving.
The enormous Titan was gone.
Only the damaged ground remained, with golden-red blood staining the shattered earth where Luke had been lying moments earlier.
"WHAT?!"
Gorzak stared toward the empty crater.
"WHERE THE HELL IS HE?!"
Vradok immediately extended his perception across the surrounding region, searching for the severely injured Hero.
Unfortunately, the devastation had left countless unstable energy fluctuations throughout the area, making it difficult to distinguish anything clearly.
More importantly, the distant dragon aura was approaching rapidly.
"Vradok!" Kroghar shouted, turning toward the Great Shaman. "We don't have time to search the entire region!"
Gorzak looked between the empty crater and the distant sky, his expression becoming increasingly furious.
"We can't just abandon him after losing our entire tribe!"
"Then do you intend to fight that crimson dragon again?" Kroghar demanded. "We're already injured, and our army is gone!"
Gorzak clenched his fists.
For a moment, he seemed ready to argue.
However, another distant rumble reached them from the direction of Rhaenyra's approach, reminding all three of the devastating strength she possessed.
Vradok's expression became ugly.
"We've already lost our tribe, but our lives are more important."
He looked toward the empty crater one last time.
"We can recover our strength and rebuild our forces, but none of that will matter if we die here."
Hearing those words, Gorzak finally lowered his fists.
Kroghar immediately nodded.
"Then let's leave before she gets any closer."

Although all three understood that fleeing would damage their reputations, especially among the proud Orc tribes of the Endless Forest, they had already reached A-Rank and possessed lifespans far beyond those of ordinary warriors.
None of them wanted to throw away those years merely to defend their pride against a furious dragon.
"Fine. Let's go!" Gorzak finally agreed.
FWHOOOSH!
The three Orc leaders immediately launched themselves into the sky, their bodies accelerating beyond the speed of sound as they fled toward the distant Endless Forest.
BOOOOM!
However, Vradok couldn't help looking back one last time.
'Hero of Light...'
His crimson eyes burned with hatred as he recalled the destruction of the Zhurkhal Tribe.
'You will pay for everything you've done today!'
With that silent vow, the Great Shaman turned away and followed the other two leaders toward the Endless Forest.
Meanwhile, some distance away from the devastated battlefield, a figure was moving rapidly through the ruined forest.

Emberlyn cursed herself as she hurried across the broken ground, carefully carrying Luke's unconscious human body in her arms.
"I really am an idiot!"
Her expression was filled with frustration, although she continued running without slowing down.

Luke had already reverted from his seventy-foot Vorthar form to his ordinary humanoid appearance, but the transformation hadn't restored his missing limbs or repaired the terrible injuries covering his body.

Emberlyn was continuously channeling her energy into him, forcing the leaking blood back inside his body while preventing his remaining life force from weakening any further.
"Hahh..."
She glanced down at Luke's pale face, feeling her anxiety increase when she noticed how faint his breathing had become.
'Please, don't die.'
Her grip tightened slightly, although she immediately adjusted her hold to avoid aggravating his injuries.

'Right now, I just have to keep you alive.'

"WHO DARES TO KIDNAP MY TOY?!"
Emberlyn's movements faltered slightly.
She immediately recognized the voice.
Then another furious shout followed.
"ONLY I CAN KIDNAP MY TOY!!!"
Emberlyn's mouth twitched uncontrollably.
'Big Sister...'
She raised her head toward the direction of the furious voice, already recognizing the familiar dragon aura rapidly approaching their location.
Even while carrying a severely injured Luke and worrying about how she would explain everything to her father, Emberlyn couldn't help feeling speechless.
'Of all the things to be angry about...'
Her gaze dropped toward Luke's unconscious face.
Then she sighed.
'She really is my elder sister.'

chapters.title: Chapter 396: Luke Can't Swallow... So Emberlyn Considers Another Method?!
paragraphs: "Hahhh..."
Emberlyn finally released a deep breath after traveling a considerable distance from the devastated battlefield.
She glanced around the dense forest, making sure that no Orcs had followed her, before noticing a small cave hidden among the rocks at the base of a nearby mountain.
'This should be safe enough.'
With Luke's unconscious body still resting in her arms, she hurried toward the entrance and stepped inside, where the faint light entering from outside revealed a relatively dry chamber.
"Just hold on a little longer, Luke."
Using her power, Emberlyn gathered some of the surrounding stone and shaped it into a flat slab, creating a temporary bed upon which she carefully placed his body.
Unfortunately, the moment she examined his condition, her expression became increasingly worried.

Although the wounds Kiki had previously sealed were no longer bleeding as severely, Luke had still lost all four limbs, while several injuries across his chest and abdomen continued releasing golden-red blood.
His breathing was weak, and his normally fair complexion had turned unusually pale.
'I have to heal him before his condition gets any worse.'
Emberlyn immediately retrieved an advanced healing potion from her belongings, carefully selecting one whose medicinal energy Luke's current body could withstand without being overwhelmed.
After all, although she possessed much stronger healing resources, giving him something too powerful in his current condition could cause more harm than good.
POP!
She uncorked the vial and gently supported the back of Luke's head with one hand, bringing the potion toward his lips.
"Come on, Luke. You just need to drink a little."
Carefully parting his mouth, she tilted the vial and allowed a small quantity of the liquid to enter.
However, instead of swallowing, Luke remained completely unresponsive, and the potion began gathering inside his mouth.
Emberlyn immediately stopped pouring.
"Why aren't you swallowing it?"
She waited for a moment, hoping his body would respond naturally, but nothing happened.
The realization made her increasingly anxious, since she couldn't simply continue pouring the potion into his mouth while he remained unconscious and unable to swallow.
"Think, Emberlyn, think. There has to be another way."
She looked toward Luke's pale face, trying to recall everything she knew about treating an unconscious person.
Then a particular memory suddenly surfaced.
'Wait...'
Some time ago, while observing the customs of the local inhabitants, she had witnessed a woman demonstrating how to administer medicine to someone who couldn't drink normally.
The woman had been helping her husband, and instead of pouring the medicine directly into his mouth, she had transferred it using her own mouth while carefully helping him swallow.
'That's right!'
Emberlyn's eyes brightened upon remembering the method, but her excitement lasted only a moment before she realized what she would have to do.
Her gaze slowly moved toward Luke's lips.
'Wait a minute...'
The woman in that demonstration had been treating her husband, whereas Luke wasn't Emberlyn's husband.
Moreover, the method required their lips to touch.
A faint blush immediately appeared across her cheeks.
'W-What am I thinking?!'
Emberlyn shook her head, attempting to dismiss the strange thoughts that had suddenly entered her mind.
'I'm only doing this to save his life. Why should I be embarrassed about something like that?'
She glanced toward the potion before looking at Luke again.
His weak breathing reminded her that this wasn't the time to hesitate over such matters.
"All right, Luke. I'm going to help you drink this, so you'd better recover afterward."
Having made her decision, Emberlyn brought the vial toward her own lips, taking the remaining potion into her mouth.
A faint sweetness spread across her tongue, and for some reason, she became unusually conscious of the fact that the vial had touched Luke's lips only moments earlier.
'It's just the potion...'
Trying to ignore the thought, she carefully placed the empty vial aside before turning toward him.
Several loose strands of her white hair had fallen across her face, so she gently tucked them behind her ear, revealing the faint blush that had yet to disappear.
Then she leaned forward.
Her icy-blue eyes settled upon Luke's unconscious face, and as the distance between them gradually shortened, she could feel her heartbeat growing faster.
'Why am I getting so nervous?'
Although she had never done anything like this before, Emberlyn knew the procedure was meant to save his life, which made her reaction all the more embarrassing.
She lowered herself a little further, until Luke's faint, warm breathing brushed against her face.
'Just do it, Emberlyn.'
Her gaze briefly shifted toward his lips.
For a moment, she even forgot that Luke was already married, becoming entirely occupied with the unfamiliar sensation of being so close to him.
Then, just as their lips were about to touch—
BAAAAAAM!
A thunderous impact suddenly erupted outside the cave.
KRRRRRUMBLE!
The surrounding ground shook violently, sending broken stones tumbling down the mountainside as the force of the landing spread through the nearby forest.
Emberlyn immediately released her energy, reinforcing the cave before the shockwave could damage its structure.
OHHMMMM!
The trembling rocks gradually stabilized, although several loose fragments still fell near the entrance.
Emberlyn froze in her position, her lips only a short distance from Luke's.
'That aura...'
She recognized the newcomer immediately.
Unfortunately, before she could decide how to explain the situation, an angry voice echoed from the cave entrance.
"Ember, don't tell me you've fallen for him."
Emberlyn slowly turned her head.
There, standing near the entrance, was Rhaenyra, whose crimson eyes were fixed directly upon her younger sister.
"And have you already forgotten that he's a married man?"
The mocking question carried obvious irritation, especially after Rhaenyra had arrived only to discover Emberlyn leaning over Luke with their lips almost touching.
Emberlyn immediately lowered her gaze, feeling even more embarrassed now that her elder sister had witnessed what she was preparing to do.
However, she didn't regret attempting to feed Luke the potion.
After all, saving his life was far more important than worrying about how the situation might appear.
As for Rhaenyra's accusation that she had fallen for him, Emberlyn chose not to answer.
She wasn't entirely certain how she should respond to that question herself.
THUD.
Rhaenyra stepped inside the cave, ignoring her younger sister as her attention shifted toward Luke's unconscious body.
The moment she saw his condition, her expression changed.
Both of his arms and legs were missing, while numerous wounds covered his body, with golden-red blood staining the stone slab beneath him.
His face was pale, and his breathing was so weak that she could barely hear it.
For an instant, something flickered within Rhaenyra's crimson eyes.
Her heart felt strangely heavy as she looked at the injuries covering Luke's body, although she immediately suppressed the unfamiliar emotion.
THUD.
She approached the stone slab and lowered herself beside him.
Then, without speaking, Rhaenyra raised one hand and gently touched his cheek, brushing aside the black strands of hair that had fallen across his closed eyes.
Her fingers paused briefly against his face.
'You really are troublesome...'
She had allowed Luke to travel with Emberlyn because she believed he would remain relatively safe while she was occupied hunting those beings.
Yet now, the human she had left behind was lying before her with nearly his entire body destroyed.
"Sister, I was just about to heal—"
"SHUT UP!"
Rhaenyra's furious shout immediately interrupted Emberlyn, causing the younger Dragon Princess to stare at her in surprise.
Emberlyn had expected anger after being discovered in such an embarrassing position, but she hadn't anticipated this level of fury.

"I thought leaving him with you would keep him safe," Rhaenyra continued, her gaze returning to Luke. "I was busy hunting those beings, so I believed you could at least prevent something like this from happening."
She glanced toward Emberlyn.
"But it seems I was wrong."
Emberlyn lowered her head, unable to immediately find an answer.
Until now, she had believed that Luke and Rhaenyra simply didn't want to remain together.
After all, Rhaenyra had never openly accepted him as her husband, while Luke had spent the past month traveling with her rather than staying beside his supposed wife.
Because of that, Emberlyn had assumed her elder sister didn't particularly care what happened to him.
Yet the expression Rhaenyra had shown upon seeing Luke's injuries suggested otherwise.

Unfortunately, Emberlyn still didn't understand how complicated the relationship between those two had become, especially when her elder sister had always been terrible at expressing her actual feelings.
Meanwhile, Rhaenyra had already turned her attention back toward Luke.
She gently pressed her lips together before concentrating upon the blood essence within her body.
OHHMMMM!

A faint crimson radiance gathered near her mouth as she carefully extracted a single drop of her own blood essence, controlling the amount so that Luke's severely weakened body wouldn't be overwhelmed by its power.
As an A-Rank dragon, her blood essence contained extraordinary vitality, and even such a small quantity would be sufficient to accelerate his recovery.
However, she still needed to administer it properly.
Rhaenyra leaned toward Luke, preparing to transfer the blood essence directly into his mouth with her lips.
Unfortunately, Emberlyn had been watching her movements the entire time.
And the moment she realized what her elder sister intended to do, an uncomfortable feeling suddenly emerged within her chest.
'Wait...'
Her gaze moved toward Rhaenyra's lips, which were gradually approaching Luke's.
For some reason, she found herself becoming increasingly unwilling to let her sister continue.
Before she could properly consider why, the words escaped her mouth.
"Sister, you should step back, because Luke was my responsibility, and I should be the one to heal him."
The cave immediately became silent.

chapters.title: Chapter 397: The Tsundere Dragon Princess Accidentally Reveals Her True Feelings!
paragraphs: Emberlyn herself froze.
'What did I just say?'
She hadn't intended to challenge her elder sister, especially when Luke's life was still in danger, yet the words had escaped before she could restrain them.
Meanwhile, Rhaenyra stopped just before her lips touched Luke's.
She slowly raised her head and turned toward Emberlyn.
"...Responsibility?"
Her voice was unusually calm, although the irritation in her crimson eyes had become unmistakable.
"When did Luke become your responsibility?"
Emberlyn hesitated, realizing she had already gone too far to pretend she hadn't said anything.
However, after recalling the month she had spent accompanying Luke, she gradually gathered her confidence.
"He's my responsibility because I've been traveling with him this entire month, while you weren't even willing to remain near him."
Rhaenyra stared at her.
She slowly rose from beside the stone slab before approaching Emberlyn, stopping directly in front of her younger sister.
The two Dragon Princesses stood face-to-face, both still holding the medicines they had intended to administer to Luke.
A faint trace of the healing potion remained upon Emberlyn's lips, while Rhaenyra's own lips carried a small crimson glow from the blood essence she had gathered.
"Ember, I think you've forgotten something."
Rhaenyra's voice became colder.
"Even if I discard him or refuse to acknowledge him, Luke is still mine, and he will always remain MINE!"
Her voice rose toward the end, and the atmosphere inside the cave became increasingly tense as her A-Rank aura began stirring.
The thought of someone claiming Luke as their responsibility was already irritating enough.
However, hearing those words from her own younger sister made the feeling even worse, especially when Emberlyn had apparently grown so close to him during the past month.
Unfortunately, Emberlyn wasn't willing to remain silent this time.
"You're wrong, Sister. Luke isn't some object you can discard whenever you want and then claim again as though nothing happened."
Rhaenyra stared at her.
Emberlyn continued, her expression becoming more determined.
"You may not accept him as your husband, but that doesn't mean you can treat him however you please."
She didn't fully understand why she was defending Luke so strongly, although the month they had spent together had changed her opinion of him considerably.
At first, she had regarded him as another human Hero connected to the gods, someone she expected to possess the same selfish ambitions and false promises she had witnessed among so many others.
Even the Dragon Hero who had previously been summoned had disappointed her, which was why she had rejected the proposed marriage, a decision her father and grandfather had respected.
However, Luke had gradually proven different.

During their journey, she had witnessed how he treated the innocent demi-humans rescued from the Orc outposts, and despite his unusual personality, she had come to recognize that his concern for them was genuine.
He could be shameless, troublesome, and occasionally ridiculous, but Emberlyn had never felt that he was pretending to be someone he wasn't.
And after seeing him nearly die, she was no longer willing to hear her sister speak about him as though he were merely a possession.
Unfortunately, her words only made Rhaenyra angrier.
"Not an object?"
Rhaenyra repeated the words with a disbelieving expression, looking at Emberlyn as though her younger sister had said something completely absurd.
Then she pointed toward the stone slab.
"IF HE ISN'T AN OBJECT, THEN TELL ME WHY THE FUCK MY LUKE IS LYING THERE WITHOUT ANY LIMBS, COMPLETELY UNCONSCIOUS!"
Her furious voice echoed through the cave.
Before Emberlyn could answer, Rhaenyra stepped forward and grabbed her by the collar.
"YOU WERE WITH HIM THIS ENTIRE MONTH, WEREN'T YOU?! THEN HOW DID YOU LET HIM END UP LIKE THAT?!"
Emberlyn's expression changed.
Although she was more talented than Rhaenyra, having reached A-Rank before her elder sister, she knew that such differences meant very little when Rhaenyra lost her temper.
Her sister had always possessed an uncontrollable temper, and even if she were facing a true god, she probably wouldn't hesitate to fight once her anger overwhelmed her judgment.
Now, with crimson flames beginning to flicker within Rhaenyra's eyes, Emberlyn could sense just how furious she had become.

Rhaenyra sneered.

"Little Sister, sometimes I really wonder whether Father has pampered you too much."
"...What?"

"You're so concerned about following orders that you've apparently forgotten they can be broken," Rhaenyra replied, maintaining her grip upon Emberlyn's collar. Emberlyn opened her mouth, but before she could answer, Rhaenyra asked another question.
"Tell me, Ember. Was Father's order more important than Luke's life?"
The question immediately silenced her.
Rhaenyra continued looking directly into her eyes, waiting for an answer.
"Because if you truly believed his life was more important, then why did you wait until he was almost dead before deciding to save him?"
Emberlyn felt her throat tighten.

She remembered how she had repeatedly hesitated while watching Luke struggle against the Orc army, and how she had finally chosen to break her father's order only after the three A-Rank leaders attempted to capture him.
"But I saved him at the last—"
"WHY SO LATE?!"
Rhaenyra interrupted her angrily.
"You could have intervened earlier, but you kept following Father's order until Luke was barely alive! Why did you wait so long?!"
Emberlyn lowered her gaze, unable to immediately respond.
Although she had possessed reasonable concerns about revealing herself, the sight of Luke's devastated body made defending those decisions increasingly difficult.
Rhaenyra finally loosened her grip slightly.
"Let me ask you something else, Ember. If Grandpa ordered Father not to protect either of us, do you think he would obey?"
Emberlyn looked toward her elder sister.
Rhaenyra answered her own question.
"Of course he wouldn't! Father would protect us even if he had to fight Grandpa himself, and you know that as well as I do!"
Her voice remained firm, carrying the certainty of someone who had never doubted their father's love.
"Because to him, his family is more important than any order."
Those words finally made Emberlyn fall silent.
She knew Rhaenyra was right about that.

Their father had always been willing to protect them, and although he could be strict about many matters, Emberlyn understood that he wouldn't hesitate to oppose even their grandfather if his daughters' lives were genuinely threatened.
After all, he had listened to her wishes before, including her decision to reject the Dragon Hero's marriage proposal.
'Then why couldn't I...'
Emberlyn looked toward Luke again, her earlier determination gradually giving way to guilt.
However, Rhaenyra had already reached the limit of her patience.
"So get lost! I'll take care of Luke myself!"
With those words, she pushed Emberlyn backward.
THUD!
Emberlyn stumbled and fell onto the cave floor, looking up at her elder sister with a complicated expression.
Rhaenyra ignored her and immediately returned to Luke's side, where the drop of blood essence she had gathered was still waiting to be administered.
She carefully lowered herself beside him, preparing to transfer it into his mouth.
However, Emberlyn couldn't remain silent.
"Rhaenyra, but you don't even accept him as your husban—"
"That's a matter between husband and wife."
Rhaenyra interrupted without turning toward her.
Her voice had become noticeably quieter, although it still carried enough firmness to prevent Emberlyn from continuing.
For a moment, even Rhaenyra seemed confused by the words she had just spoken.
After all, she had never properly accepted Luke as her husband, and much of their relationship had been defined by her anger, pride, and unwillingness to acknowledge the connection between them.
She had even hurt him during one of their earlier encounters, allowing her temper to overwhelm her judgment.
Yet seeing him lying before her in such a terrible condition had awakened an unfamiliar heaviness within her chest.
'You troublesome human...'
Her fingers gently brushed the black hair away from his forehead.
'Why do you always have to make things so difficult?'

chapters.title: Chapter 398: Two Sisters, One Human Husband, and a Forbidden Jealousy!
paragraphs: Rhaenyra couldn't explain why the sight of his injuries affected her so strongly, nor was she willing to examine those feelings while her younger sister was watching.
However, one thing remained perfectly clear in her mind.
Regardless of whether she openly acknowledged him as her husband, Luke belonged to her, and she had no intention of allowing anyone to take him away.
With that thought, Rhaenyra finally leaned closer.
Then her lips met his.
She carefully transferred the drop of crimson blood essence into Luke's mouth, using her energy to guide it down his throat.
GULP!
A faint crimson glow immediately spread through his body as the blood essence entered his system.
However, Rhaenyra didn't immediately pull away.
She remained close for several moments, her lips still resting against his as she looked at his unconscious face.
For someone as prideful as Rhaenyra, admitting she had done something wrong was almost impossible, especially when the person involved was the human she had repeatedly refused to acknowledge.
Yet the gentle way she remained beside him carried an apology she wasn't prepared to express aloud.
'You'd better wake up...'
She finally closed her eyes for a moment.
'And stop making me worry about you.'
Meanwhile, Emberlyn was watching everything from the cave floor.
Her fists slowly tightened.
Although she knew Rhaenyra was administering blood essence to save Luke's life, watching her elder sister kiss him caused an uncomfortable feeling to spread through her chest.
'It should have been me...'
She immediately became startled by her own thought.
However, the jealousy continued growing as Rhaenyra remained close to Luke.
'You don't deserve him...'
Emberlyn pressed her lips together, refusing to say those words aloud, although her fingers had tightened enough for her nails to dig into her palms.
After spending an entire month accompanying Luke, she had begun caring about him far more than she initially realized.
And now, seeing her elder sister openly claim him while simultaneously refusing to acknowledge their marriage made Emberlyn feel increasingly frustrated.
Unfortunately, she also knew that arguing further would accomplish nothing while Luke remained unconscious.
So she turned her face away.
Several minutes later, Rhaenyra finally separated from Luke's lips.
"Hahhh..."
She released a quiet breath before looking down at his body.
The effects of her blood essence had already begun appearing.
OHHMMMM!
Crimson energy circulated beneath Luke's skin, spreading through his injured body as the extraordinary vitality of dragon blood accelerated his natural regeneration.
The wounds covering his chest and abdomen gradually began closing, while the places where his arms and legs had been destroyed started producing new flesh.
Within moments, the outlines of his missing limbs began forming, with bones, muscles, and skin gradually regenerating as the healing energy continued circulating through his body.
The process was accompanied by a faint golden-red radiance, while Luke's breathing became increasingly stable.
Rhaenyra carefully observed his condition, making sure the blood essence wasn't overwhelming his weaker cultivation.
Fortunately, she had controlled the quantity precisely, allowing his body to absorb its restorative power without suffering additional damage.
As the minutes passed, Luke's arms and legs continued regenerating, while the terrible wounds covering his body gradually disappeared.
Even his pale complexion began returning to its usual fair appearance.
Seeing the improvement, Rhaenyra finally relaxed.
'Good...'
She gently touched his cheek once more before standing beside the stone slab.
However, instead of waiting for him to awaken, she simply bent down and lifted his unconscious body.
Then she placed him across her shoulder.
Emberlyn stared at the sight.
After everything that had happened, Rhaenyra was now carrying Luke like a sack of potatoes, apparently completely unconcerned about how strange the position looked.
However, the familiar movement suddenly reminded Rhaenyra of something.
'This...'
She remembered how she had carried Luke in almost the same manner during their earlier encounter at the Holy Church.
At the time, she had been furious with him, treating the troublesome human as someone she could simply pick up and carry away whenever she wished.
Yet now, after nearly losing him, that memory felt strangely different.
A small smile appeared on her lips.
Unfortunately, the expression didn't escape Emberlyn's notice.
Her eyes widened slightly.
'Did Sister just smile?'
Emberlyn was genuinely astonished, since making Rhaenyra laugh or smile naturally had always been extremely difficult.
As far as she remembered, their grandmother was among the very few people capable of consistently bringing out that side of her elder sister.
'What is happening to her?'
Before Emberlyn could think further, Rhaenyra's familiar cold voice interrupted her thoughts.
"Ember, what happened here today must remain between us."
Emberlyn looked toward her.
Rhaenyra adjusted Luke's position upon her shoulder before continuing.
"Especially the part where I healed him. Luke must never find out about that."
Emberlyn stared at her elder sister, wondering how someone could behave so tenderly one moment and immediately return to acting cold the next.
However, Rhaenyra wasn't finished.
She turned toward Emberlyn, her crimson eyes carrying a clear warning.
"If Luke discovers what happened here, I'll kill you!"
Emberlyn sighed.
"Yeah, yeah. I won't tell him anything."
Her reply was rather casual, since she knew her elder sister's terrible temper well enough to understand that the threat wasn't something she would actually carry out.
After all, Rhaenyra might become furious over the smallest provocation, but she would never genuinely kill her own younger sister over something like this.
Moreover, Emberlyn wasn't particularly interested in revealing what had happened either.
'It's not like I want Luke to know what I was about to do...'
Recalling how close she had come to kissing him before Rhaenyra interrupted, a faint blush returned to her cheeks.
Fortunately, her elder sister seemed too occupied with Luke to notice.
"Hmph! You'd better remember that."
Rhaenyra ignored Emberlyn's half-hearted response, since she knew her younger sister wasn't foolish enough to deliberately reveal something so embarrassing.
With Luke still resting across her shoulder, she slowly rose into the air.
FWHOOOSH!
A faint crimson aura surrounded her body as she floated toward the cave entrance, preparing to return to the Dragon Palace where Luke could recover safely.
Emberlyn immediately stood up.
She brushed the dust from her clothes before hurrying after her elder sister.
Emberlyn had done this without hesitation, her expression carrying a determination that hadn't been present earlier.
After witnessing how close Luke had come to dying, she had finally decided that she wouldn't remain passive if his life were threatened again.
Even if her father became angry, she intended to protect him properly from now on.
Rhaenyra noticed, Emberlyn action, but still she made no attempt to stop her.
With that, Rhaenyra accelerated toward the Dragon Palace, carrying the unconscious Luke across her shoulder while Emberlyn followed closely behind.

And so, the two Dragon Princesses returned home together, both concerned about the same human man, although neither was willing to openly acknowledge just how much he had begun affecting her feelings.
If news of what had happened inside that small cave ever reached the Dragon Royal Family, even their own relatives would probably struggle to believe it.

After all, who would have imagined that Rhaenyra, the proud Crimson Dragon Princess who refused to acknowledge her human husband, would personally feed him her precious blood essence and then threaten her own sister to keep the matter secret?
Or that Emberlyn, who had initially regarded Luke as merely another troublesome Hero, would openly challenge her elder sister over him?
Unfortunately for Luke, he remained completely unconscious throughout the entire incident, unaware that the two Dragon Princesses had nearly started fighting over who possessed the right to save him.
And with that, we've reached the end of a small arc within Volume III!

Of course, this isn't the end of the entire volume, since we've only completed roughly half of it, but the next few chapters will finally bring Luke closer to his long-awaited breakthrough into C-Rank.

After that, the remaining part of this volume will focus more on Rhaenyra and how she gradually begins falling in love with Luke for real, while Luke, as always, continues playing the role of an perfect husband.
So, I hope all of you have been enjoying the story so far, and I sincerely want to thank everyone who has continued reading and supporting this novel.
Your support means a lot to me, especially because it motivates me to keep writing and improving the story.
There are so many of you who have supported this story, and for that, I can only say:
THANK YOU SO MUCH!
And as always, your best author,
— EternalVoidRuler

chapters.title: Chapter 399: The Hero of Light Sleeps in a Dragon Princess's Lap!
paragraphs: 1st Day of Messis, the Ninth Month, Year 50,001.
Throughout Valtharion, autumn had arrived, bringing a change of season across the world, something Luke would have found rather unusual compared to his previous life on Earth.

Of course, this seasonal change only affected regions where unusual weather conditions weren't already present, since certain territories continued experiencing their own unique climates regardless of the time of year.
Meanwhile, in Bravaryn, peace had finally returned following the conclusion of the ten-day battle against the Zhurkhal Tribe.
And the Hero of Light, who was responsible for ending that conflict, was currently sleeping peacefully with his head resting upon the lap of a beautiful young woman.
Her long, snow-white hair flowed over her shoulders, while a pair of elegant silver horns rose from her head, complementing her striking icy-blue eyes and delicate facial features.
She was Emberlyn Starfall, the younger princess of the Dragon Royal Family.
"Hahhh..."
Emberlyn released a quiet sigh as she looked down at Luke's sleeping face, gently running her fingers through his shoulder-length black hair.
It had already been ten days since they returned to the Dragon Palace, yet Luke hadn't awakened even once during that time.

She had remained beside him throughout those ten days, rarely leaving his company, especially since beings at her cultivation level no longer needed to concern themselves with ordinary necessities in the same manner as mortals.
"Luke, when are you finally going to wake up?"
She gently caressed his cheek, looking somewhat confused as she recalled the treatment he had received.

Rhaenyra's blood essence should have been more than sufficient to restore Luke's damaged body, and considering its extraordinary healing properties, Emberlyn had expected him to regain consciousness by the following day.
However, despite his injuries having completely recovered, he continued sleeping.
"I already told Big Sister not to feed you any more of her blood essence," Emberlyn muttered, her fingers pausing briefly against his cheek.

After Luke failed to awaken, Rhaenyra had become increasingly concerned and subsequently fed him her blood essence nine additional times, even increasing its concentration in the hope that the stronger medicinal effect would help him recover.
Unfortunately, Luke remained unconscious, while the repeated expenditure eventually exhausted Rhaenyra to the point that she needed to sleep to restore her energy.
Emberlyn couldn't understand why the treatment hadn't worked as expected.
What she didn't know was that Luke's body was currently undergoing a far more complicated process.

Deep within his unconscious body, "Eternal Titan Zero" had been continuously reconstructing his cells and internal structures, using the enormous quantity of Blood Essence he had absorbed to accelerate the formation of his new physique.
And Rhaenyra's blood essence had contributed tremendously to that process.
In fact, if Luke were conscious and able to examine his cultivation status, he would have been astonished by the number displayed before him.
[ETERNAL TITAN ZERO — BODY RECONSTRUCTION]
His reconstruction had almost reached completion.

Considering that his EX-Rank technique normally required him to absorb Blood Essence from slain beings, the sudden increase was extraordinary, especially since most of this additional progress had come from a living A-Rank Dragon Princess.
However, Rhaenyra's blood essence possessed such exceptional quality that even a relatively small quantity contained tremendous value.
Moreover, there was another reason for its effectiveness, one connected to a certain conspiracy involving the gods.
Unfortunately, neither Luke nor the two Dragon Princesses knew anything about that particular matter.
Meanwhile, the System was observing the situation with an expression of utter disbelief.
[Seriously...]
It looked toward Emberlyn, who was still gently caressing Luke's hair while waiting for him to awaken.
[Instead of making Rhaenyra fall in love with him, this idiot somehow managed to make her younger sister fall for him first.]
The System hadn't expected such an outcome, especially when Luke's original objective involved conquering the heart of his proud dragon wife.
However, the developing relationship between Luke and Emberlyn was no longer its greatest concern.
Its attention gradually returned to the reconstruction taking place within Luke's body.
[Was this really a good thing?]
The System sighed.
[The path of shortcuts never ends well.]
At that moment, its attention shifted toward a distant hill, where Rhaenyra had finally awakened after recovering from the exhaustion caused by repeatedly giving Luke her blood essence.
However, the moment she looked toward Luke's location and discovered Emberlyn once again behaving affectionately toward him, her expression immediately became unpleasant.
"I already told her not to touch him! Why can't that girl listen to me?!"
Rhaenyra cursed her younger sister under her breath, becoming increasingly irritated as she watched Emberlyn continue caressing Luke's hair.
For a moment, she even considered going over and dealing with her troublesome sister directly.
Unfortunately, Emberlyn was also an A-Rank Dragon Princess, and even Rhaenyra couldn't confidently predict the outcome if the two of them seriously fought.
Moreover, their father, mother, grandmother, and grandfather would all become furious if they discovered that the sisters had started fighting with each other.
After all, internal conflicts were strictly forbidden within their family.
"Hmph!"
Rhaenyra folded her arms, clearly dissatisfied.
"Should I just kidnap Luke again and take him somewhere nobody can find us?"
The thought suddenly appeared in her mind, and she couldn't help considering whether that might be the simplest solution.
However, the System ignored her increasingly possessive behavior, even though it was beginning to resemble the development of a rather healthy yandere.
Instead, its attention moved toward something far more troubling.
Besides the golden marriage chains, several other connections had begun forming between Rhaenyra and Luke.
These connections were invisible to ordinary beings, but the System could clearly perceive their existence.
[Karma, fate, destiny, past, future... even her death is being transferred to Luke.]
The System's expression became unusually serious.

Although Luke had gained an extraordinary amount of Blood Essence through Rhaenyra, there was no such thing as a completely free shortcut in this universe, especially when dealing with an EX-Rank cultivation technique.
Its purpose was to reconstruct Luke into an Eternal Titan Zero, and the requirements involved in that transformation extended far beyond simply collecting enough Blood Essence.
That was precisely why the System had never recommended obtaining all the necessary resources from a living, higher-ranked existence.
Although such a method could help Luke complete the first stage of his reconstruction, the following stages wouldn't necessarily accept the same shortcut.
[He obtained the Blood Essence, but he didn't personally accumulate all the karma and other requirements needed to complete his C-Rank Eternal Titan Zero body.]
The System examined the connections forming between Luke and Rhaenyra.
[And now, his technique is attempting to obtain those missing requirements from her.]
The consequences were far more serious than Luke could currently imagine.

Rhaenyra had killed an extraordinary number of beings throughout her life, and the karma associated with those deaths was now being transferred toward Luke through the connection created by the Blood Essence.
Even certain aspects of her fate and destiny were becoming entangled with his reconstruction.
[That means her accumulated killings, her karma, and everything connected to them are becoming part of his burden.]
The System sighed again.
Under ordinary circumstances, Luke's advancement should have resulted in a tribulation appropriate to the strength and requirements of his own cultivation.

However, because he had obtained the final portion of his Blood Essence from a living A-Rank existence rather than accumulating it through killing, the universal laws would no longer evaluate the process in the same manner.
Rhaenyra herself was an A-Rank being, and the value attached to her existence was naturally far greater than that of the enemies Luke had previously absorbed.
Consequently, instead of facing a B-Rank-level tribulation, Luke would now have to endure one reaching A-Rank.
And that wasn't even considering the hidden laws involved in the process.
[Well, at least Luke has canceled that possible future death of hers.]
For once, the System's voice contained none of its usual playfulness.
It had previously witnessed a possible future in which Rhaenyra would die, and the time associated with that event was gradually approaching.
However, now that Luke had begun taking on the consequences connected to her existence, including that particular death, the System expected the future to change.
If Luke survived the coming tribulation, then logically, the danger associated with Rhaenyra's predicted death should also disappear.
Unfortunately, something was wrong.
The System attempted to examine that future again, only to discover that the scene remained concealed beneath a strange ash-colored fog.
[Again? Those beings are doing whatever they want.]
The System looked at the obscured future with growing dissatisfaction.
At the height of its former power, it could have easily torn through restrictions of this nature, including certain traps capable of rendering even Eternal-Rank existences helpless.
However, in its current weakened state, it couldn't do anything about the interference.
Eventually, it withdrew its attention from the hidden future and returned its gaze toward Luke.
[Become stronger, Luke. As you need every bit of strength you can gather.]
Its expression became increasingly grave.
[Because when that time comes, it will be only you and Rhaenyra, and if you fail, you'll lose her forever.]
At that exact moment, Luke's eyelids suddenly flickered.
After remaining unconscious for ten days, his body finally showed the first signs of awakening.
Whether he had somehow heard the System's warning or had simply reached the moment when his long-awaited destiny would begin moving forward remained unknown.
